chapters.title: Chapter 2101: It seems like I now can...?
paragraphs: [A being who has a domain that is an entirely different world on its own,
What do you think I am?]
[A-A d-different w-world...?]
The women stared at the screen in front of them with dumbfounded looks on their faces. No one dared to say anything, as if scared that Neremoth might hear them.
However, after a long, long silence, Aisha couldn’t hold back any longer and—
"...you think he will buy it?"
The Succubus questioned as she tilted her head toward her mother.
"It... seems like he is...?"
Eisheth answered. Even she seemed confused by what was happening. It wasn’t just her, everyone else was the same.
"I can’t believe he is actually pulling it off."
Edda couldn’t hold herself back and laughed out loud.
"A-A d-different w-world...???"
Allura placed her hands on her cheeks and shouted in an exaggerated manner.
"Ahhhh!! He must be an infinity!!"
Edda joined her as well.
"Be silent, will you? He might hear us."
Lyriana spoke with a cautious look on her face.
"He cannot."
Edda waved her hand. She obviously had complete trust in her husband.
"There is no way this is going to work..."
Lyriana muttered. The elf had started biting her nails in anxiety.
This was an Eternal they were talking about, dammit!
An Eternal!!
An Eternal from the Supreme World!!!
One of the strongest beings in the entire Universe! UNIVERSE!!!

They were no longer in their little world where the Ancestral Order regulated everything and they, as mere Divines, acted like the rulers. The opponent here wasn’t a mere Incomplete Divine Stage Cultivator who was having an anger fit because a child taunted him.
This was different.
This was VERY different!!
"Well, this is Nux."
Suddenly, Felberta chuckled.
She had seen this man’s complete journey. She had seen him grow with her very eyes, in front of her. This wasn’t the first time he was doing something absurd; it won’t be the last time either.
The Eldraeth Progenitor had complete, absolute faith in her husband.
This was her pride as the first wife.
Lyriana stared at her and... suddenly her anxiety started to fade away.
It was something that surprised even her.
’What...?’
She couldn’t understand. Even her increased heartbeat seemed to have calmed down as she stared at Felberta.
’Did she have a power like this...?’
The elf wondered in her head. She didn’t recall her having such an ability. The one who actually had this ability was—
Suddenly, Lyriana turned to glance at Skyla only to find her staring at her. The second wife smiled brightly, as if saying ’everything will be fine, don’t worry,’ and Lyriana finally realized it.
She nodded at Skyla, as if thanking her. Skyla laughed again as she once again turned towards the screen, watching her husband pull off something like this again.
"This is going to work, huh..."
Lyriana muttered. Her eyes fell on Shadow. Out of everyone present here, the one who knew about the situation the most was her.
The rest of the women turned towards Shadow as well and the woman grinned,
"Ten more seconds."
The rest of the women grinned as well. There was still some tension, but with Skyla’s presence, it couldn’t grow much.
"Five more seconds..."
Shadow informed,
"Four...
Three...
Two...
One and—"
BOOOOOOOOM
A powerful shockwave rippled throughout the Universe, grabbing the women’s attention. Every one of them could sense how the Universe was changing, but—
Suddenly, Shadow’s expression changed as she noticed a strange change in her body. Instinctively, she raised her head, staring at... nothingness?
At least that was what everyone else would believe if they followed her gaze. However, as the Soul of the Universe, Shadow was different.
She could sense it.
The birth of the ’Star’.
It was merely a spark at first, but she felt it. It was something much different than anything she had ever felt.
Something... much stronger.
Something... that seemed to be connected to her?

No, that wasn’t correct. It wasn’t the only thing connected to Shadow. As the Universe’s Soul and its First Goddess, she was connected to every entity here. Every change here had some effect on her and changed her.
The new ’Star’ was no exception—just that... this entity was so strong that the connection she had with it felt much stronger as well.
And...
The change it was making here... was changing her as well.
And this change...
It was unlike anything she had ever felt.

Deep inside her, something changed—something she could not understand—and before she could even begin to, or inform Nux about this, a familiar warmth spread through her. A warmth that eased all her thoughts. Nux’s warmth.
This ’Star’...
Shadow finally realized why it was so strong.
It...
It represented Nux.
In an instant, an extremely beautiful smile appeared on Shadow’s face and she just closed her eyes, accepting the ’change’ in her.
The star grew brighter, a light rippled through space, and Shadow... her body began to shift.
At first, it was her hair.

Black waves poured from her head like liquid night, and no, it wasn’t her usual colorless dark hair. Now, they felt alive, shining like they held galaxies in them. Her strands curled and danced, catching light like the edges of a nebula.
Then her face began to form.
From the smooth blankness, the shape of her brow emerged—gently arched, regal, and calm.

Her nose formed, delicate and straight, casting the faintest shadow along the curve of her face. Then her lips came into being—full, gently parted, with the faintest hint of color. Her jaw was firm and graceful.

Her body filled with light and color. The darkness of her form deepened into a strangely powerful fabric that seemed to represent the very Universe itself. Her skin glittered with stars, her limbs curved with a regal grace.
Gold earrings shaped like falling stars dangled from her ears, catching the new star’s light with ease despite the ridiculously huge distance between them.

Once the transformation ended, Shadow finally opened her eyes, revealing her striking, glowing violet eyes. The shine in those eyes was deep—endless even—as if each iris held a whole galaxy spiraling quietly inside.
The first thing she saw were her sisters staring at her with dumbfounded looks on their faces.
Shadow also didn’t fail to notice that their Universe had now gained color. Her sisters no longer looked like shadows but like they did back in the main Universe.
The sisters in question, however, didn’t seem to care about it. Their focus was all on her.
"What the hell...?"
Amaya cursed out loud, clearly not liking the situation.
"Shadow...?"
Lane muttered, unable to believe what she was seeing.
"I got a new body~"
Shadow chuckled, making a ’V’ with her fingers as she laughed out loud.
"...please don’t do that."
Lane muttered.
"Huh? Why?"
Shadow frowned.
"It doesn’t suit your... new look at all..."
Lane’s answer, however, only confused Shadow even further.
"Huh??"
"Tsk, such a look doesn’t suit you at all!"
Edda snorted.
"I agree."
Aisha nodded.
"Me too."
Allura nodded as well.
The rest of the women nodded as well.
"Too beautiful. Doesn’t look like her at all."
Thyra added, and once again, the rest of the women—especially Amaya—nodded without stop.
"You guys..."
Shadow didn’t know how to react.
Should she be offended?
But they were calling her beautiful...
But they were also calling her... ugly?
Is that even possible?
Just how exactly does she look for them to react like this?
Suddenly, she waved her hand. The Power of Genesis gathered around her, forming a mirror, and finally, her eyes fell on... herself.
*Picture*
"That’s... me?"
She muttered, blinking her eyes more than once. She even started pulling her cheeks and making strange expressions with her face, and the more she did it,
The stranger the women felt.
Shadow’s new look felt... too regal, like a trueborn noble instilled with proper etiquette for decades.
Seeing someone who looks like her act like... this.
It felt too out of place.
"Yep. Doesn’t suit her one bit."
Allura nodded, now becoming even surer. The women nodded once again. It was rare for all of them to agree on things, but this... this seemed to be something that brought them together.
Heck, even Shadow didn’t dare refute them.
However, not all women were thinking about this.
"Shadow, you..."
Suddenly, Felberta called out, attracting everyone’s attention.
"Hm?"
Shadow, who was currently stretching the skin beneath her right eye, glanced at Felberta and tilted her head. And Felberta...
"How did you use the Energy of Genesis...?"
Felberta questioned, and in an instant, everyone’s expression changed—even Shadow’s.
"...what?"

Shadow, as the Soul of the Universe, had the deepest connection to it. She could move anywhere in the Universe, and she could make anyone else move anywhere she wanted as well. She had a certain level of authority here, but...
All of this was done through her ’Will’.
She couldn’t use any Energies here.
But...
"It seems like I now can...?"
Shadow tilted her head as suddenly, all Ten Primordial Energies materialized around her with just her thought alone, horrifying all the women present here.
"What...?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2102: I like you.
paragraphs: "It seems like I now can...?"
Shadow tilted her head in confusion and suddenly, with just a thought, all Ten Primordial Energies materialized around her.
"What...?"
Shadow blinked, unable to understand what was happening. The rest of the women were no exceptions either; they all stared at Shadow and the Energies flowing around her.

To test it even further, Shadow began moving the energies. They moved just as she wanted them to. When she willed them to disappear, they disappeared, and before she and others could understand what was happening,

Shadow’s expression changed as her eyes fell on the man who appeared out of nowhere. In an instant, a smile appeared on her face. The rest of the women turned towards their husband and smiled as well, instantly forgetting Shadow and every strange thing she did right now.
"It is good to see you all in color."
Nux chuckled lightly.
The wives laughed.
"We finally did it, huh..."
Amaya muttered.
"Indeed."
Nux nodded. Then, he finally glanced at his wife who had changed into an entirely different person and—
"Shadow."
He called out.
"Do you like it?"

Shadow stepped forward, rolling around as if showing her new body to her husband. She even went a step ahead and fell into his arms. Again, the regal aura her new appearance gave out did not match her movements at all.
Of course, Nux couldn’t care less.
He smiled brightly as he held his wife.
"I love it~"
He praised, pulling her into his arms. Shadow laughed. She lifted her chin to the side, wanting Nux to bury his face into her neck.
Nux did what she wanted. His canines elongated, his golden eyes shining with a crimson light—clearly, he was tempted to bite her.
For now, however, he simply licked her neck and kissed her gently.
It still wasn’t over. Sharnoth was still fighting, and he did not have any real updates on how the fight was playing out.
If he wanted to protect her, getting there as fast as possible was the priority. Shadow and the others knew that as well, so after Shadow’s initial greeting, others held back and—
"Can you take care of him?"
Nux questioned, pointing towards the distant space only Shadow could see.
Neremoth.

The Darkness Eternal could escape the loop the moment Nux lost focus. If Nux left his Universe and no one took care of things here, he would be freed—and with his strength, he could cause quite a big ruckus here.
Or at least...
That was what should have happened before—
But now, things were different.
Nux’s Universe was complete, so it was now much stronger than before.
And as the Soul of this Universe and its First Goddess, the one that was affected by it the most was Shadow.

She had not only broken through the Transcendent Stage together with Nux, her connection with the Universe had strengthened to an absurd level, allowing her to use its Powers as long as the Universe, or Nux, allowed her to.
Yes, inside the Universe, she was as strong as the Universe itself—or more accurately, she had all the abilities Nux had, except for his Physical Strength and Enhanced Mind.
"Can you deal with him?"
Nux requested.
This was the fastest way. Killing Neremoth would still take some time, and honestly, Nux did not wish to kill him quickly at all.
He wanted to devour him.
After all, Neremoth wasn’t the only sadistic one in their battle. Everything he did to him—every nail pulled, every finger broken, every time he skinned him, gouged his eyes, and everything else—
Nux was planning to pay it many times over.
He wanted to see it,
The fear in his eyes. He wanted him to feel the fear of pain, just like Neremoth wanted him to.
Honestly, Neremoth’s sadistic desires strengthened Nux’s even further. This was what happened when one sadistic monster met another.
Shadow could sense Nux’s emotions. She knew what he wanted to do, and for it to happen, he needed her help, but—
"Can I... do it?"
She still wasn’t sure.
Sure, she had Nux’s powers, but she still did not have his mind. Honestly, she didn’t have as good control over all these powers as Nux did.

That was simply impossible for someone like her. Nux had trained for countless centuries to achieve the level he was at, and he was a never-seen-before genius. There was no way anyone could be even half as good as him even if they had all these powers.

"You do not have to do anything. You simply need to continue altering this space with this formula. As long as you will it, it will happen on its own. It is the same as when you used the Energy of Genesis to create the mirror just now."
Shadow wasn’t surprised that Nux knew about it. She already knew he was keeping an eye on them while fighting Neremoth, making sure they were safe all the time.
She was worried about something else,
"Would a single formula work?"
She questioned.

"I came up with this after trapping him inside. He only uses Space Artifacts to travel through space. His understanding of Space itself is lacking. The formula I came up with has been made by observing his Space Movement patterns. I already know how the artifacts work. They are not programmed to be able to counter this formula, at least for the next few hours before they learn and adapt themselves.
As for his movement abilities, there are three of them. One uses Darkness as the means, another alters the reality around him, and the last one repels his light to propel his body.
I have erased the concept of light and darkness inside that loop and have separated that space’s reality from ours, essentially crippling his movements.
All you need to do is maintain that space the way I have and constantly use the formula to keep the artifacts from teleporting him outside."

Nux explained briefly as he instilled the formula into Shadow’s head at the same time. While he was at it, he instilled the formula into the other women’s heads as well, in case Shadow needed some sort of assistance.
"Do not take too much pressure. If something goes wrong, I will return."
Nux spoke, reassuring her.
"Yes."
Shadow nodded, preparing herself as she took a deep breath.
She did not think the first thing she would do after getting a new body and powers would be to keep a fucking Eternal in check.
Now that’s a story worth telling.
Nux nodded. He kissed Shadow’s forehead gently as he stepped away from her. However, before he left—
"Nux."
Shadow called out, stopping him. He turned towards her and laughed,
"Yes, I know.
I accept what you have in your mind."
He then stared at her body perversely and,
"I wasn’t planning on letting you go anyways."
"Good."
Shadow grinned.
Nux nodded and then, he disappeared—returning to the Main Universe, right into the battlefield of two of the strongest Eternals in the entire Universe.
"Do not think your end will be dignified."
Zarveth spoke, his mind already coming up with the worst possible tortures to make Sharnoth regret her actions.
And Sharnoth...
"See, this is the difference between us.
I do not care about your end.
I would simply end you in an instant because that is all you mean to me—
Nothing."
She just shrugged disdainfully, as if Zarveth’s very existence never mattered in the first place. The two grabbed their weapons and a soft pulse spread through the space between them.
The battle had begun.
Zarveth moved first—or that was what he thought—but...
Sharnoth was faster.

She exploded forward, spinning into a storm of arms, wings, blades, and... tentacles. Yes, her current body was completely different than before. The Power of Chaos that she had been holding back all this while had now started leaking from her body, forming shapes that seemed to be escaping reality itself.
Her attack came from every direction at once—impossible to dodge for normal Eternals.
Yes, ’normal’ Eternals—not Zarveth.
The Being of Eternity first expanded his Law and created his domain. Since both of them had Absolute Laws, very quickly, their Domains crushed each other, making themselves completely ineffective.
Then, Zarveth raised his staff. This was his greatest creation—a creation that held together all his inventions and made it possible for him to use everything at will.
In an instant,
A square barrier appeared around him—the Tesseract Aegis.
It wasn’t a wall. It was folded space, and anything that touched it was sent somewhere else. Sharnoth’s attacks vanished into other parts of space, completely missing him.
"I didn’t think you would dodge this cowardly after all that grand talk."
Sharnoth laughed. Her grin, combined with the black-purple Chaos Energy leaking out of her body, gave her an entirely different aura than before.
A side that she usually hid from the world.
Something only Nux and Zylarith knew about.
She...
She was enjoying this.

Zarveth didn’t say anything. He observed the woman in silence. Clearly, even he was taken aback by how much the once solemn and regal-looking woman had changed. It looked like she was possessed and was an entirely different person.
His staff moved, changing its shape into a glowing sword.
It was another one of his Artifacts—Chronoedge, a blade made from every future where he wins.
Zarveth moved.
He wasn’t particularly fast. He had no reason to be—after all, he had already won.
Every step he took was perfect. Every swing of his sword had already succeeded before he made it.
Slash
He slashed toward Sharnoth.
But Sharnoth didn’t dodge.
She laughed—and melted into a puddle of shadows, then reappeared behind him, riding a snake made of burning roses.
"I like you,"
She said with a wink.

He wanted to devour him.
After all, Neremoth wasn’t the only sadistic one in their battle.
Everything he did to him—every nail pulled, every finger broken, every time he skinned him, gouged his eyes, and everything else—
Nux was planning to pay it many times over.
He wanted to see it,
The fear in his eyes.
He wanted him to feel the fear of pain, just like Neremoth wanted him to.
Honestly, Neremoth’s sadistic desires strengthened Nux’s even further.
This was what happened when one sadistic monster met another.
Shadow could sense Nux’s emotions.
She knew what he wanted to do, and for it to happen, he needed her help, but—
"Can I... do it?"
She still wasn’t sure.
Sure, she had Nux’s powers, but she still did not have his mind.
Honestly, she didn’t have as good control over all these powers as Nux did.
That was simply impossible for someone like her.
Nux had trained for countless centuries to achieve the level he was at, and he was a never-seen-before genius.
There was no way anyone could be even half as good as him even if they had all these powers.
"You do not have to do anything.
You simply need to continue altering this space with this formula.
As long as you will it, it will happen on its own.
It is the same as when you used the Energy of Genesis to create the mirror just now."
Shadow wasn’t surprised that Nux knew about it.
She already knew he was keeping an eye on them while fighting Neremoth, making sure they were safe all the time.
She was worried about something else,
"Would a single formula work?"
She questioned.
"I came up with this after trapping him inside.
He only uses Space Artifacts to travel through space.
His understanding of Space itself is lacking.
The formula I came up with has been made by observing his Space Movement patterns.
I already know how the artifacts work.
They are not programmed to be able to counter this formula, at least for the next few hours before they learn and adapt themselves.
As for his movement abilities, there are three of them.
One uses Darkness as the means, another alters the reality around him, and the last one repels his light to propel his body.
I have erased the concept of light and darkness inside that loop and have separated that space’s reality from ours, essentially crippling his movements.
All you need to do is maintain that space the way I have and constantly use the formula to keep the artifacts from teleporting him outside."
Nux explained briefly as he instilled the formula into Shadow’s head at the same time.
While he was at it, he instilled the formula into the other women’s heads as well, in case Shadow needed some sort of assistance.
"Do not take too much pressure.
If something goes wrong, I will return."
Nux spoke, reassuring her.
"Yes."
Shadow nodded, preparing herself as she took a deep breath.
She did not think the first thing she would do after getting a new body and powers would be to keep a fucking Eternal in check.
Now that’s a story worth telling.
Nux nodded.
He kissed Shadow’s forehead gently as he stepped away from her.
However, before he left—
"Nux."
Shadow called out, stopping him.
He turned towards her and laughed,
"Yes, I know.
I accept what you have in your mind."
He then stared at her body perversely and,
"I wasn’t planning on letting you go anyways."
"Good."
Shadow grinned.
Nux nodded and then, he disappeared—returning to the Main Universe, right into the battlefield of two of the strongest Eternals in the entire Universe.
"Do not think your end will be dignified."
Zarveth spoke, his mind already coming up with the worst possible tortures to make Sharnoth regret her actions.
And Sharnoth...
"See, this is the difference between us.
I do not care about your end.
I would simply end you in an instant because that is all you mean to me—
Nothing."
She just shrugged disdainfully, as if Zarveth’s very existence never mattered in the first place.
The two grabbed their weapons and a soft pulse spread through the space between them.
The battle had begun.
Zarveth moved first—or that was what he thought—but...
Sharnoth was faster.
She exploded forward, spinning into a storm of arms, wings, blades, and... tentacles.
Yes, her current body was completely different than before.
The Power of Chaos that she had been holding back all this while had now started leaking from her body, forming shapes that seemed to be escaping reality itself.
Her attack came from every direction at once—impossible to dodge for normal Eternals.
Yes, ’normal’ Eternals—not Zarveth.
The Being of Eternity first expanded his Law and created his domain.
Since both of them had Absolute Laws, very quickly, their Domains crushed each other, making themselves completely ineffective.
Then, Zarveth raised his staff.
This was his greatest creation—a creation that held together all his inventions and made it possible for him to use everything at will.
In an instant,
A square barrier appeared around him—the Tesseract Aegis.
It wasn’t a wall.
It was folded space, and anything that touched it was sent somewhere else.
Sharnoth’s attacks vanished into other parts of space, completely missing him.
"I didn’t think you would dodge this cowardly after all that grand talk."
Sharnoth laughed.
Her grin, combined with the black-purple Chaos Energy leaking out of her body, gave her an entirely different aura than before.
A side that she usually hid from the world.
Something only Nux and Zylarith knew about.
She...
She was enjoying this.
Zarveth didn’t say anything.
He observed the woman in silence.
Clearly, even he was taken aback by how much the once solemn and regal-looking woman had changed.
It looked like she was possessed and was an entirely different person.
His staff moved, changing its shape into a glowing sword.
It was another one of his Artifacts—Chronoedge, a blade made from every future where he wins.
Zarveth moved.
He wasn’t particularly fast.
He had no reason to be—after all, he had already won.
Every step he took was perfect.
Every swing of his sword had already succeeded before he made it.
Slash
He slashed toward Sharnoth.
But Sharnoth didn’t dodge.
She laughed—and melted into a puddle of shadows, then reappeared behind him, riding a snake made of burning roses.
"I like you,"
She said with a wink.

chapters.title: Chapter 2103: Not very easy to remember, now is it?
paragraphs: "I like you,"
She winked, moving her face right in front of Zarveth with a big grin on her face. Then, she glanced at his sword and—
"Too bad I’ll break your little toys."
She laughed.
The space around them twisted.
Now, instead of open void, they floated inside a massive ring of swirling magic—a circle of chaotic energy, spinning with colors, sounds, and pieces of broken worlds.
Dozens of copies of Sharnoth appeared all around him—each one doing something different.
One was dancing.
One was crying.
One was screaming.
Most of these Sharnoths weren’t doing anything related to Zarveth, almost as if she didn’t care about his existence.
Zarveth narrowed his eyes. Till now, he was confident in winning—even now, that hadn’t changed—but seeing the woman change so much the moment the Anomaly disappeared made him feel strange.
It was... almost as if she was trying to hide her worst side from the Anomaly and was acting properly.
’Is she... trying to impress him?’
He wondered in his head.
’Are they closer than I thought?’
Something instantly clicked in his mind. It was an emotion he had seen after a long time and—
’I can use it.’
The moment he thought about it, his staff shined, and four of his relics spun around him in response.
Suddenly, five versions of Zarveth split away from his body.
Each one moved to a different direction, countering Sharnoth’s strange attacks.
One blocked a scream that seemed like it could shatter armies.
One redirected a falling asteroid.
Another swung Chronoedge to cut through Sharnoth’s blade.
For a few moments, the battle looked even.
Zarveth’s calm, perfect movements and powerful relics kept up with Sharnoth’s wild, shifting chaos.
Their movements were fast; most of it didn’t even make sense. Because of her unpredictability, Sharnoth looked like she had the initiative, but Zarveth didn’t look like he was at a disadvantage.
The battle continued. Sharnoth laughed as she unleashed a series of attacks. Zarveth was already forced to use his 18th relic in the midst of the battle. It was something that surprised even him.

After all, most Eternals who did not come from the Four Supreme Worlds could usually be dealt with using three relics at most. The Subordinate Eternals from other Supreme Worlds were usually dealt with within fifteen relics, yet...
Sharnoth stood tall, without any change in that crazy grin of hers, even after he had used eighteen relics.
’She is stronger than I thought.’
Zarveth muttered.
Her laughter rang over his ears. He could tell how this would intimidate a young Eternal, even the ones from the Supreme Worlds. Of course, to him, this did not matter.
Rather, this only made things more interesting. He wanted to see how long she could keep this smile up.
The battle continued. Zarveth continued to use his relics to suppress Sharnoth, who attacked relentlessly and unpredictably. Her nature was similar to the energy she used—
Chaotic.
They moved across space like divine beings dancing through storms.
The space cracked.
Dimensions surrounding the region became weaker.
Fragments of light and shadow exploded with each strike.
Zarveth’s relics hummed in patterns—some of them had even cracked.
Just as Sharnoth said, she was breaking his ’toys.’ Of course, Zarveth didn’t let it affect his mind. He continued as if nothing had happened, replacing damaged artifacts with different ones.
The dense energy of Chaos around Sharnoth’s body disfigured it even further. Her form was becoming... formless.
Her entire body was cracking, and the more it was happening, the more chaotic energy she was releasing. Almost as if...
A seal was breaking and pure, unfiltered Chaos was about to be unleashed.
Yes, with every exchange, Sharnoth was getting stronger and stronger.
But...
As the battle continued, something strange began to happen.
Zarveth... he was starting to understand her.
Zarveth was billions of years old. He was in his prime when Sharnoth wasn’t even born, and he was far from falling from his prime yet—rather, he was only growing stronger.

As a being who chased after knowledge and was strengthened the more knowledge he gained, creating different relics for different situations, his rich experience made him a much, much scarier opponent.
In all these years he had existed, he had seen and analyzed hundreds of thousands of completely different powers and styles.
Sharnoth’s Chaos was unpredictable, but... Zarveth had now started to predict that very unpredictability.
He had begun to adapt.
Each time she did something new, he countered it faster.
Each time she grew more unpredictable, he grew more precise.

Her spear of thunder was dealt with like it was a harmless flicker of electricity. Her sword made of wind was blocked by a relic of perfect silence. Her illusion of a black hole was scattered by a wave of stored energy from a previous future.
Sharnoth narrowed her eyes.
She could sense what was happening as well. She could sense she was... losing.
"You’re cheating,"
She pouted.
"I’m remembering,"
Zarveth replied calmly, almost as if he was now certain of his victory.
"Is that so...?"
Sharnoth grinned even more.
Crack
The cracks on her body widened even further. A part of the skin on her elbow came off, and dense, black-purple energy of Chaos seeped out of it.
Then—
BOOOOOM
The energy of Chaos exploded, rising to levels even Zarveth did not predict, and something even stranger happened.
Sharnoth changed the rules.
The space around them shook. The stars in the far distance faded. The very universe around them began to feel... wrong.
Time moved sideways. Even Zarveth’s relics began to flicker. Some of them began misfiring, allowing Sharnoth’s clones to destroy them completely.
The lights spun backward. Zarveth began losing his footing, almost as if his mind was being altered with, and directions no longer made sense.
Before he could realize it, Sharnoth, with the big grin on her face, was already floating above him, her crimson eyes glowing with madness, her hair moving everywhere, as if no laws governed them.
Zarveth’s face turned grim.
This...
This was a domain.
It wasn’t the concept of domain people were familiar with. After all, their domains had already crushed each other—no domains could be deployed again.
This wasn’t exactly a domain, not in the known terms...
Just that...
Sharnoth was releasing so much energy of Chaos that the very reality around them was bending to her will—her Chaos.
It was a state any warrior could achieve if they released enough energy. However, it had a fatal flaw—it wasn’t a state that can be held for a long time.
Even an Eternal could not release this much ridiculous amount of energy and not feel overwhelmed. They would run out of energy, and once that happens...
It would be over.
"This is MY battlefield now.
Why don’t you try and remember this?"
Sharnoth laughed, her crimson eyes becoming even more intense. Zarveth took a deep breath as he pressed his hand into the space beneath him.
Twelve relics formed a circle around him, glowing bright and pushing back against the Chaos.
He could feel it, the temporary domain—he was slower here.
Sharnoth’s Chaos was tilting the fight.
Her madness was spreading.
But he didn’t panic.
After all, there was no way the woman would last any longer than a few minutes.

He looked around with a calm look on his face. The space around them was no longer normal. Colors floated through the void like smoke. Time flow didn’t follow natural direction. Gravity twisted in circles.
Reality no longer made sense.
Even his thoughts felt slower... heavier... confused, making it difficult to control his relics.
Flicker Flicker Flicker
His relics began to flicker.
They weren’t made to function in a place where the laws of the universe seemed... meaningless.
Sharnoth continued to float above him. Her form kept changing—tentacles, feathers, flames, mirrors, laughter.
The more time passed, the less sense it made.
"HAHAHAHA!!"
The woman laughed—loud, wild, and... crazy.
"Not very easy to remember, now is it?
Come onSupreme Born! What happened!? Aren’t you a little too silent?"
She exclaimed, releasing even more chaotic energy. The action somewhat surprised Zarveth.
She should already be feeling overwhelmed by the huge energy consumption. Releasing more energy wasn’t exactly a solution.
Or was she...
’Is she trying to end it quickly?’
Zarveth wondered inwardly. In this situation, normally, he would try to read his opponent’s expression, but the only thing he could see was that crazy smile on her face.
There was no way he could read what she was thinking—or if she was thinking at all...
For now, he just decided to make a move.
His hand moved slowly, adjusting the alignment of his relics.
But Sharnoth was faster now. Faster than anything that made sense.
BOOOOM
She attacked.
Hundreds of her appeared at once, spinning around Zarveth in wild, unpredictable patterns.
Some threw fire made of memory. Some launched spikes of pure emotion. Others whispered words that turned into blades of sound.
Her attacks became more and more unpredictable—even more than what Zarveth could adapt to.
The Eternity-born Eternal tried to block.
His relics moved to protect him, but because of his lack of control, some of them missed.
A shard struck his shoulder. A ray of melted space cut his leg.
Zarveth stumbled.
And suddenly...
Dark green blood floated out of his injuries and hovered in the void.
First blood was drawn.
And the moment she saw that,
Sharnoth’s grin widened even further.
"That’s better,"
She laughed.
"So even the oh-so-mighty Supreme Borns bleed like the rest of us, eh?
HAHAHAHA!"

chapters.title: Chapter 2104: Toy King~~
paragraphs: "So even the oh-so-mighty Supreme Borns bleed like the rest of us, eh?
HAHAHAHA!"
Sharnoth laughed like a maniac. Zarveth looked up at her, his face still seemed calm; his body, however, was now tensed.
But Sharnoth simply did not care.
She dove again.
This time, her body twisted into a spinning storm—blades, teeth, ink, feathers, everything, comprehensible and incomprehensible moved together.
BOOOOOM
Sharnoth smashed into him like a comet.
Zarveth raised a barrier as always, ready to block her attack, but—
Crack
The barrier cracked under the pressure.
Zarveth flew backward, crashing through a drifting asteroid made of frozen time. The rock exploded into black-purple dust.
Zarveth stopped himself with a flick of his hand, floating back into control.
His breathing became affected. Yes, he had taken damage after a long, long time. What’s worse?
This wasn’t yet over.
Without giving him any time to recover, Sharnoth spun in front of him, laughing wildly.
"Alright, Toy Lord!
Show me all your toys!"
The woman’s grin then widened even further and—
"So I can break every single one of them!"
"Understood."

Zarveth nodded softly. Even if he had taken damage, he didn’t show anything. Plus, the relics on his body had already started working. The wounds would be healed within a few seconds—he just needed to deal with this chaotic energy that had seeped inside his body, making it difficult for him to move.
He raised two fingers.
His staff shined and another relic—an orb covered in glowing rings—appeared around him and flared with bright light.
Temporal Rewrite.
In an instant, the damage to his body vanished.
The blood disappeared.
The cuts closed.
Even his unstable relics stabilized.
It was like the last few seconds had never happened.
Sharnoth blinked.
"Cheating again?"
She asked.
"This is called being prepared,"
Zarveth replied.
But even when his body had healed completely, the pressure was building.

Sharnoth’s partial domain continued to grow. Yes, the mad woman was putting in even more energy into this, almost as if she did not care about running out of energy at all. She was fighting as if she left the results to fate, an action that made no sense—especially in the eyes of someone like Zarveth, who calculated every possibility and only made a move when he was sure he would win.
Of course, even though he didn’t agree with her methods, right now, he had to admit that he was being overwhelmed.
His relics needed structure to function—but the stronger Sharnoth’s partial domain grew, the less ’structured’ it became.
It was too chaotic.
One moment they floated straight, the next they bent sideways or reversed. It wasn’t just space or time—every energy in this place made no sense at all.
It was pure madness.
And Sharnoth...?
She thrived in the madness.
"HAHAHA!!"
She clapped her hands, and the asteroids behind her cracked like glass. Their energy exploded and formed something that looked like wormholes.
A portal to... nowhere?
And from these portals, theycame out.
"KRRIIIEEEKK!!"
"KKRRAAAKKK!!!"
"GRRIIRRR!!!"
Incomprehensible dark purple-black creatures, creatures that could not be explained. They weren’t beasts, demons, or any known species.
They were just... ideas.
A hammer made of forgotten dreams.
A snake that bit logic and made spells fall apart.
A rain of glowing cubes that turned into music, then fire, then ice, then darkness.
And these were the most simple ones that could be described—the more... brutal-looking things were simply impossible to describe.
Even Zarveth was taken aback. Clearly, his years of experience weren’t helping here. For now, however, he activated another relic—a spinning shield made of metal and light.
The creatures all rushed at him, and the shield blocked most of them.
But not all.
One creature slipped through and bit into his mind.
Zarveth flinched, his relics dimming for a second.
For the first time in his entire life, he saw it.
Visions.
Visions that disturbed even his mind.
A Universe where he had lost.
A Universe where he had never been born.
A Universe where his relics turned on him.
His mind, which considered all the possibilities, started considering even these, and the more he thought about them, the more possibilities his mind started exploring on its own.
His strongest ability—his ability to think—had become his weakness.
His body moved on its own, pushing the creature out and burning it into nothingness.
"KRRIIIISSSHHH!!!"
The creature screeched, but it couldn’t hold on, and once it was gone, Zarveth finally heaved a sigh of relief, his mind returned to him—overloaded by all his thoughts.
For a moment, he felt it.
Fatigue.
As for Sharnoth—
Clap Clap Clap
"Hahaha!!
Good Good Good!
You did well!"
The woman clapped, spinning in joy as she laughed without stopping.
Yes, no traces of Sharnoth Nocthys, the Princess who rose Chains, could be seen from her. She seemed like an entirely different person.
Heck, she didn’t even attack Zarveth when she had the opportunity to because of how much fun she was having.
"I like you even now!"
She laughed, spinning around him as the Chaos energy around her grew even further.

He had been waiting for more than 15 minutes now!
By now, any normal Eternal would have run out of energy more than a few times, considering the absurd amount of energy this woman was using.
The very Universe was being affected by the energy she was releasing!
The very Universe!
It was already reaching the levels of Lowest-Level Worlds!
Even the Supreme Born Eternals would be at their wits’ end by now after sensing their energy reserves falling at such a ridiculous rate.
But she...
She didn’t even look like she was getting started.

If she did, it would mean she didn’t care about her energy reserves at all.
If she did not, it would mean all of this was an act—a brave front.

"Confident? What does that mean?"
Sharnoth just tilted, then a crazy smile appeared on her face and—
"Is that a new Toy!?"

"Is it fun!?!?"
Zarveth’s test—it was not made for madness.

He spoke.
"Yes, sure.

BOOOOOOOOM
Her body released even more energy of Chaos.

Just where was all this energy coming from!?
How had she still not run out of it!?

"Use better Toys, Toy King!!"
Sharnoth laughed as she increased the intensity of her ’plays.’
Her body twisted into a long spear made of spinning symbols and shot forward like a bolt of lightning.
BOOOM
Zarveth raised his blade, but the force of the strike sent him crashing through space. The impact of energy was so strong that the very space trembled.
Pieces of broken asteroids flew in every direction.
And in the silence of deep space, only Sharnoth’s voice echoed:
"Come onnnn!
Playyyy!!!"

Zarveth floated in the distance, silent, surrounded by fragments of burning stardust. The Chaos energy around him had become ridiculously strong. His mind continued to think of theories that could explain her and predict just how much energy this woman had, but suddenly...
Something happened.
Crack
Another part of Sharnoth’s skin on her forearm came off, and once again, dense, black-purple energy of Chaos seeped out of it.
And once again,
BOOOOOM
The energy density around them increased even further, horrifying Zarveth to his core.
And for the first time in this battle, this thought appeared in Zarveth’s mind.
He... He might lose.
"HAHAHA!!
I am coming!
Toy King~~"

HAHAHAHA!"
Sharnoth laughed like a maniac.
Zarveth looked up at her, his face still seemed calm; his body, however, was now tensed.
But Sharnoth simply did not care.
She dove again.
This time, her body twisted into a spinning storm—blades, teeth, ink, feathers, everything, comprehensible and incomprehensible moved together.
BOOOOOM
Sharnoth smashed into him like a comet.
Zarveth raised a barrier as always, ready to block her attack, but—
Crack
The barrier cracked under the pressure.
Zarveth flew backward, crashing through a drifting asteroid made of frozen time.
The rock exploded into black-purple dust.
Zarveth stopped himself with a flick of his hand, floating back into control.
His breathing became affected.
Yes, he had taken damage after a long, long time.
What’s worse?
This wasn’t yet over.
Without giving him any time to recover, Sharnoth spun in front of him, laughing wildly.
"Alright, Toy Lord!
Show me all your toys!"
The woman’s grin then widened even further and—
"So I can break every single one of them!"
"Understood."
Zarveth nodded softly.
Even if he had taken damage, he didn’t show anything.
Plus, the relics on his body had already started working.
The wounds would be healed within a few seconds—he just needed to deal with this chaotic energy that had seeped inside his body, making it difficult for him to move.
He raised two fingers.
His staff shined and another relic—an orb covered in glowing rings—appeared around him and flared with bright light.
Temporal Rewrite.
In an instant, the damage to his body vanished.
The blood disappeared.
The cuts closed.
Even his unstable relics stabilized.
It was like the last few seconds had never happened.
Sharnoth blinked.
"Cheating again?"
She asked.
"This is called being prepared,"
Zarveth replied.
But even when his body had healed completely, the pressure was building.
Sharnoth’s partial domain continued to grow.
Yes, the mad woman was putting in even more energy into this, almost as if she did not care about running out of energy at all.

She was fighting as if she left the results to fate, an action that made no sense—especially in the eyes of someone like Zarveth, who calculated every possibility and only made a move when he was sure he would win.
Of course, even though he didn’t agree with her methods, right now, he had to admit that he was being overwhelmed.
His relics needed structure to function—but the stronger Sharnoth’s partial domain grew, the less ’structured’ it became.
It was too chaotic.
One moment they floated straight, the next they bent sideways or reversed.
It wasn’t just space or time—every energy in this place made no sense at all.
It was pure madness.
And Sharnoth...?
She thrived in the madness.
"HAHAHA!!"
She clapped her hands, and the asteroids behind her cracked like glass.
Their energy exploded and formed something that looked like wormholes.
A portal to... nowhere?
And from these portals, theycame out.
"KRRIIIEEEKK!!"
"KKRRAAAKKK!!!"
"GRRIIRRR!!!"
Incomprehensible dark purple-black creatures, creatures that could not be explained.
They weren’t beasts, demons, or any known species.
They were just... ideas.
A hammer made of forgotten dreams.
A snake that bit logic and made spells fall apart.
A rain of glowing cubes that turned into music, then fire, then ice, then darkness.
And these were the most simple ones that could be described—the more... brutal-looking things were simply impossible to describe.

chapters.title: Chapter 2105: Legacy of Zylarith Chaosveil.
paragraphs: "HAHAHA!!
I am coming!
Toy King~~"
Sharnoth laughed, losing whatever little control she had over herself.
Zarveth floated in space, breathing slowly.
He had a solemn look on his face. The relics around him continued to flicker nonstop, their condition worsening with each second.
By now, he had already used sixty-three relics in this battle.

It was already at the level of facing experienced Supreme Borns from other Supreme Worlds. Honestly, if instead of him, a million-year-old or a younger Eternal was facing her, the battle would have ended in her victory already.
’And to think she is only a hundred thousand years old...’
Zarveth thought inwardly with a grim look on his face. One of his attacks had managed to penetrate her body, allowing him to check her bone density, and the results surprised him.
Of course, right now, he didn’t have the time to care about those emotions. He could no longer look down on her.
"Tsk."

The Eternity Born snorted, replacing another one of his relics that had broken down. A small crack ran through the edge of the armor that had protected him since the battle started. There were blood marks on his cloak, and his left hand was trembling slightly.
It had never happened before, not in a long, long time, even when he faced a few of the strongest beings in the Universe.
But now... he was being pushed back.
Sharnoth smiled wide, spinning slowly in the air, glowing with wild purple and black energy. Pieces of space behind her kept breaking apart, unable to handle the madness leaking from her body.
"This is so much fun!"
She laughed. Her crimson eyes glared at Zarveth and—
"You are the best toy I ever had!"
She praised.
"You’re still standing!! It feels like I can go all out without having to worry about you breaking easily!!"
She exclaimed excitedly, applauding for Zarveth for being such a good sport.
Zarveth didn’t answer.
His eyes studied her calmly. His relics floated close, forming a tight shield. He needed answers, and he needed them desperately if he wanted to win.
’How is her energy not running out?’
He couldn’t understand.
No Eternal—no matter how strong—could release this much power for long. She was moving faster, striking harder, and using attacks that bent space like paper.

Even her illusions were becoming real. The partial domain she had created now looked almost as strong as a real one. There was so much chaos around him that the number of relics he could use was being limited.
Relics dependent on their surroundings had already become useless.
That amount of output... even the oldest Eternals would have collapsed by now.
Yes, even the strongest Supreme Borns Eternals from the Supreme Worlds were no exception. They would have collapsed and run out of energy as well.
But Sharnoth didn’t slow down.
In fact—she got faster.
The woman charged again, her body turning into a tornado of blades and wings. Zarveth raised three relics. A barrier appeared.
It held—for two seconds—before cracking.
BOOOOM
The woman slammed into him, and he flew backward, crashing into a drifting mass of metal and bones—where they came from?
He had no clue.
Neither could he think about it, because Sharnoth didn’t allow him to.
She didn’t wait.
She materialized behind him instantly and kicked him through a glowing ring of warped time. He landed hard—even in space, the impact cracked his armor.
Zarveth stabilized himself. His face stayed calm, but his thoughts moved faster than ever.
Answers.
He needed answers!!
His thoughts started to become chaotic, he...
He started panicking.
"Still releasing energy... no cooldown... no cost..."
He muttered, his confusion only growing stronger with each passing second. For a second, he even thought about escaping.
Of course, that thought disappeared as soon as it appeared. He had already committed to this path, he simply could not give up now.
After all, he had nowhere left to escape.
If he failed to get his hands on the Anomaly, the Infinities would find him no matter what he did, and once that happened... death would become an option he would choose in an instant.
A leisure.
Zarveth trembled at that thought. Even he, who had lived for billions of years, didn’t dare to think about what would happen to him if he was captured.
Instantly, he shifted his focus back on Sharnoth. His mind once again began finding ways to defeat her.
And during all this—
"HAHAHAHA!"
Sharnoth laughed, floating upside down now, her hands glowing with swirling black-purple light.
Then—he saw it.
The crack on her skin widened, and a piece of skin under her right eye came out, and once again—
BOOOOOM
Instead of blood, pure Chaos energy exploded outward.
This was the third time this had happened. Zarveth didn’t miss it before, he didn’t miss it now, and soon, his mind started moving again.
That purple-black thing hiding beneath her skin... whatever it was...
That was dangerous.
The Eternity Born narrowed his eyes, trying to think but—
Another attack came.
Whoosh
Sharnoth threw a ball of shifting matter—part star, part storm, part shadow. Zarveth dodged, but the ball split into dozens of smaller shards that looped around him, chasing him with wild motion.
He waved a relic—Chrono Displacement—and blinked out of their path.
But even that took more effort than before. The domain had gotten stronger again, and as if that wasn’t enough—
Another patch of skin peeled off—this time her arm.
BOOOOM
More Chaos energy blasted out.
"...What are you doing?"
Unable to hold back any longer, Zarveth finally questioned.
"Hmm?"
Sharnoth tilted her head, confused.
"Your skin... it’s peeling."
"Ehehehe~"
She giggled.
"Oh, this? It doesn’t hurt, silly.
It’s just the boring layer coming off."
She reached up and scratched her shoulder. A long strip of skin peeled away—and the light that burst from beneath shook the stars.
BOOOOOOOOOM

Even more energy was released. The purple-black energy all around the Universe became much, much denser. Even the Universe Energy that devoured everything around it stopped working—almost as if all this Chaos was changing its property.
That was simply how ridiculous this energy was.
Zarveth sensed this as well, and he did not like this.
’Zylarith Chaosveil.’
He sensed a jolt down his very spine as he recalled that name.
’Did he really...?
He couldn’t believe it, his eyes staring at Sharnoth in disbelief.
Authority.

That was what made the Supreme Worlds as strong as they were. Unlike other worlds that tried to develop themselves, the Supreme Worlds understood that there was a limit to how strong a world could grow.
Therefore, instead of their own world, they expanded their focus to the rest of the Universe. The Supreme Borns started forming Absolute Dependent Laws—Laws that they called ’Authority’.
The Supreme World of Light had the Authority over positivity. Any positive thing that happened in the entire Universe—peace, love, birth of a new life, or growth—it strengthened them.
Just like that, the Supreme Worlds of Darkness and Balance developed their own Authorities.
However, the one who had the strongest Authority out of all Supreme Worlds was...
The Fifth Supreme World, the Supreme World of Chaos.
They had the Authority over Chaos.
Chaos was different from other energies. While Light, Darkness, and Balance had to make it so that the Universe was in their favor...
The Light wanted to keep Peace. Darkness wanted to wage War. And Balance wanted to keep the balance between these two energies.
But Chaos?
It simply did not matter.

Be it Peace, War, or a perfectly Balanced, ideal world, Chaos continued to grow. It was the sole energy that is never limited, an energy that could never be contained—an energy so strong that the Supreme World of Chaos became the strongest Supreme World simply because it had Authority over Chaos.
However, not everything was perfect with this energy.

As if the very Universe wanted to balance it, the Energy of Chaos was so strong that the being sitting at the very top of this ladder—the Chaos Progenitor, or the Chaos Infinity—a being who handled the ever-growing Chaotic Energy of the entire Universe, couldn’t keep this energy for long.
The Energy of Chaos ruined their bodies—so much so that no Chaos Infinity lasted more than a billion years.
Yes, every single Chaos Infinity perished after a billion years had passed because their body couldn’t take the abuse and contain this wild energy. There was no exception to this rule.
For trillions of years, this became a cycle. A cycle that lasts a billion years.

At the end of this cycle, a new Progenitor is chosen. The new Progenitor, because of his inexperience, weakens the Supreme World of Chaos, and by the time he becomes strong enough, the cycle restarts again.
This kept the Supreme World of Chaos from growing too strong, maintaining the Universal balance.
But...
This changed when ’he’ took over.
The Supreme World of Chaos’s last Progenitor—Zylarith Chaosveil.
Even before he became the next Progenitor and an Infinity, Zylarith created something he called the ’Body of Chaos’—a body capable of handling any amount of Universal Energy without any problems.

He was hands down the strongest Eternal who had ever lived in the history of the Universe—capable of taking on multiple Supreme Born Eternals from all Supreme Worlds at the same time and still coming out victorious.

Even as an Eternal, his power was so absolute that none dared to challenge him. He truly was the strongest under the Five Supreme Infinities. The Chaos Infinity was so proud of him that he gave his life on his own just to make sure that he could choose Zylarith as the next Progenitor and nothing out of the ordinary happened.
And once Zylarith was crowned as the next Progenitor and became an Infinity—
The Supreme World of Chaos ushered into a new era.
His Body of Chaos achieved something no one else was able to—he became the sole Chaos Infinity to live past a billion years, and he still went strong.

So strong that eventually, he reached a level where he could defeat other Infinities—who were much, much, much older than him—in a fair one-on-one battle without any problems. On his good days, he even took two of them at the same time.
His achievements sealed the Supreme World of Chaos’s place at the very top, making it the strongest out of all Supreme Worlds.
While he himself was crowned as the undisputed strongest Infinity to ever exist in the history of the Universe.
That was the legacy of Zylarith Chaosveil and his Body of Chaos.
And right now...
His famed Body of Chaos...
Zarveth could see its reflection in Sharnoth.
Zylarith Chaosveil.
The name that once echoed throughout the Universe, that madness... that impossible legacy...
It was breathing again—inher.

Even the Universe Energy that devoured everything around it stopped working—almost as if all this Chaos was changing its property.
That was simply how ridiculous this energy was.
Zarveth sensed this as well, and he did not like this.
’Zylarith Chaosveil.’
He sensed a jolt down his very spine as he recalled that name.
’Did he really...?
He couldn’t believe it, his eyes staring at Sharnoth in disbelief.
Authority.
That was what made the Supreme Worlds as strong as they were.
Unlike other worlds that tried to develop themselves, the Supreme Worlds understood that there was a limit to how strong a world could grow.
Therefore, instead of their own world, they expanded their focus to the rest of the Universe.
The Supreme Borns started forming Absolute Dependent Laws—Laws that they called ’Authority’.
The Supreme World of Light had the Authority over positivity.
Any positive thing that happened in the entire Universe—peace, love, birth of a new life, or growth—it strengthened them.
Just like that, the Supreme Worlds of Darkness and Balance developed their own Authorities.
However, the one who had the strongest Authority out of all Supreme Worlds was...
The Fifth Supreme World, the Supreme World of Chaos.
They had the Authority over Chaos.
Chaos was different from other energies.
While Light, Darkness, and Balance had to make it so that the Universe was in their favor...
The Light wanted to keep Peace.
Darkness wanted to wage War.
And Balance wanted to keep the balance between these two energies.
But Chaos?
It simply did not matter.
Be it Peace, War, or a perfectly Balanced, ideal world, Chaos continued to grow.

It was the sole energy that is never limited, an energy that could never be contained—an energy so strong that the Supreme World of Chaos became the strongest Supreme World simply because it had Authority over Chaos.
However, not everything was perfect with this energy.

As if the very Universe wanted to balance it, the Energy of Chaos was so strong that the being sitting at the very top of this ladder—the Chaos Progenitor, or the Chaos Infinity—a being who handled the ever-growing Chaotic Energy of the entire Universe, couldn’t keep this energy for long.
The Energy of Chaos ruined their bodies—so much so that no Chaos Infinity lasted more than a billion years.
Yes, every single Chaos Infinity perished after a billion years had passed because their body couldn’t take the abuse and contain this wild energy.
There was no exception to this rule.
For trillions of years, this became a cycle.
A cycle that lasts a billion years.
At the end of this cycle, a new Progenitor is chosen.
The new Progenitor, because of his inexperience, weakens the Supreme World of Chaos, and by the time he becomes strong enough, the cycle restarts again.
This kept the Supreme World of Chaos from growing too strong, maintaining the Universal balance.
But...
This changed when ’he’ took over.
The Supreme World of Chaos’s last Progenitor—Zylarith Chaosveil.
Even before he became the next Progenitor and an Infinity, Zylarith created something he called the ’Body of Chaos’—a body capable of handling any amount of Universal Energy without any problems.

He was hands down the strongest Eternal who had ever lived in the history of the Universe—capable of taking on multiple Supreme Born Eternals from all Supreme Worlds at the same time and still coming out victorious.
Even as an Eternal, his power was so absolute that none dared to challenge him.
He truly was the strongest under the Five Supreme Infinities.
The Chaos Infinity was so proud of him that he gave his life on his own just to make sure that he could choose Zylarith as the next Progenitor and nothing out of the ordinary happened.
And once Zylarith was crowned as the next Progenitor and became an Infinity—
The Supreme World of Chaos ushered into a new era.
His Body of Chaos achieved something no one else was able to—he became the sole Chaos Infinity to live past a billion years, and he still went strong.
So strong that eventually, he reached a level where he could defeat other Infinities—who were much, much, much older than him—in a fair one-on-one battle without any problems.
On his good days, he even took two of them at the same time.
His achievements sealed the Supreme World of Chaos’s place at the very top, making it the strongest out of all Supreme Worlds.
While he himself was crowned as the undisputed strongest Infinity to ever exist in the history of the Universe.
That was the legacy of Zylarith Chaosveil and his Body of Chaos.
And right now...
His famed Body of Chaos...
Zarveth could see its reflection in Sharnoth.
Zylarith Chaosveil.
The name that once echoed throughout the Universe, that madness... that impossible legacy...
It was breathing again—inher.

chapters.title: Chapter 2106: Booo!!
paragraphs: Zylarith Chaosveil.
The name that once echoed throughout the Universe, that madness... that impossible legacy...
It was breathing again—inher.
"HAHAHA!"
Zarveth felt his very soul shake when he heard that laughter again.
More and more of Sharnoth’s skin was coming off, releasing more and more Energy of Chaos, strengthening the partial domain she had created.
’So she is the onehechose, huh...’
Zarveth muttered inwardly, his left hand started to tremble.
Suddenly, all his questions were answered.
The source of Sharnoth’s seemingly limitless energy—it was all clear now.
’She’s not using her energy alone.’
He realized it as he looked at the purple-black glow bursting from under her skin. He could feel its connection with the space around them.
Yes, Sharnoth wasn’t just using her own Energy of Chaos.
She...
She was using the Universe’s Energy of Chaos. She was using the Authority of Chaos, just like the Supreme Borns from Light, Darkness, and Balance.
Yes, Zarveth was no longer fighting any random Eternal. He was fighting an Eternal from the strongest Supreme World, the Supreme World of Chaos.
Not just that—the said Eternal’s potential was somewhat comparable to the strongest being to ever exist in the history of the Universe.
In an instant, the situation flipped. Zarveth was no longer in the position to look down on Sharnoth. His gaze now became much more solemn than before.
His mind, however, still couldn’t comprehend this.
Most beings in the Universe did not know, but he, as one of the oldest beings in this Universe, knew that Zylarith’s story hadn’t ended with the destruction of the Supreme World of Chaos.
The Chaos Progenitor was still alive.
And while those who knew this did not care about it because it is said that the Chaos Progenitor is too weak to do anything...
Somewhere in his heart, Zarveth found it foolish.

How could the strongest being to ever exist end up in such a state? According to him, it was foolish to underestimate him, and the Infinities should get rid of that monster entirely before it is too late.

Honestly, the reason he was first interested in Sharnoth was because she was using the Energy of Chaos. He knew she must have some connection with Zylarith. He just did not know the connection between them was so strong.
To think she inherited his Body of Chaos.
But...
’Why would Lord Zylarith choose... her?’
He wondered inwardly.
From the looks of it, the woman seemed close to the Anomaly. No, she didn’t just look close to him, she... she seemed like she was his subordinate.
Why would the one who was chosen by Lord Zylarith be... someone else’s subordinate?
Also, what is the connection between Lord Zylarith and the Anomaly?
Could it be that in all this time, Lord Zylarith developed something even stronger than the Body of Chaos and passed it to the Anomaly?
Could it be... that the Anomaly is Lord Zylarith’s true disciple and this woman is merely the Anomaly’s guard?
’But to teach the Body of Chaos to a mere bodyguard...
Does it no longer hold the same importance?’
Zarveth wondered in his head.
He still did not know the powers the Anomaly had, but seeing how the very Universe reacts to it, he could tell that it was something much grander, even when compared to the Body of Chaos.
He could see how what the Anomaly has would be more important—something much stronger—but...
Zarveth couldn’t believe the Body of Chaos was something that could be thrown away.
This woman—there was no way she was just a mere subordinate.
’I need more answers.’
His hollow eyes shined, staring at Sharnoth desperately. The woman continued to smile. The Energy of Chaos around her continued to grow.
"You’re looking pale, old man,"
She teased with a huge grin.
"Don’t tell me you’re scared?"
Zarveth didn’t reply.

He just prepared himself for the battle ahead. He could see it—Sharnoth’s Body of Chaos was incomplete. It couldn’t control the Energy of Chaos completely. She still needed to spend her own energy to do it.

So while the body still helped her control more energy than normal, there was still a limit to how much energy she could use. So eventually, she would run out of energy and fall. He just needed to hold on till then.
Honestly, Zarveth got lucky.
If he had met this woman any later, when she had completely inherited the Body of Chaos, this day would have been his last.
As long as the Body of Chaos wasn’t complete, he could still win and get all the answers he wanted.
With a determined look on his face, he clenched his staff tightly, ready to end this battle.
Sharnoth floated in front of him upside down. The woman wasn’t even panting, she was just smiling because of how much fun she was having.
The energy around her felt heavier now.
Her body shimmered like glass filled with lightning. More pieces of her old skin peeled off—her arm, her thigh, her back. From beneath, a glowing body formed, shining like a black sun.
Zarveth’s relics spun faster, preparing his attack, but Sharnoth was faster. The woman raised both her hands and—
"Boom."
She laughed as a tidal wave of Chaos energy exploded from her. It rolled across space like a living storm—colors and sounds no being could understand.
Zarveth summoned twenty relics at once.
A sphere of protection formed around him, barely holding against the ridiculous attack.
But Sharnoth wasn’t done.
From inside the wave, she appeared again, her body half-transformed, glowing with energy so dense it made Zarveth’s relics flicker.
She raised a hand. A long lance of Chaos formed—black, purple, and silver, shimmering with power.
"Come onnnn~~
Why did you stop talking!?
Don’t tell me you are tired already~~
Or are you really that scared~~
You aren’t scared, are you???"
The woman questioned, tilting her head like an innocent demon toying with her prey.
Then—
She threw the lance.
Pierce
It tore through space. Zarveth’s relics moved to protect him but...
BOOM

One of his strongest defensive relics, Tesseract Aegis, exploded in an instant, unable to take the unbearable amount of force any longer. The crack on Zarveth’s armor widened, and the impact sent him flying.
His hand bled. Floating in silence, he took a breath, looking at his damaged hand and broken Tesseract Aegis with a surprised look on his face.
The rest of his relics floated around him—still loyal, but their energy was dwindling. They could no longer keep up.
Zarveth realized it as well.
He looked up and saw Sharnoth floating above him, spinning slowly, clapping as he blocked another one of her attacks, and soon, another similar spear appeared in her hand.
No...
It wasn’t just one.
Whoosh Whoosh Whoosh
Ten more similar-looking spears appeared behind her as her crazed grin widened even further, her crimson eyes shining dangerously.
She was using the same attack that shattered one of his strongest relics like it was nothing more than just some random spell she could use anytime she wanted.
There was no cooldown, no high energy requirements, nothing...
It was... effortless.
And when Zarveth realized it, he gulped.
He once again noticed the part of skin on her left leg coming out, releasing even more Energy of Chaos, and he realized it.
This woman...
Her energy wasn’t running out.
She wasn’t weakening.
No, it was the opposite.
She was evolving.
The more of her skin she lost, the stronger her connection to Chaos became—the more ’complete’ her Body of Chaos became.
And the more... energy she had.
’She... She is building the Body of Chaos... during the battle!’
Zarveth’s eyes widened in horror.
This... this couldn’t happen!
If he didn’t stop her before her transformation was complete, she would no longer need to use her own energy to manipulate the Universe’s Chaos.
She would gain limitless power, making her unstoppable. The battle would be as good as over then!
He needed to end it right now!
Not in a few minutes, not when he found the perfect counter—
Now.
There was no other way.
After a long time, he felt a sense of urgency, but then—
While Zarveth was thinking all this, suddenly, Sharnoth appeared behind him and—
"Booo~~"
"Aaaahhh!!"
She gave him a scare, looking right at him with her deep, horrifying crimson eyes. In an instant, the Eternity Born moved away.
"HAHAHA!!"
Sharnoth started laughing, holding her belly as if laughing so hard made her stomach ache.
"S-Stop this!! Are you t-trying to make me laugh to death!? HAHAHA!!
TheSupremeBorns!!
Pffftt!"
The woman continued to laugh. Zarveth stared at her in silence, almost as if he was saying his last prayers in his head.
But then suddenly—
"You are strong.
You leave me no other choice."

He spoke as he raised his hand, and from deep within the folds of space, a new, oddly perfect amount of light shined, and a set of six relics emerged—each one larger, more detailed, more complete than any of the ones Zarveth used before.
They didn’t look like weapons or tools. They looked like concepts—ideas carved into matter.
They floated around him slowly, humming with a quiet, ancient sound. And the instant Sharnoth saw them...
Her smile faded.
"...those aren’t yours,"
She muttered. The energy these things released was completely different from the relics Zarveth used before.
And this time—
Zarveth was the one who smiled.
"As I said,
You didn’t leave me any other choice."

chapters.title: Chapter 2107: I feared this might happen.
paragraphs: "...those aren’t yours,"
Sharnoth muttered, staring at the six relics that appeared out of nowhere with a solemn look on her face.
It seemed quite strange to look at her serious face when all she had been doing all this while was laughing like a maniac who had lost her mind.
Zarveth, however, instead of feeling strange—
"As I said,
You didn’t leave me any other choice."
He just smiled lightly.
"I must praise you though,
I thought you had lost yourself in your emotions, but you can sense danger even in that state, huh?
Does this mean you didn’t consider me an actual threat till now?"
He questioned curiously. Even though his own question put him down, he didn’t mind; his curiosity far overwhelmed his sense of shame.
Not to mention, this woman wouldn’t survive for long anyway. This incident would disintegrate here with her.
"...what are these?"
Sharnoth questioned.
"Shouldn’t you answer my question first?"

Zarveth chuckled. He could tell that Sharnoth was trying to buy time to complete her Body of Chaos. However, he could also see that time wasn’t everything she needed. If that were the case, she would have been a lot stronger than she currently was.
The Body of Chaos was the strongest physique known to the universe. There was no one who could comprehend it just because they had ’enough time.’
More than time, Sharnoth needed to continue to comprehend Chaos through battle.

Yes, that was what the woman needed—a fight against a being stronger than her, a fight where she could push herself beyond her limits and comprehend the True Chaos. This was the reason she, who had been Eternal for a long time now, was finally making progress.
She had finally found a being she didn’t have to hold back against.
But if Zarveth stopped trying...?
Sharnoth’s progress would halt again.
Or at least that was Zarveth’s theory, and right now, he was willing to risk it. After all, he now had the absolute advantage.
"I will answer when you answer."
Sharnoth narrowed her eyes, the Chaos energy around her increasing even now. Zarveth laughed; he didn’t miss what the woman was trying to do.
"You are correct. These relics aren’t mine."
Zarveth nodded, deciding to answer Sharnoth’s question.
"They were forged by Lord Infinity himself."
"Lord Infinity...?"
Sharnoth narrowed her eyes, and Zarveth’s grin widened.
"Indeed."
"Can you... use those?"
Suddenly, Sharnoth questioned with a frown on her face.
Zarveth tilted his head and—
"I thought the relics distributed throughout the universe were connected to the Supreme Worlds. Shouldn’t it be the same for the relics given to you by the Infinity?
Using those relics..."
"Lord Infinity would find out about our battle."
Zarveth completed the woman’s words, and Sharnoth frowned.
Did he really want Lord Infinity to know about them?
But he just betrayed them...
There was no way the Infinities would let him go after this. His past actions had all been trying to hide from the Infinities and learn the Anomaly’s secrets. Then why...
"You underestimate him."
Suddenly, Zarveth spoke up, attracting Sharnoth’s attention.

"He is connected to every relic that is created inside the Supreme World of Eternity. Because I share his blood, it doesn’t matter if I create my relics on my own. If he ever desires it, my relics will become his.
If he wishes to observe me, he doesn’t have to use the relics he gave to me. He can connect through any relic present in the universe and observe any being he wishes."
He revealed.
"Then why..."
Sharnoth frowned as more and more questions appeared in her head.
"He simply does not bother."
Zarveth frowned.
"According to him, we were sent to deal with mere mercenaries. He wouldn’t waste his time keeping an eye on us.
Even if I use his relics, as long as I do not spend too much time, everything will be fine."
"Then why didn’t you use these relics before?"
Sharnoth asked another question.
"I didn’t feel the need to."
Zarveth answered honestly. Then, his grin widened and—
"It wouldn’t have been fun if I defeated you before you could show me all this, wouldn’t it?"
"You sound confident, quite different from how you were acting before."
"Aren’t you the same? I’m not hearing that crazy laughter anymore."
Zarveth chuckled and suddenly—
"Is that so?"
Sharnoth grinned as well.
This time, however, her grin did not affect Zarveth. Rather—
"For billions of years, I worked harder than anyone to get these relics in hopes to use them against beings who I feel threatened by to change the tides of battle,
But by the time I got these, I reached a level where very few could challenge me and make me use them.
Today, however, is different."
He began, as he then looked into Sharnoth’s eyes and—
"Congratulations,

You have become one of the beings who successfully managed to make me feel threatened. For a mere hundred-thousand-year-old Eternal, it is something you can boast about for the rest of your reincarnations."
He declared, as suddenly—
The relics around him snapped into formation.
One was a circular mirror that reflected not the present—but the ideal future.
Another was a pen-like blade that could rewrite anything it touched.
A cube of silence, that erased sound, thought, and will.
A key, that unlocked the structure of time and bent it in favor of the wielder.
A lantern, that showed all possibilities at once.
And at the center—the Crest of Chronos, the true mark of the Eternal Infinity.
As they lit up, the space around Zarveth changed. Different energies that seemed chaotic started realigning.
Time stabilized.
Space strengthened.
All other Primordial Energies found a balance they had initially lost and—
Chaos was... pushed back.
"That’s not fair."
Sharnoth pouted, her grin, however, did not fade away. Rather, it only widened. She wanted to see it; she wanted to peek into the strength of an Infinity!
"It never was."
Zarveth laughed at her words, as he then moved. His movements were no longer slow. The Chaos that made it difficult for his relics to work properly no longer seemed to bother him.
He no longer had to play defensive.
He dashed forward, and space bent to make way.

The blade-pen slashed through Sharnoth’s partial domain—instantly changing its property mid-battle. Sharnoth tried to change it, unleashing more Chaos energy to overpower Zarveth’s relics, just like she had always done till now,
But this time, it didn’t work.
Sharnoth, however, did not give up. She waved her hand, and a wave of Chaos energy exploded toward Zarveth, trying to overwhelm his emotions and weaken his connection with his relics.
Sharnoth wanted to use this chance to take away these relics and end the battle, but the mirror relic showed only a future where it failed—and so, it did.
The cube of silence floated past her—placing her in an empty void where, even though she wasn’t chained, her movements were taken away.
She tried to shift and materialize somewhere else through the Chaos dispersed everywhere. Her body blurred, but then froze mid-transformation, locked in place by the key relic.
Zarveth raised a hand, and the Crest of Chronos glowed.
"Chaos cannot grow,"
He declared.
"Not if time itself refuses to move."
His calm words showed just how much control of the battlefield he had regained. The Infinity Relics were simply too powerful. Sharnoth couldn’t do anything against them.
