chapters.title: Chapter 2116: Where am I?
paragraphs: Nux reappeared in front of him and with a flick of his finger, all his women were teleported next to him.

The women stared at him in silence. Even though they had concluded that they were safe, they still couldn’t completely discard the possibility of Zylarith having a certain level of control over their bodies.
The more they thought about it, the bigger the seed of doubt grew.

Amaya even thought about how Zylarith was able to take over Sharnoth’s body in the past, even when she hadn’t completed Body of Chaos. Sure, it was merely for a second, but at their level, a single second could have fatal consequences.
Of course, she also thought about several counters to this theory, making it seem Zylarith didn’t hold any power, but she just couldn’t convince her mind.
Nux knew what the women were thinking, and he couldn’t blame them. The thought didn’t leave his mind either.
For now, however, there was no point worrying about it. Even if Zylarith had some level of control over his body, he didn’t gain this control recently—he had it a long time ago.
Suddenly worrying about it made no sense, not unless they had a way to solve this problem, which they did not.
Therefore, Nux decided to focus on what was important.
He waved his hand again, and this time, Sharnoth appeared in front of him.
After Nux devoured Zarveth, he became a part of his Universe, and Sharnoth was no exception. Their bodies reformed in Nux’s Universe with no connections to their respective worlds or Universes.
The only difference between the two was that unlike Zarveth, who still hadn’t regained his consciousness because Nux willed it so, Sharnoth was awake and she...
She had absolutely no idea what was happening.
She called out, confused.
"You all are here as well..."
She muttered, staring at Nux’s wives.
"I-It is nice to meet you..."
She greeted politely. Nux had helped her a lot; she couldn’t be disrespectful to his wives. After all, she knew how much he cherished them.
The women blinked in surprise. While they were all expecting a greeting...thiswasn’t what they had in their minds.
Sharnoth, however, didn’t seem to notice their surprise. She looked around. From the looks of it, this seemed like Outer Space; at the same time, it felt... different.
There were a few things she couldn’t recognize, things she had never heard of in her entire life.
"Nux... where is this place?"
She questioned with an uncertain look on her face. Soon, however, without listening to the answer, the frown on her face deepened as she stared at her own hands,
"And... why do I feel... different?"
She muttered, confused.
She inspected her body, staring at her arms and legs. Physically, her appearance was still the same. No, actually, something was different—the crack on her face was no longer there.
Yes, her body was reformed completely. The skin she had shed was now back.
But that was it—
Her physical appearance may not have changed too much, but everything else...
It was completely different.
She still had complete Body of Chaos, making her entire body nothing but an Entity of Chaos.
She was now the Physical Manifestation of Chaos.
The amount of energy inside her body did not matter. She could now connect with the Chaos Energy around her and use it without any limits whatsoever.
Yes, she had now become an entity with an endless amount of energy—a monster through and through.
And Sharnoth could feel that.
She could feel how much her body had changed; she could feel just how much stronger she had become.
She just... could not understand how this happened.
"So... does it mean you no longer wish to play with me?"
As the confused Sharnoth tried to understand how all this happened, she suddenly heard a strange question.
"What? Play...?"
She tilted her head, now even more confused.
"So you don’t remember, huh..."

Nux muttered in a low voice. His wives finally realized it as well. No wonder current Sharnoth was acting so differently. Honestly, they were expecting the woman to instantly jump at them and start ’playing’.

Honestly, Astaria and Vyriana were actually looking forward to it. They knew Sharnoth was much stronger than them, but they still wanted to ’play’ with her. They wanted to defeat her, even if it took hundreds of thousands of years.
Of course, the fact that they couldn’t die inside Nux’s Universe gave them even more confidence to go all out.
For now, however, the two warriors could only feel disappointed. They stared at each other and sighed.
The rest of the women shook their heads when they saw how the two were acting. They were indeed helpless.
As for Sharnoth...
"I don’t remember...?"
She frowned.
"What do you mean...?
I remember I was fighting that Supreme..."
Suddenly, Sharnoth’s expression changed.
"Nux! What happened to him!? And are you alright!? The Eternal from Supreme World of Darkness chased after you!
Where is he now!? Is he still after you!? Are you alri—"
"Calm down."
Nux spoke, his voice heavier than before. His words seemed to have a much stronger effect on Sharnoth than she expected. For an instant, all her questions were flushed out of her mind.
And finally,
"Zarveth is dead."
Nux informed.
"I killed him."
Sharnoth blinked.
"Yes, I broke through."
"What...?"
"I broke through."
Nux repeated.
"So you are now..."
"A Transcendent."
Nux answered honestly, and Sharnoth... she had no clue how Nux being a Transcendent could possibly be related to him killing Zarveth, an Eternal.
Yes, he was strong, much stronger than any normal cultivator she had met. The tricks he used were creative enough for even Eternals to fall for his words, but...
The enemy was an Eternal, that too, from one of the Four Strongest Worlds. There was no way a Transcendent could defeat someone as strong as Zarveth.
Just... what happened...
Sharnoth could not understand.

She also didn’t understand why she couldn’t recall her battle with Zarveth. All she knew was that she challenged him, they exchanged some blows, and after that, it was all a blank—almost as if someone took over her.
Suddenly, Sharnoth’s expression changed.
In an instant, she suspectedhim.
"Didheappear...?"

She questioned with a grim look on her face. Of course, she still had doubts. First, Zylarith could only take control over her body for less than a second, and even then, the last time he did it, she remembered everything he did. Her mind did not blank out.
Or...
Did something else happen...?
Did he find a way to take over her body for a longer period of time in a way that she won’t remember anything after it?
The instant that thought appeared in her head, her eyes widened in fright,
"Nux, move away from me! It isn’t safe!"
She warned Nux.
The last thing she wanted was for that man to take control over her body and get to Nux through her.

This was also the reason she only used call artifacts to contact Nux and never once appeared in front of him. Even when they attacked Zarveth, they only did it after Zarveth changed the Space Laws, making it difficult for anyone to teleport next to them, and before that, Sharnoth had constantly used her domain to make sure Zarveth wasn’t around her and didn’t know anything they were planning.
They were beingthatcareful, and Sharnoth didn’t want all of it to go to waste because of one mistake.
But—
"He didn’t appear, at least not now."
Nux shook his head, trying to calm her down.
"And even if he does appear, it won’t be here."
"What does that mean...? Where are we?"
Sharnoth questioned and—
"My Universe."
"Your... what...?"
Sharnoth blinked. She was one hundred percent sure she heard him wrong.
At her innocent reaction, the women smiled. Nux too, took a deep breath.
It was finally time to reveal everything so they could get on the same page.
"This place is..."
The explanation began. The more Sharnoth heard, the more ridiculous expressions appeared on her face. Nux had to constantly prove his words to assure her that he wasn’t trying to fool her.
And after about an hour of constant back and forth, Sharnoth decided to believe him—barely.
She still had doubts, quite a few of them actually, but for now, she decided to put blind faith in Nux. After all, she had something much more important to worry about—
"Why do I not remember my battle with Zarveth?"
She questioned and—
"Because it wasn’t you who fought him."
Nux answered directly.
"What...?"
Sharnoth’s expression changed, and this time, Nux’s expression became a little difficult as well.
"This is just my theory, but honestly, I am pretty sure that is the case."
"What does that mean?"
"The one who fought Zarveth was your True Self—no, calling her your True Self won’t be correct anymore..."
Nux frowned as well, thinking of a way to explain this to Sharnoth and his wives, and soon, the right words came to his mind,
"Yes! Your other self!
The one who defeated Zarveth was your other self!"
Nux answered proudly, completely believing that his words made perfect sense, but...

Suddenly worrying about it made no sense, not unless they had a way to solve this problem, which they did not.
Therefore, Nux decided to focus on what was important.
He waved his hand again, and this time, Sharnoth appeared in front of him.
After Nux devoured Zarveth, he became a part of his Universe, and Sharnoth was no exception.
Their bodies reformed in Nux’s Universe with no connections to their respective worlds or Universes.
The only difference between the two was that unlike Zarveth, who still hadn’t regained his consciousness because Nux willed it so, Sharnoth was awake and she...
She had absolutely no idea what was happening.
She called out, confused.
"You all are here as well..."
She muttered, staring at Nux’s wives.
"I-It is nice to meet you..."
She greeted politely.
Nux had helped her a lot; she couldn’t be disrespectful to his wives.
After all, she knew how much he cherished them.
The women blinked in surprise.
While they were all expecting a greeting...thiswasn’t what they had in their minds.
Sharnoth, however, didn’t seem to notice their surprise.
She looked around.
From the looks of it, this seemed like Outer Space; at the same time, it felt... different.
There were a few things she couldn’t recognize, things she had never heard of in her entire life.
"Nux... where is this place?"
She questioned with an uncertain look on her face.
Soon, however, without listening to the answer, the frown on her face deepened as she stared at her own hands,
"And... why do I feel... different?"
She muttered, confused.
She inspected her body, staring at her arms and legs.
Physically, her appearance was still the same.
No, actually, something was different—the crack on her face was no longer there.
Yes, her body was reformed completely.
The skin she had shed was now back.
But that was it—
Her physical appearance may not have changed too much, but everything else...
It was completely different.
She still had complete Body of Chaos, making her entire body nothing but an Entity of Chaos.
She was now the Physical Manifestation of Chaos.
The amount of energy inside her body did not matter.
She could now connect with the Chaos Energy around her and use it without any limits whatsoever.
Yes, she had now become an entity with an endless amount of energy—a monster through and through.
And Sharnoth could feel that.
She could feel how much her body had changed; she could feel just how much stronger she had become.
She just... could not understand how this happened.
"So... does it mean you no longer wish to play with me?"
As the confused Sharnoth tried to understand how all this happened, she suddenly heard a strange question.
"What?
Play...?"
She tilted her head, now even more confused.
"So you don’t remember, huh..."
Nux muttered in a low voice.
His wives finally realized it as well.
No wonder current Sharnoth was acting so differently.
Honestly, they were expecting the woman to instantly jump at them and start ’playing’.
Honestly, Astaria and Vyriana were actually looking forward to it.
They knew Sharnoth was much stronger than them, but they still wanted to ’play’ with her.
They wanted to defeat her, even if it took hundreds of thousands of years.
Of course, the fact that they couldn’t die inside Nux’s Universe gave them even more confidence to go all out.
For now, however, the two warriors could only feel disappointed.
They stared at each other and sighed.
The rest of the women shook their heads when they saw how the two were acting.
They were indeed helpless.
As for Sharnoth...
"I don’t remember...?"
She frowned.
"What do you mean...?
I remember I was fighting that Supreme..."
Suddenly, Sharnoth’s expression changed.
"Nux!
What happened to him!?
And are you alright!?
The Eternal from Supreme World of Darkness chased after you!
Where is he now!?
Is he still after you!?
Are you alri—"
"Calm down."
Nux spoke, his voice heavier than before.
His words seemed to have a much stronger effect on Sharnoth than she expected.
For an instant, all her questions were flushed out of her mind.
And finally,
"Zarveth is dead."
Nux informed.
"I killed him."
Sharnoth blinked.
"Yes, I broke through."
"What...?"
"I broke through."
Nux repeated.
"So you are now..."
"A Transcendent."
Nux answered honestly, and Sharnoth... she had no clue how Nux being a Transcendent could possibly be related to him killing Zarveth, an Eternal.
Yes, he was strong, much stronger than any normal cultivator she had met.
The tricks he used were creative enough for even Eternals to fall for his words, but...
The enemy was an Eternal, that too, from one of the Four Strongest Worlds.
There was no way a Transcendent could defeat someone as strong as Zarveth.
Just... what happened...
Sharnoth could not understand.
She also didn’t understand why she couldn’t recall her battle with Zarveth.
All she knew was that she challenged him, they exchanged some blows, and after that, it was all a blank—almost as if someone took over her.
Suddenly, Sharnoth’s expression changed.
In an instant, she suspectedhim.
"Didheappear...?"
She questioned with a grim look on her face.
Of course, she still had doubts.
First, Zylarith could only take control over her body for less than a second, and even then, the last time he did it, she remembered everything he did.
Her mind did not blank out.
Or...
Did something else happen...?
Did he find a way to take over her body for a longer period of time in a way that she won’t remember anything after it?
The instant that thought appeared in her head, her eyes widened in fright,
"Nux, move away from me!
It isn’t safe!"
She warned Nux.
The last thing she wanted was for that man to take control over her body and get to Nux through her.
This was also the reason she only used call artifacts to contact Nux and never once appeared in front of him.

Even when they attacked Zarveth, they only did it after Zarveth changed the Space Laws, making it difficult for anyone to teleport next to them, and before that, Sharnoth had constantly used her domain to make sure Zarveth wasn’t around her and didn’t know anything they were planning.
They were beingthatcareful, and Sharnoth didn’t want all of it to go to waste because of one mistake.
But—
"He didn’t appear, at least not now."
Nux shook his head, trying to calm her down.
"And even if he does appear, it won’t be here."
"What does that mean...?
Where are we?"
Sharnoth questioned and—
"My Universe."
"Your... what...?"
Sharnoth blinked.
She was one hundred percent sure she heard him wrong.
At her innocent reaction, the women smiled.
Nux too, took a deep breath.
It was finally time to reveal everything so they could get on the same page.
"This place is..."
The explanation began.
The more Sharnoth heard, the more ridiculous expressions appeared on her face.
Nux had to constantly prove his words to assure her that he wasn’t trying to fool her.
And after about an hour of constant back and forth, Sharnoth decided to believe him—barely.
She still had doubts, quite a few of them actually, but for now, she decided to put blind faith in Nux.
After all, she had something much more important to worry about—
"Why do I not remember my battle with Zarveth?"
She questioned and—
"Because it wasn’t you who fought him."
Nux answered directly.
"What...?"
Sharnoth’s expression changed, and this time, Nux’s expression became a little difficult as well.
"This is just my theory, but honestly, I am pretty sure that is the case."
"What does that mean?"
"The one who fought Zarveth was your True Self—no, calling her your True Self won’t be correct anymore..."
Nux frowned as well, thinking of a way to explain this to Sharnoth and his wives, and soon, the right words came to his mind,
"Yes!
Your other self!
The one who defeated Zarveth was your other self!"
Nux answered proudly, completely believing that his words made perfect sense, but...

chapters.title: Chapter 2117: Would she have a second body as well?
paragraphs: "Yes! Your other self!
The one who fought with Zarveth was your other self!"
Nux answered proudly, as if his words made perfect sense to everyone present here but—
Sharnoth blinked. Now she was even more confused. Not just her, the other women were confused as well, especially Lane.
"Her other self...?"
She muttered, pointing at Shadow, who no longer looked like her other self at all. Nux turned towards Lane, knowing exactly what she was thinking, and shook his head—
"No, this isn’t the same case as yours.
It is much simpler."
"Simpler...?"
Lane muttered softly.
"Mhm."
Nux nodded.
"There have been similar cases in the past, quite a few actually. It is usually known as split personality."
"Split Personality?"
"Mhm, two personalities sharing the same body."
Nux nodded. He then turned towards Sharnoth and—
"In your case, your current personality is much stronger."
"Are you saying... there is another being living inside me...?"
Sharnoth tilted her head in confusion.
"Well, theoretically... you are the one living in her body."
Nux corrected casually and Sharnoth...
"What...?"
She felt like her world was falling apart. Nux then looked into her eyes and—
"Answer honestly, how much of your past do you truly remember?"
"My past...?"
"Your life back in Nocthys, then your time in Aurendor, and the time after Zylarith—how much do you remember?"
Nux asked in more detail.
"Do you remember your mother’s face? Your father’s face? The subordinates who worked for your family? The traitors who turned to the enemy the moment your father fell? Do you remember everything?"
"I... remember my mother’s face..."
Sharnoth answered, her voice, however, was oddly low.
"Do you?"
Nux narrowed his eyes.
"Can you draw her for me?"
"...I do not remember it that accurately."
"What about your father?"
Nux questioned and Sharnoth slowly shook her head.
She did not remember.

And Nux did not even bother asking about the subordinates. Sharnoth was quite close to her father and mother. If she didn’t even remember their faces, then the subordinates were obviously out of the question.
The rest of the women stared at Sharnoth, a little taken aback, and Sharnoth felt compelled to explain herself.
"All of that was more than a hundred thousand years ago. It is obvious I won’t remember everything in detail!"
However, instead of answering her question, Nux waved his hand. The Energy of Genesis gathered, forming a clone of a being from his memories—
"What about him? Do you remember him?"
He questioned, staring at Sharnoth, and her expression turned grim.
"He raped my mother thirteen times."
The answer came automatically. It surprised even her. After all, this happened a hundred thousand years ago as well...
To think she remembered this face and everything he did as if the memory was fresh in her head—
It... it made no sense, especially when she couldn’t even picture her mother, the one who was suffering through everything this man did.
"What about the time you spent with Zylarith? How much of that do you remember?"
Nux asked another question, and this time, Sharnoth turned silent. She had never thought about it before since everything felt so natural, but now...
It didn’t.
Did Zylarith do something to her?
She wondered in her head.
"Answer the question, Sharnoth."
And as if knowing her mind was distracted, Nux spoke up, pulling her out of her reverie.
"I... I remember the time when I acted as a mercenary and gathered allies, later taking over Khaemorr and everything after that..."

Sharnoth answered after giving it a thought. It was quite strange. Her memory before this time was so blurry that, other than a small overview of what she actually did, she did not remember anything at all. Her mind could not recall even a single beast out of the hundreds of thousands she had killed.
And surprisingly enough, everything changed after she became a mercenary and started gathering allies. From here on out, she remembered every detail, every face she met, everything she did—clearly.

It was almost as if... someone had messed up her memories before that time. Other than everything that happened in Aurendor, she did not remember most of the things or had a very blurry memory of what she did.
"Makes sense."
Nux nodded to himself. The more he heard her talk, the more assured he grew. Sharnoth and the rest of the women stared at Nux, waiting for an explanation, and he began.
"Sharnoth was born with Darkness Element. That element was then forcibly taken from her, and her body was changed into something capable of handling a completely different form of Energy.
All of this doesn’t come without a cost, and this is especially true for Energy as strong as Chaos."
"So her true self..."
Lane muttered, slowly understanding what happened, and Nux nodded at her words as he turned towards Sharnoth—
"The Energy of Chaos affected your mind. It made you more... chaotic. You started loving chaos—everything that caused more chaos—you started loving them.
Thus, your love for battle was born.
The more difficult the battle, the more you loved it, and the stronger you became. There were even times where you defeated beasts you shouldn’t be able to defeat at all.

Your progress became scarily fast, and seeing this progress, Zylarith didn’t stop you either. He allowed you to do whatever you wanted, so your crazy self went all out, sometimes even challenging beasts with higher cultivation than yours and returning completely battered up.
If it weren’t for Zylarith constantly following you, you would have died thousands of times because you participated in battles you couldn’t win.
That was how reckless you were."
"That... doesn’t sound like me."
Sharnoth answered in a low voice.
"Because it is notyou."
Nux replied, and Sharnoth stared at him, waiting for him to explain.

"Surprised by your progress, Zylarith allowed you to go all out. However, he also knew this couldn’t continue. He could help you here in a Dead World where no one could see the two of you, but once you returned to the Universe and revealed your existence—
It wouldn’t be the same.
Because of Zylarith’s condition, he couldn’t appear and protect you as often as he normally does.

He had to suppress your nature, and the way to do that was simple—as much as you loved battles, what truly drove you forward was your thirst for revenge, and he told you that unless you suppress your true nature and become a calm, level-headed being capable of making quick and correct decisions in any situation, you wouldn’t be able to get your revenge.
And those words changed you."
Sharnoth narrowed her eyes. Again, she did not recall this conversation at all. However, Nux, who had seen her memories, knew everything in detail—

"You started suppressing your true self. Instead of challenging yourself, you began targeting opponents you could defeat. You ’killed’ your love for battle, and you did it for so long that you ’killed’ yourself and were turned into... someone else."
"Someone else..."
Sharnoth muttered those words.
She knew who this ’someone else’ was.
A calm, level-headed being who tries to make quick and correct decisions in most situations. A being who chooses her opponent wisely and only acts when she is sure of her victory—
It washer.
Thecurrenther.
"So I... took over the real me’s body..."
Sharnoth muttered in a weak voice.
"Well, it was something therealyou chose to do.
As I said, calling her therealyou or yourtrueself is incorrect.
She is your other self—a self who decided to hide herself for both of your revenge."

Nux explained. Sharnoth nodded at his words and passed a small, forced smile. She couldn’t just ignore everything she had heard. Thinking about how her body wasn’t exactly hers... she didn’t know how to feel about it.
"Also—"
Suddenly, Nux called out.
"You didn’t exactly ’take over’ your other self. She isn’t gone. She is still here."
Those words attracted Sharnoth’s attention as she quickly recalled where this all began—
"So the one who fought Zarveth..."
"Mhm, that was your other self. And trust me when I say this—she was indeed a monster through and through.
I saw Zarveth’s memories, specifically of his battle with you, and I felt his emotions clearly.
He was scared.
One of the strongest Eternals in all of the Universe was scared of you."
"He was scared of my other self."
Sharnoth clarified.
"That is you. You just... do not have a normal relationship with her."
Sharnoth didn’t know what to say about it.
"So... how does it work?"
Suddenly, Amaya asked a question.
"How do she and her other self switch? They aren’t present all the time, right? She cannot talk to her other self. Or would she be able to do that in the future?
Would she have a second body as well?"
This was what the Devourer was worried about the most.

She already knew Sharnoth was going to join them whether she liked it or not—it was all set in stone. She wanted to know if they would need to pointlessly add another one into the mix just like they did before.
The woman stared at Lane and Shadow and then—
"Tsk."
She snorted before turning towards Nux, waiting for an answer, and Nux just laughed.
He could literally look into her eyes and tell what she was thinking—it was that apparent.
His Devourer was indeed adorable.
"No, Sharnoth won’t have two bodies.
She would need to share the one she has with her other self.
So stop eyeing Lane and Shadow like that."
"Good."
The Devourer nodded.

chapters.title: Chapter 2118: Make sure you repay me well.
paragraphs: "No, Sharnoth won’t have two bodies,
She would need to share the one she has with her other self.
So stop eyeing Lane and Shadow like that."
Nux explained with a soft chuckle, knowing exactly what his devourer was thinking. Amaya stared at him for a moment and then—
"Good."
She nodded, satisfied.
"...two bodies?"
And Sharnoth tilted her head in confusion.
"We actually had a case similar to yours before."
Skyla quickly walked towards her new sister with a light smile on her face as she then pointed at Lane and Shadow.
"The two of them faced the same issue as me?"
Sharnoth raised her eyebrow, a little taken aback.
"No, only she did."
Skyla shook her head, pointing at Lane.
Lane then shrugged and—
"This one came out of me."
The Heir of Chaos blinked in confusion and—
"She is mysecond personality."
Lane answered as she stared at Shadow, who picked up her left leg, leaned a little, and showed a ’V’ sign with her fingers as she winked at Sharnoth.
"Nice to meet you, ’muh lady."
Sharnoth did not know how to react to that greeting. The impression she had of Shadow when she saw her appearance wasn’t... this.
She was also having a hard time believing that she was someone’s... second personality.
’So she is like me...’
Sharnoth muttered, and seeing how Shadow was now resting her chin on Lane’s shoulder teary-eyed because ’she ignored her’—
’So her situation is the same as me...’
She quickly changed her sentence.
"As I said, Lane and Shadow’s case is different."
Suddenly, Nux shook his head, staring at his two girls.
"Their case is more... confusing.
While there are still cases of two personalities inside one body conversing with each other, and even betting or making conditions as to who would be in control of the body at what time,
The two personalities cannot form separate Laws.
Not to mention that in Lane’s case, Shadow never had control over her body, she always remained in her Lane’s shadow.
I still haven’t seen or heard of a similar case."
Nux muttered.
"Right."
The rest of the women nodded as well, they still remembered just how strange it felt when Shadow got a body of her own and started conversing with them like a separate entity.
"Wait."
Suddenly, as if she thought of something, Skyla called out.
"Shouldn’t Sister Shadow have a new name? We have been calling her Shadow all this while, but she is much more than Sister Lane’s shadow now, isn’t she?"
She suggested.
Nux looked at Shadow too, wanting her to express her opinion. He obviously already knew it because he had already brought this topic up when the two of them were together.
Shadow momentarily blinked as all attention fell on her. She stopped crying and stood straight, then she glanced at Lane, who was staring at her, waiting for her answer.
And then—
"I wish to keep my name."
She answered with a light smile on her face as she then glanced at Lane.
"My name is what keeps me connected to my cute Lane~"
The woman then jumped on the Shadow Demon, hugging her from behind—
"Righttttt~~"

She laughed, tickling Lane’s body even though it clearly wasn’t working. Lane, too, had a deadpan look on her face; she resembled a tired mother who had given up on stopping her overly excited child and had allowed her to do whatever she wanted.
From the looks of it, she currently wanted nothing but some time away from this ’thing’.

Of course, Sharnoth was the only one who saw her annoyance. As for those who knew Lane better, they all could see the very light, almost imperceptible smile that had crept up on her face when she heard those words.
"Hehe~"
Shadow laughed, rubbing her face on Lane’s back and Lane just sighed.
Nux laughed at the situation.

Yes, the two were having a competition of their own and once again, Lane just stood there in the middle in silence. She had already given in to her fate.
She just wanted Nux to get over with the fight so she could return to his shadow again. Conversing with Nux from in there was indeed the second-best feeling in the Universe.
"S-So... where has Nux gone to...? If it isn’t too much to talk to me..."
Sharnoth tried initiating the conversation in an awkward manner, not staring at anyone in particular.
The women quickly sensed her awkwardness and—
"He is taking care of Neremoth, he didn’t finish him because he was worried about you."
Felberta answered with a light smile on her face, taking her role as the first wife and making her new sister comfortable.
Her words, however, did not do that.
"He... he is fighting Neremoth? The Eternal from the Supreme World of Darkness? Shouldn’t I help him??"
She questioned as she prepared for battle.
"Ah, don’t worry about it. It won’t take long, he defeated Zarveth, did you forget?"
Felberta smiled lightly and Sharnoth’s expression changed.
"Right..."
She nodded, not knowing what to do. She thought she could leave the awkward environment and go battle.
"Actually, do you wish to see the battle between Nux and Zarveth? We recorded it."
Felberta suggested. Her words instantly attracted Sharnoth’s attention.
"You have it recorded?"
"We do, we record most of the things in case we are bored.
Do you wish to see it?"
"I do."
Sharnoth nodded.
"Fair warning though, you will appear in that fight, quite a lot."
"Me as in..."
"Mhm, your other self."
Felberta nodded with a light chuckle.
"It is okay...
I wish to see my other self as well..."
Sharnoth answered. She had already accepted the fact that she now had a second self living inside her body. If she had come this far, she might as well find out how her other self acts like, no?
"Fufufu~
I am sure you will enjoy it."

For some reason, she felt like her smile had another meaning behind it.

OI! FIGHT HIM PROPERLY!!
WHAT ARE YOU ACTING LIKE A FOOL FOR!?]
Sharnoth couldn’t believe what she was seeing.

chapters.title: Chapter 2119: Shall we begin now?
paragraphs: "Just what is this place..."
Neremoth growled. His voice couldn’t be more frustrated as he looked around. Nothing was clearly visible. As far as his eyes went, he could only see darkness.
Normally, this environment was where he was at his strongest, when he was the most comfortable.
But here...
Something felt different.
The darkness around him was familiar, but at the same time... it was unfamiliar.

Neremoth stood at its center, his eyes staring at the storm of swirling shadows around him. It was strange. These shadows, or whatever they were, came crashing into his body like waves, but it didn’t have any effect.
Almost as if this place did not follow the Laws he was familiar with.
It was... eerie.
And when a being from the Supreme World of Darkness thought this... then it meant something.
After all, these beings represented the word eerie back in the Main Universe. They saw and relished things that most people’s stomachs wouldn’t be able to digest.
This place, however, was dangerous.
Neremoth realized it as well. Actually, he had been trying to escape this cursed place for what felt like days, maybe even weeks.
Yes, time here didn’t flow normally.
There were no stars, no anchor points, no sense of direction.
Only him... and this strange place that refused to let him go.
His hand stretched forward, cutting through a tear he had carved in space but—
Nothing happened.
He tried again, forming a gateway with his core energy, using the raw essence of despair to anchor his escape.
It worked—for a moment.
Then the tear closed on its own, folding into a spiral and twisting itself into a mirror.
That same mirror reflected his failure right back at him, almost as if the very place was trying to mock him.
"LET ME LEAVE!!"
Suddenly, Neremoth screamed at the top of his lungs.
A scream that would have made most beings in the Universe tremble in fear, but here—it felt different.
More than fear, one could feel Neremoth’s desperation.
"I AM DARKNESS, DAMMIT!"
He shouted again, releasing more energy, trying to overwhelm this place with his energy. He raised his arms, black claws of energy stretching into the distance, warping space as they moved.
But the warped space repaired itself on its own. Neremoth didn’t even get the chance to sense the space the tear was opened to, let alone move into the warp himself.
With another failed attempt, he tried reshaping his form—became smoke, then shadow, then formless hunger.
He did everything he could but...
Still nothing.
Every path he created crumbled under him.
Every exit unraveled the moment he reached it.
Worse still—sometimes it felt like the very Universe itself was laughing at him.
Once, he’d found a portal.
He’d reached into it with everything he had. He saw stars beyond it—real stars.
He even touched the edge of something familiar.
Then... a single blink later... the stars turned to eyes. Dozens of them, watching him.
He even heard a conversation between people he did not know.
’That’s him?’
’Yeah.’
’And you are keeping him here?’
’It is not very difficult. He is quite dumb.’
’Can he listen to us? He seems to be reacting to our words.’
’Hmm? Oh wait—’
And just like that, the conversation ended, the eyes vanished, and the portal closed like it was never there.
"LET ME LEAVE OR THIS WILL NOT END WELL!!"
He threatened, releasing more energy, as if trying to overwhelm whoever it was doing all this to him.
But he didn’t receive any answers.
No matter how many threats or curses he hurled, there was no answer, almost as if those people were no longer interested in him.
It was... humiliating.
After cursing, threatening, and shouting for he didn’t know how long, Neremoth stood completely still.
Breathing heavily, his shoulders rose and fell and his hands shook at his sides. He wasn’t tired—he was... frustrated.
Every time he got close to understanding this place, it changed.
Every rule bent the moment he learned it.
Every crack healed just before he could slip through.
It was almost as if someone was purposefully making sure he didn’t leave.
And whoever it was... he was watching him.
The more he thought about it, the angrier he got.
"Enough games..."
He spoke in a low, hoarse, and cold voice as he clenched his fists, more and more darkness dripping from his hands like ink.
"Show yourself, you miserable little insect..."
He threatened again.
But once again.
Nothing answered.
"I SAID SHOW YOURSELF, YOU BASTARD!!
FACE ME IF YOU DARE!"
He screamed again, his words reverberated throughout the space and then—
"Holy fuck, you are angry."
He suddenly heard a voice.
For an instant, Neremoth froze. He had gotten so used to the silence that his mind couldn’t react to an answer.
He slowly turned his head and there—
His eyes fell onhim.
The Anomaly.
Standing calmly, hands in his coat, hovering in the air with a smile on his face.
"Chill dude, it has only been a few hours. Stop acting like you have been trapped for centuries. Aren’t you an Eternal? Shouldn’t your mentality be much stronger than normal people? Why wou—"
Before Nux could even complete his lecture, Neremoth launched himself towards him, intending to capture him alive and crush every part of his body.
An act that obviously did not work.
Nux willed himself away from Neremoth and...
Well, the attack failed.
This, however, did not calm Neremoth. He glared at the Anomaly, his crimson eyes shining with absolute hatred.
"You... you did this,"
He said, voice trembling with anger.
"You made this... this maze... this lie of a Universe!"
"It is not a lie, trust me."
Nux nodded in an assuring manner.
Neremoth’s anger rose even further. It almost seemed like he was going to explode. Nux shook his head in disappointment.
Then,
"Anyways,
Shall we begin now?"
Nux asked, as he stretched his body.
"Begin what?" Neremoth growled.
Nux’s smile widened just a little and—
"Your end."
He answered.

chapters.title: Chapter 2120: You fought well.
paragraphs: "Begin what?"
Neremoth growled.
Nux’s smile widened just a little and—
"Your end."
He answered.
"I have things to do, you see."
Neremoth’s crimson eyes glared at Nux as the space between them vanished. The Darkness Eternal moved like a shadow.
He was fast, silent, brutal. His clawed hand sliced through layers of barriers Nux created for fun, aiming for his chest.
Nux dodged, letting the claws pass just beside his cheek.
"Nice."
Nux praised.
"You’re fast."
Neremoth didn’t speak.
He just attacked again.
His body exploded into tendrils of pure darkness, spinning, twisting, closing in from all sides. Each tendril left behind a scar of dead space—making sure Nux wouldn’t be able to teleport there.
Nux spun in the air, avoiding all the tendrils.
Yes, he was in his Universe, yes, he was pretty much immortal here, but this didn’t mean Neremoth wasn’t a threat.
Unlike Zarveth, who mostly relied on his relics, Neremoth was strong on his own, and because Nux hadn’t devoured him yet, he didn’t have complete control over him like he had with Zarveth.

Right now, Neremoth was like an external entity visiting his Universe. It was similar to how his wives appeared in the Main Universe—even though they weren’t at their strongest, they still weren’t weak.
Neremoth too wasn’t weak; his attacks could still prove to be lethal.
Nux had to be careful.
Of course, his surroundings helped him too.
But Neremoth did not stop and continued unleashing one attack after the other, as if he was prepared to kill this bastard today.
It was no longer about personal gain from ’getting his hands on the Anomaly’, he just needed to take his anger out on this bastard.
"You are dead."
Neremoth growled.
And Nux...
He clapped his hands, as if praising Neremoth’s efforts.
Suddenly, an asteroid that formed out of nowhere rose like a wave, slamming into Neremoth, but the Eternal of Darkness burst through it, his cloak spreading like wings.
Oblivion Ray.
A thick beam of black light shot from his palm. Everything it touched began to fade.
Nux flew around it, the edge of the beam barely brushing his coat, which crumbled for a second before being remade by his will.
"Oi Oi,"
Nux called out.
"Not the coat, I actually like this one."
Neremoth growled, his voice echoing in every direction as he activated another one of his abilities.
Eclipse Spiral.
Dozens of black tendrils burst from his chest, homing in on Nux. They spun in circles, warping space, tearing through asteroids Nux had created just moments ago.
Nux caught one of the tendrils and crushed it.
He pointed a finger at the next one, and it vanished before it reached him.
He was being careful, yes, but it was clear he wasn’t actually trying very hard.
But Neremoth refused to stop.
Again and again, he attacked.
Dreadwake Pulse.
Nullfang.
Hollow Rebirth.
He turned into smoke, reappeared behind Nux, struck from below, from above, even from within the shadows of Darkness itself.
Nux kept up, but during the battle, his coat was ripped two times now—it was quite bad.
"I told you,
Not the coat!"
He complained as he stopped dodging for a moment.
Then—
Then punched forward.
And—
BOOOOOOM
His fist hit Neremoth in the stomach, sending him flying backward across the sky like a comet. The very space around crumbled, unable to bear the force of Nux releasing his full strength.
If it was any other being than Neremoth, his body would have disappeared into oblivion, but...
Nux could sense Neremoth’s presence.
"Let’s not drag this out,"
Nux spoke, floating calmly as he dusted off his sleeve and stared at where Neremoth was.
"You can’t kill me,"
Neremoth answered in a calm voice. Using Hollow Rebirth, his torn body had once again recovered back to its optimal state.
"You think this strange world gives you strength.
ButIam darkness itself.
I do no—"
"Yes, yes.
Darkness, blah blah blah.
As I said, let’s not drag this out."
Nux interrupted and then, he moved forward, attacking again.

Ten.
Then twenty.
Then thirty.
The battle raged across Nux’s Universe.
Nux used his reality control to bend laws, change gravity, flip time. He honestly experimented quite a lot—it was like he was using Neremoth as a practice dummy.
He was throwing everything he could at him, and impressively, Neremoth was taking it all. The attacks he could crush, he crushed. Those he could avoid, he avoided. As for those that crushed him...
He simply recovered and continued fighting again.
No matter how much Nux pushed, he kept coming.
But...
Neremoth realized it as well.
His Endless Energy...
It was fading away.
Hollow Rebirth used his Life Force as a cost. Theoretically, as an Eternal, he was an immortal with endless Life Force.
However, this did not mean he could use his Life Force however much he wanted...
There was a limit to abuse.
The very Universe made it that way.
One’s Life Force wasn’t an infinite resource. Yes, an Eternal had infinite Life Force but... nothing in this Universe was truly ’infinite’.
Everything came with a cost.
And Life Force...
It came at the cost of one’s Soul.

When one uses Life Force, his very Soul burns itself to supply that energy. Of course, the first few uses don’t make a difference—a being’s Soul was the purest entity in the Universe, something the Universe cherished quite a lot.
Even a small amount of Soul Energy could fill even an Eternal’s Energy reserves, but...
What if...
One was forced to use this energy again and again and then again.
Ten times?
A hundred times?
A thousand times?
Or...
A million times?
No matter how strong a Soul was—in the end, even it had its limits.

As Neremoth continued to use Hollow Rebirth to recover, every time he was reborn... he became slower and weaker. Even his very instincts and mind began to slow down—so much that even he himself didn’t seem to realize it.
And by the time he did—
Nux was already grabbing him by his neck, lifting him in the air and he...
He had absolutely no energy to move or resist him.
"You fought well."
Nux praised.
"But I guess you have no use for me now that you have spent all your Soul.
Oh well,
I guess I’ll have to make do with Zarveth alone."
Nux shook his head and then, he devoured Neremoth, absorbing everything he once stood for.
The battle finally ended.

chapters.title: Chapter 2121: New Slav—Subordinates.
paragraphs: "Still nothing, huh..."
Nux muttered with a somewhat disappointed sigh as he stared at two unconscious beings hovering in front of him.
They were Neremoth and Zarveth.
Both of them were unconscious because Nux willed it so. Right now, Nux was reading their memories to figure something out.
From his sigh, however, it was clear that things didn’t go his way.
It all began after he defeated Neremoth and devoured him. He had already spent 30 minutes fighting him, so he thought he might as well read his memories while he was at it.

He had checked that Sharnoth and his wives were getting along well. Yes, those women were teasing Sharnoth to the point the poor woman had no choice but to cover her face with her hands, constantly muttering, "That’s not me," but honestly, Nux was already used to this sight by now.
Those women were bona fide bullies. They bullied every single woman they met. What’s worse?
When that woman joined their group, she became an active bully as well.
Sometimes, Nux actually wondered whose influence made things turn out this way, but soon, he intelligently stopped wondering about it.
There was no point in monitoring a woman’s mind—even if he had all the information in the Universe, he knew he still would not understand it.

In the end, he just shook his head and sighed. Yes, Sharnoth was being bullied, but this also meant that she was accepted by the others. Nux could already see her getting along with the rest of his wives, and the thought made him smile.
For now, however, he focused on what was in front of him. He closed his eyes and started reading Neremoth’s memories.
Now that he had no one to save or a Universe to complete, his mind was free, so the entire process only took a minute. But after that long minute, Nux’s face turned solemn as he noticed something.
Neremoth...
In all his life, he had never met Darkness Infinity even once.

Which was quite surprising if one thought about it. Neremoth was one of the strongest beings in the Supreme World of Darkness—an Eternal. The number of beings he was actually wary of, other than the Infinities, could be counted on one hand.
He was that strong, and he had lived for hundreds of thousands of years, and yet...
He still hadn’t seen the Darkness Infinity.
Yes, he received their orders. He, of course, fulfilled the said order and reported it, but never once did he get to see them.

Every time the Darkness Infinity wanted something, Neremoth would ’know’ on his own and act on it. Once he was done, he would compile a report and leave it wherever he completed it, and in a few days, the said report would disappear.
Everything just... happened on its own.

There were no messengers, no building where he was supposed to report to—nothing. Even back when he was a child and was being trained together with others, the Infinity never came personally. They were taught by others.
Honestly, Neremoth did not know a single thing about Infinity. Heck, he didn’t even know his name. He just knew one thing—
That Lord Infinity was strong, and he was supposed to respect and fear him.

And this feeling inside him was so strong that it was quite surprising. It made Nux wonder what gave Neremoth the courage to betray the Infinity he respected and feared so much and join Zarveth to come after him.

When he looked at it, it seemed like he only did it because he was bored. The reasoning was something similar along the lines of wanting to do something great. The only difference was, unlike Zarveth, who did it because of his endless thirst for knowledge, Neremoth just craved power.
Yes, he respected and feared the Infinity, but his greed for power was stronger. He wanted to devour the Anomaly and get stronger than the Infinities and make them grovel under his feet.
Also, the fact that the Anomaly was a mere Primordial who was still wet behind his ears motivated him as well.
If a Primordial Anomaly caused so much destruction throughout the Universe, he wanted to see what he could do as the Anomaly.

It was quite strange actually. Nux noticed the connection between a few of Neremoth’s memories was weak. With all these doubts in his mind, he began reading Zarveth’s memories. He had only read the part where he fought Sharnoth, but now, he was going through his entire life, and the more he read it, the stronger his doubts got—
By the end—
He understood.
It wasn’t that these beings didn’t know anything about the Infinities or had never seen them, it was just that...
Everything they did, their memories were manipulated, and they were made to forget about it without them realizing it.
They didn’t just ’know’ what their respected Infinity wanted from them—they were told that, and the order was instilled into them. This memory disappeared.
Even Zarveth, who had witnessed the Supreme Battle between the Five Supreme Worlds with his own eyes, was no exception.
In that battle, he remembered everything about Zylarith and how he faced the four Infinities, but the Infinities, in his mind—they were just different ’lights.’
Black.
Golden.
White.
Grey.
That was all he remembered. Their faces, their abilities—he didn’t know anything despite being one of the oldest beings in the Universe.
"They are quite cowardly for ones who claim themselves to be the strongest beings in the Universe,"
Nux commented, somewhat disappointed.
Honestly, half the reason he was excited about defeating the beings from the Supreme World was that he would finally get to uncover just how strong his enemies were.
But it seemed like his enemies were quite cautious.
’Who are they so wary of?’
Nux wondered in his mind.
Is there an enemy he does not know about?
Or were they... just wary of each other?

That was one possibility. But if Nux wasn’t wrong, then they should know each other’s strengths and weaknesses by heart now. After all, they had lived for a long, long time. They even fought together when they fought Zylarith.
What could they possibly be hiding from each other?
Or... was he just following the wrong line of thought all this while?
All these questions bothered Nux. Reading the two’s memories only made him more confused. For now, however, he shook his head and shrugged.
There was no point in thinking about it right now.
Even though he hadn’t gained information on the enemy, he had still gained quite a lot in this battle.

He had finally managed to complete his Universe. He got his hands on strong Laws. He even got his hands on Supreme-Level Bloodlines. However, the Supreme Bloodlines weren’t as big of a deal as he thought they would be.
Or more accurately—he couldn’t use them to their fullest potential.

Essentially, a bloodline is connected to a World, which in turn is dependent on the Universe. The Supreme Worlds, that are the closest to the Universe, have the strongest bloodlines—the Supreme Bloodlines.
But when Nux devoured the Supreme Borns and got their bloodlines, the connection these bloodlines had with their worlds broke.

Now usually, this wasn’t a problem when Nux got bloodlines of High-Level or weaker-level Worlds. However, his current Universe, which had only just become a complete Universe a while ago, was nowhere near strong enough to replicate the strength of the Main Universe’s strongest bloodlines.
Did this mean Nux’s current bloodline was weaker than the Supreme Borns’?
There was no answer to this question.
Bloodlines usually dictated one’s potential and gave them abilities. Supreme Bloodlines were obviously strong, but—bloodlines had long stopped mattering to Nux.
It was foolish to link his potential with his bloodline. He was a Universe—an entity far more complex than any living being.

Only his wives and other beings connected to his Universe would care about matters regarding bloodlines, and in their case, yes, their bloodlines were weaker than the Supreme Borns’, but as Nux’s Universe grows, that would change.
More than the bloodlines, abilities, energies, and memories he had gained, what made Nux the most excited were the two beings in front of him.
Zarveth and Neremoth—few of the strongest beings in the Universe—were now in his hands. It obviously went without question what their fate was going to be.
He was going to manipulate their memories, turning them into two of his strongest subordinates.
And the best part?

Because they were now connected to him and his Absolute Law of Inseparable Together, they couldn’t die either—not unless they were trapped inside domains that are stronger than theirs, which obviously would not happen easily since the only beings capable of that were Infinities.
Basically, Nux now had ridiculously strong subordinates that could not be truly killed unless they went against leaders of the Supreme Worlds.

Of course, Zarveth and Neremoth were still not at their strongest—Zarveth had lost his Infinity Relics, and most of his relics couldn’t be used since they were somewhat reliant on the Main Universe. He would now need to create new relics that are connected to Nux’s Universe.
Neremoth, on the other hand, had used up too much of his Soul Power. He would need centuries to recover and return to his peak.
’Tsk, I should have killed them faster.’
Nux snorted in his head. For now, however, he just shrugged as he began manipulating their memories and turning them into his loyal puppets.
Of course, while he was at it, he also grabbed the rest of the pupp—Supreme Borns he had devoured before and manipulated their heads before.
Now, he had a little party of Supreme Born Slav—Subordinates.
Ahem. Ahem.

chapters.title: Chapter 2122: So that’s the Anomaly, eh?
paragraphs: RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
The Universe reacted in anger again.

By now, this had become such a common sight that almost no being was surprised by it—even Mortals were no exception. They had heard about the ’God’s anger’ from their ancestors, and experiencing it on their own was nothing new to them.

However, while the rest of the Universe simply thought of it as an everyday occurrence, in Vael’Terros, the world where the Supreme Borns had gathered all the Mercenary Guild Leaders, things were different.
Their reaction to the Universe’s anger was much heavier than others.

Of course, the Universe’s anger didn’t really affect Vael’Terros. With a wave of his hand, the Eternal from the Supreme World of Balance negated all the tremors that could have caused any harm to any being present here.
The problem, however, was the fact that the Universe had reacted when they were waiting for the party they sent to return.
This... felt ominous.
"They still aren’t back."
The Eternal from the Supreme World of Light muttered in a low voice, staring at Balance, who nodded solemnly.
Zarveth, the party of other Supreme Borns, and Neremoth who went after them, had left a few hours ago. Their goal was to investigate the Mercenary Worlds that were destroyed by the Chain Breakers.
The goal was simple. They wanted to find a clue regarding the Chain Breakers—or better yet, meet a member of the said group and bring him here to know more about them.

If it was just the investigation, then with Zarveth’s speed, they should have been back a long time ago. After all, the Chain Breakers had only destroyed fifty-six worlds. There was no way Zarveth would investigate fifty-six Mercenary Worlds for more than a few hours.
Even if the task was tedious, he would have ordered his subordinates to do it while he himself would have returned with a bored look on his face.
That was the type of being he was.
Neremoth too wasn’t an exception. The entire reason he left was because he was bored. Both Light and Balance knew it. If they were still investigating, that being would have returned a long time ago.

After all, investigation was definitely much more boring than whatever was going on here. At the very least, here, he could have rightfully tortured a few mercenaries to death while they begged him for mercy.
It was something Neremoth usually enjoyed.
But...
Since the two of them hadn’t returned, both Light and Balance could tell what was happening.
A fight.
Zarveth, Neremoth, and their party must have encountered an enemy. However, when they tried to contact them, there were no replies—almost as if they didn’t have the time to react.
Which in itself was surprising. After all, both Neremoth and Zarveth were strong—Light and Balance knew it better than everyone present here.
If the enemy was strong enough to keep both of them busy, then the enemy was quite strong as well—
Dealing with such an enemy... the two of them should have already called for reinforcements, yet they did not.
It was something that confused Light and Balance.
Were they... defeated before they could call for reinforcements?

Honestly, if that was the case, then the reinforcements wouldn’t have done anything either. No being other than an Infinity could push Zarveth and Neremoth to such a state. Even if the two of them were facing tens of Supreme Born Eternals, Zarveth alone would have had more than enough time to call for reinforcements.
He had more than a hundred relics specifically made for calling reinforcements before anyone could stop him. As long as he wasn’t instantly killed, he could call reinforcements by his will alone.

Balance questioned in a heavy voice.

Eternity shook his head.
"He got greedy."
He answered.
"Greedy...?"
Light muttered slowly, and suddenly, a screen showing Nux appeared in front of the four entities.

Darkness questioned. He was annoyed that he lost more people than Light and Balance, but since whatever was happening seemed exciting, he didn’t pay much attention to it—for now.

Darkness laughed.

"That’s the Heir of Chaos."

Darkness grinned again.

"She’s different.
She was close to completing the Body of Chaos."
He revealed, and in an instant—
"...What?"
The air in the hall changed.

chapters.title: Chapter 2123: What is his plan?
paragraphs: "She was close to completing the Body of Chaos."
Eternity revealed, and suddenly the air in the hall changed.
"...what?"
Darkness muttered, his voice much lower than before.
"Watch this."
Eternity answered, and suddenly, the scene in front of them changed.
[Come onnnn~~
Why did you stop talking!?
Don’t tell me you are tired already~~
Or are you really that scared~~
You aren’t scared, are you???]
The four Infinities saw Sharnoth laughing at Zarveth as her body released a ridiculous amount of Chaos Energy to overpower him and for an instant—
Heavy silence fell over the place.
After all, every single one of the Infinities could see it.
The Body of Chaos.
Yes, it was still incomplete, but as they continued watching the recording and more and more of that girl’s skin came off, the more complete the body became.
"He really found another monster to succeed him..."
Balance muttered, somewhat taken aback.
Was he scared?
Well, not really.
Yes, the Body of Chaos was strong, but...

What was in front of him was incomplete, not to mention the girl was not the Chaos Progenitor Zylarith. Even if she somehow managed to complete the Body of Chaos, she wouldn’t reach the level that monster had reached.
What did worry him, however, was that this meant Zylarith had succeeded.
And that wasn’t good news.
"Do we know whathisplan is?"
Light questioned. She seemed to be worried about the same thing. Yes, billions of years had passed since they defeated Zylarith, and in all these years, all of them had improved to some extent but—
Zylarith’s existence was still a matter of concern.
The Infinities never liked how someone as dangerous as him was roaming freely. They tried to capture him multiple times, but it did not work.
And now, the man who had been avoiding them all this while was suddenly making a move, revealing what should be his most cherished disciple to them...
This did not make any sense, and it made the Infinities wary.
"We do not."
Eternity shook his head. Soon, however, his tone became solemn and—
"But I do have a theory."

The rest of the Infinities stayed silent, waiting for him to continue. He fast-forwarded the battle between Sharnoth and Zarveth, pointing out every time Sharnoth’s skin was peeled off, and by the end, when Zarveth used the Infinity Relics to defeat her and the Anomaly appeared, he paused and—
"I believe that the Body of Chaos is made of the Energy of Chaos. This is the reason it is able to use all of the Universe’s continuous Chaos without any limits."
"But that shouldn’t be possible."
Balance frowned.
"No body can be made entirely of Energy. Any Energy needs matter to be st—"
He tried to counter, but Eternity once again shifted the screen back, focusing on the area where Sharnoth had no skin.
"That Black Purple glow beneath her skin—it comes from the physical condensation of Chaos."
He answered as suddenly, a purple-black-colored sphere appeared in the middle of the table, a sphere that had the same glow as whatever it was beneath Sharnoth’s skin.
When the Infinities saw that, their expressions changed.
"I have been looking into it for a while and...
Chaos is one of the few energies that can be turned into physical matter, and because of that, it does not require matter."
Eternity explained.

"Of course, just creating this little sphere required quite a bit of effort. Keeping the energy as volatile as Chaos together, bound into a physical form, is nowhere near easy. So making an entire body out of just the Energy of Chaos should be extremely, extremely difficult but..."
"But it is possible."
Balance completed those words in a solemn tone, and once again, Eternity nodded.

"That is what Zylarith did all those years ago. As to how he did it, that I do not understand. He must have had quite a thorough understanding of Chaos—something far beyond what me or any being in the Universe can have."
"Are you saying that she has the same level of understanding as Zylarith?"
Light questioned, her voice clearly expressing her suspicion, and Eternity laughed at her words.
"Of course not."
He shook his head, clearing the misunderstanding.

"That girl is barely a hundred thousand years old. Even Zylarith himself did not have such a deep understanding of Chaos by then, and he was hailed as the strongest being in the history of the Universe.

I can say for certain that that girl is nowhere close to Zylarith’s level. If I had to guess, then Zylarith must have helped her in some way, changing her body’s constitution so her body has an easier time adapting or something along those lines.
He had billions of years to prepare—I am sure someone like him would have found a way."
Eternity answered. He did not hold back his praises when it came to Zylarith.
"So she is just someone Zylarith helped."
Light muttered, somewhat relieved, but...
"That does not reassure me."
Balance spoke. This time, his tone was far more solemn than before.
Darkness nodded at those words.
"That monster would not ’help’ someone without any reason."
He spoke, his tone was quite grim as well.
Light remained silent.
She understood the seriousness of this matter as well.
"What is he planning then?"
She questioned. Once again, the three Infinities turned silent, waiting for Eternity to complete his theory, and after a slight pause, Eternity continued.
"I will say this again—that this is just a theory, and I do not have any way to prove my words."
"Just speak!"
Darkness groaned, annoyed.
"The Body of Chaos is made of Chaos Energy. Energy can only be controlled by the one who has the strongest understanding of that energy.
So...
If worse comes to worst, then once she completes her Body of Chaos...
Zylarith will have absolute control over her body and...
We will not be facing Zylarith’s disciple, but Zylarith himself."
Silence.
Heavy silence fell over the place.
Once again, the Infinities recalled the final battle that lasted years and how difficult it was to take down that monster...
If...
If that monster was indeed back inside a new body...
The Infinities did not even wish to think what would happen then.
Again, yes, billions of years have passed, yes, all of them had gotten stronger than they were before, but...
Wouldn’t Zylarith be the same?
He had the Power over Chaos.

The only Energy in the Universe that grows endlessly together with the Universe itself. While for billions of years, they face each other, keep each other in check, and try to expand their own influence on the Universe to get stronger,
The Chaos, no matter what happens, continues to grow.
So by the end, the more time passes, the stronger it would be.

Zylarith, at his prime, was already a monster who fought four Infinities on his own, then what about the current Zylarith? What if he reached the level he was before—this time, with the amount of Chaos Energy nearly twice as much as before,
Wouldn’t he be... twice as strong...?
It was next to impossible to imagine how absurdly strong that monster was going to be.
But at the same time, Balance couldn’t help but frown—
"Something does not add up."
The rest of the Infinities turned toward him and—
"Let’s say you are right. All along, his plan was to indeed take over one of his disciple’s bodies the moment he or she completes the Body of Chaos, but...
The Body of Chaos was only a part of his strength.
What about the World?"
Again, the Infinities became silent. Balance’s words made sense. Yes, Zylarith was strong, absurdly strong, but... every existence needs a World to support them.
And...
Only Five Worlds in the entirety of the Universe can support an existence as strong as Zylarith.
The Five Supreme Worlds.
Even if Zylarith took over that girl’s body, he wouldn’t be able to break through the Infinity Stage without being connected to a Supreme World.
But...
There are no Supreme Worlds available for that.
There is no way the Zylarith in his current state would even dare to get close to the Four Supreme Worlds, since he knew he would be captured.
The only world left would be the reincarnation of the Chaosveil, but even then, getting connected to that world wouldn’t be easy becausehedefends it.
The being who once protected the Anomaly from all four of them.
The Infinities hadn’t forgotten about him.

They did not know how strong he was, but the very fact that he hadn’t revealed his existence after that incident shows that he is quite cautious—and the last thing he would do would be to trust someone as suspicious as Zylarith.
So...
What was Zylarith’s plan?
Was he going to take over one of the Supreme Worlds?
But that would only be possible if one of the five present Infinities perishes.
But for an Infinity to perish...
Zylarith would need something as big as a Universal War but...
The four Infinities did not see that happening—at least not anytime soon.
"Wait..."
Suddenly, Light called out, her tone much more different than before.

It was next to impossible to imagine how absurdly strong that monster was going to be.
But at the same time, Balance couldn’t help but frown—
"Something does not add up."
The rest of the Infinities turned toward him and—
"Let’s say you are right.
All along, his plan was to indeed take over one of his disciple’s bodies the moment he or she completes the Body of Chaos, but...
The Body of Chaos was only a part of his strength.
What about the World?"
Again, the Infinities became silent.
Balance’s words made sense.
Yes, Zylarith was strong, absurdly strong, but... every existence needs a World to support them.
And...
Only Five Worlds in the entirety of the Universe can support an existence as strong as Zylarith.
The Five Supreme Worlds.
Even if Zylarith took over that girl’s body, he wouldn’t be able to break through the Infinity Stage without being connected to a Supreme World.
But...
There are no Supreme Worlds available for that.
There is no way the Zylarith in his current state would even dare to get close to the Four Supreme Worlds, since he knew he would be captured.
The only world left would be the reincarnation of the Chaosveil, but even then, getting connected to that world wouldn’t be easy becausehedefends it.
The being who once protected the Anomaly from all four of them.
The Infinities hadn’t forgotten about him.

They did not know how strong he was, but the very fact that he hadn’t revealed his existence after that incident shows that he is quite cautious—and the last thing he would do would be to trust someone as suspicious as Zylarith.
So...
What was Zylarith’s plan?
Was he going to take over one of the Supreme Worlds?
But that would only be possible if one of the five present Infinities perishes.
But for an Infinity to perish...
Zylarith would need something as big as a Universal War but...
The four Infinities did not see that happening—at least not anytime soon.
"Wait..."
Suddenly, Light called out, her tone much more different than before.

chapters.title: Chapter 2124: What do we know about him?
paragraphs: "Wait..."
Suddenly, Light called out, her tone much more different than before.
"Why is Zylarith’s disciple together with the Anomaly?"
She questioned with a suspicious voice.
A question that spread another wave of silence amongst the Infinities.
"Is Zylarith related to the Anomaly?
That Fifth Infinity once covered for the Anomaly as well. Is... he perhaps working together with Zylarith as well?"
Light asked another question and this time—
"No Infinity in his right mind would work together with Zylarith."
Darkness quickly shook his head.
Knowing how tricky that monster was, the last thing he wanted was to be associated with him. After all, it was almost impossible to predict what that bastard might do next.
But—
"What makes you sure about that?"
Light questioned again.
"We all know what kind of—"

"He should not know that. He was born long after Zylarith’sdeath. It wouldn’t be difficult for Zylarith to trick him, especially if he encountered Zylarith before becoming an Infinity. Don’t forget, the number of beings Zylarith has fooled isn’t small.
He has destroyed worlds using his trickeries. He definitely can be... quite convincing."
Again, silence fell over the place. None of the Infinities could deny those words.
"Does this mean Zylarith already knows which world is the reincarnation of Chaosveil?"
Balance questioned.
"I wouldn’t be surprised if he does."
Eternity answered.
"He has been looking for it for billions of years while we... all have been busy with our own things."
He spoke carefully.
Once again recalling that the beings next to him weren’t his allies either.
"Of course, all of this could also be a false alarm. Maybe Zylarith is wary of the Fifth Infinity."
"But then why would the Fifth Infinity help the Anomaly?"
"The Anomaly is not Zylarith.

Maybe the Fifth Infinity only wishes to protect the Anomaly. Maybe the two of them are working together and Zylarith is working on his own. Maybe he is using his disciple to get his hands on the Anomaly."

"You think the Fifth Infinity would not understand his plans? That filthy Chaos Energy releasing from her body can be smelled from a long distance. Do you truly think an Infinity would not recognize it?"
"Maybe it is the opposite? Maybe the Fifth Infinity is using the disciple to get his hands on Zylarith.

If you think about it, the Fifth Infinity came after Zylarith. Since the information regarding the Chaosveil and Zylarith had become inaccessible to the rest of the Universe, he obviously wouldn’t know much about them—or even us.
But what if he gets his hands on Zylarith?
If he extracts Zylarith’s memories, he would not only be able to pry upon his secrets, he would also know about us and be able to come up with ways to deal with us."
Balance gave his own theory.
"So you are saying he sees Zylarith as a target?"
Light questioned.
"In his current state, he wouldn’t be wrong to do so.
He is an Infinity. Any being in this Universe except us is a target for him."
Balance muttered.

His thinking was simple. The Fifth Infinity did not truly know who Zylarith was. It wouldn’t be surprising for him to arrogantly believe that he could deal with one who was once called the strongest being in the Universe.
And in all honesty, it wouldn’t be very surprising if he did manage to deal with that.
Rather, he was somewhat hoping he does.
He would rather face a new enemy than have Zylarith resurrect and return to his prime—and he was quite sure the rest of the Infinities would want the same thing.
But—

"These are all just theories. I am sure every single one of us has many in our heads. There is no point in discussing these, not unless we have any way of knowing how likely each of these theories are."
Suddenly, Eternity spoke up.
"Currently, what we know for sure is that the Anomaly is related to the Fifth Infinity as well as Zylarith.
Both of them are dangerous beings, and so is the Anomaly.
If anything, I believe the Anomaly is much scarier than the other two."
Again, the Infinities nodded with their silence.

Both Zylarith and the Fifth Infinity—they knew something about them. Zylarith was currently in a state so weakened that he was of no threat to them at all. All he could currently do was plan his return—and it wouldn’t be that simple.
The Fifth Infinity, on the other hand, he was more of a physical threat—a being capable of going against them.

None of them knew what he was like or how strong he was. What they did know, however, was that he came from a world that is the reincarnation of Chaosveil, the Strongest Supreme World. He would be anything but weak.
But—
He would still be limited by the Universe’s restrictions.

Even Zylarith wasn’t able to take all four of them on his own. They were sure the Universe must have placed some sort of restriction on the Fifth Infinity to protect itself from complete domination by a single being.
That was how the Universe worked.
The problem, however, was the one who the very Universe was wary against.
The Anomaly.
A being who went beyond what even the Universe could control.

Yes, from the looks of it, he looked like a child still wet behind his ears, but... the number of times he had alerted the Universe with his actions was far, far greater than all four of them combined.
It was almost as if his very existence went against the Universe.
Till now, the Infinities did not take this matter very seriously because the Anomaly never directly harmed them, but today...
It was different.
Today, the Anomaly interrupted the operation they commanded.
It was an open declaration.
The Anomaly...
He was finally making moves against them—and this time, they needed to take action in order to deal with the enemy surrounded by mystery.
"What do we know about him?"
Balance questioned, looking at Eternity for answers.
And Eternity...
"Nothing."
He shook his head.
"What...?"
Balance’s expression changed.
"We do not know anything?"
He questioned again with a frown.
"We do know how he looks, but the problem remains the same—looks are subjective. Most beings have the ability to change them. Someone like the Anomaly should have the means to change his appearance."

"What about his abilities? From the looks of it, he protected Zylarith’s disciple from Zarveth. The two of them must have fought each other, did they not? What about that fight? Or was it too one-sided for us to know anything?"
Balance questioned.
Of course, not for a single moment did he think that Zarveth actually won against the Anomaly. He just wanted to know if he gathered anything useful.

Eternity did not answer his question directly. The screen that was in front of them started playing instead. The recording that had stopped where Sharnoth released a ridiculous amount of Chaos Energy to battle Zarveth started again.

The battle between the two Eternals continued. The Infinities watched in silence. The level of battle did not impress them, but since Eternity was showing it to them, they knew something important was about to happen.

Of course, they were also observing Zylarith’s disciple and comparing her with Zylarith. After all, every single one of them had seen Zylarith grow from a Sovereign to an Infinity—they were more than qualified to judge here.
"The difference between Zylarith and her couldn’t be clearer. Zylarith would have never struggled so much in a battle at this level."
Light couldn’t help but comment. She seemed somewhat disappointed.
Yes, Zarveth was comparatively stronger and a somewhat difficult opponent at the level of Eternals because of how resourceful and experienced he was, but...
Zylarith was in a league of his own.
Light expected... a bit more from his disciple.
"What were you even expecting? Of course the two of them would be different. She is just a tool Zylarith plans to use. He wouldn’t have taught her anything substantial."
Darkness snorted. He never believed the disciple could reach her master’s level anyway.
"Keep in mind, Zylarith had a complete Body of Chaos. That girl does not."
Balance spoke lightly. It wasn’t fair to compare Zylarith and the girl anyway.
"Whatever."
Darkness simply didn’t care.
He wasn’t interested in watching some Eternals fight anyway. He was only watching because Eternity wanted them to.

That child might be arrogant, but even Darkness had to agree that he was quite resourceful. Honestly, all beings from the Supreme World of Eternity were—even Zarveth, who was facing the girl, was no different.
The moment he realized that he was being overpowered, he quickly took out the Infinity Relics and began overpowering Sharnoth—ending the battle almost instantly.
In the end, the girl was trapped, unable to resist Relics made by an Infinity—
"That was disappointing."
Darkness snorted. He then turned towards Eternity and—
"Did you make us watch because you wanted us to see how good your toys are in a battle against children?"
He questioned, somewhat annoyed.
But then—
[BOOOOOOM]
Inside the recording, just when Zarveth was about to end the battle, dark energy began to gather and suddenly—
[So in the end—you failed to suppress your true nature, huh?
I feared this might happen.]
He appeared.
