chapters.title: Chapter 2125: An Infinity.
paragraphs: [So in the end—you failed to suppress your true nature, huh?
I feared this might happen.]
The Anomaly appeared, and in an instant, Darkness turned silent. His focus once again fell on the screen.
Eternity did not react to his words; he was already used to his antics.
The other two Infinities weren’t interested in Darkness either; they had learned to ignore him as well.
All Infinities just focused on the screen.
[Nah.]
Suddenly, the Anomaly laughed.
[I wanted to play with you.
I wanted to play with therealSharnoth Nocthys, not the Sharnoth you became to please those around you.]
"They seem to be having a conversation in the middle of the battle."
Light muttered.
"Haa! They are treating Zarveth and those Infinity Relics like a joke!"

Darkness laughed out loud, unable to control himself. He actually started liking the two—the Anomaly, who didn’t seem to care about anything, and Sharnoth, who, despite her state, was laughing like a maniac.
He felt like if they were in another timeline under different circumstances, he might have gotten along with them quite well.
Too bad, in this timeline, they would have no choice but to perish under his claws.
The recording continued. Just as Darkness said, it showed just how much the girl and the Anomaly disregarded Zarveth.
Their conversation wasn’t just a little greeting—it was a full-blown conversation with no care for anything around them.
It was quite humiliating, actually. Even the Infinities felt bad for Zarveth.
Then suddenly, something even more surprising happened—
[Then how about I give you another chance?]
Suddenly, the Anomaly spoke up as he extended his hand and grabbed the Blade of Rewriting that had pierced through the girl’s core.
And then—
[Crack Crack Crack
Shatter]
The Blade of Rewriting was crushed into pieces.
"What...?"
Light narrowed her eyes, a little surprised.
Balance too reacted quite strongly.
"So... the Anomaly’s an Infinity, huh...?"
Darkness spoke.
There was no doubt about it.
No being other than an Infinity could break an Infinity Relic with such ease.

The other Infinities did not say anything either. This was the reason it surprised them. Yes, being able to break an Infinity Relic wasn’t exactly the sign of an Infinity, since every single one of them could do it with a mere thought, especially considering it was a Relic given to an Eternal, so it was much weaker than Relics Eternity himself used.
But still...
It wasn’t something even the Eternal whose entire focus was physical strength could do. Or at least... not by the Universe’s standards.
So either the Anomaly was an absurdly strong Eternal, a being at the level of Zylarith when he was an Eternal, or... he was an Infinity, just like them.
[Tsk Tsk, I can’t believe you were defeated by this Toy.
You disappoint me, Sharnoth Nocthys.]
The Anomaly snorted, dusting his hand away as if he had touched something disgusting, and Darkness—
"Would it be alright if I side with him instead?"
He grinned.
The more he watched the Anomaly, the more he started liking him. Now, even killing him seemed boring.
This one...
He was even more interesting than Zylarith himself!
The other three Infinities did not say anything, but in their minds, they started considering the possibility of Darkness actually betraying them when the time came.
Darkness, on the other hand, did not care about what they were thinking.
None of them were true allies in the first place; they just sat here together because the monopoly they had was convenient.
Of course, he had a few thoughts of his own as well, but for now, he pushed them all to the side and enjoyed the show in front of him.
He saw how the Anomaly looked for the Relic that stopped Sharnoth from moving, completely disregarding Zarveth. The Eternal tried to stop him, but then—
[Shatter]
The second Relic was shattered.
[Now I am even more disappointed in you, Sharnoth Nocthys. To think you lost against someone who can’t even differentiate between an illusion and reality.
Tsk Tsk Tsk.]
The Anomaly snorted as his illusion faded away and...
"He doesn’t seem to be an Infinity..."
Light muttered in a low voice. One could still sense her uncertainty.
The Anomaly was overpowering Zarveth, one of the strongest Eternals in the Universe. She could see that.
But...
An Infinity wouldn’t need to play such games against an Eternal...
Sure, if an Infinity wanted, they could still play around, but most of the time... they just wouldn’t bother.
What’s the point of playing around with an opponent you can defeat with a flick of your hand?
One would rather capture the opponent if they had any need for him, or end his existence and be done with it.
Dragging things out like this...
It didn’t seem like something an Infinity would do.
The other Infinities agreed in silence—even Darkness.
The Anomaly... didn’t seem as strong as an Infinity.
But...
If he was truly an Eternal—then things become much more complicated.
After all, every single one of them could see it.
The Anomaly...
He was physically stronger than the strongest known Eternals.
He was faster than the fastest known Eternals.
And... he was far trickier than any known Eternal.
He...
He was a True Absolute.
Seeing as how he wasn’t just fighting Zarveth, but also playing around with the Chaos girl, holding her by her neck, it was clear that he was far, far stronger than them.
He...
He was stronger than Zylarith when he was an Eternal.
If such a being became an Infinity...
None of them would be able to defeat him, even if they acted together.
Of course, all of this was still under the assumption that the Anomaly was only an Eternal and not an Infinity who simply enjoys playing with his prey.
Heck, for all they know, he might know that this battle of his might be getting recorded by Zarveth’s Relics and he was simply trying to trick them.
It wouldn’t be very surprising considering just how tricky that being is.
After all, he had the very Universe at his toes.
Never once in their long lives had they seen the Universe on edge because of one individual.
Using normal standards on the Anomaly was quite foolish.
So for now...
The Infinities decided to watch till the end.
[Unhand me!]
The Chaos girl shouted, trying to do everything in her power to get away from the Anomaly, but everything failed.
[We will play later. I have something to do.]
The Anomaly replied, and for the first time ever since he appeared, he glanced at Zarveth—
[You and Neremoth—who amongst you is stronger?]
He questioned.
[What did you do to him?]
Zarveth narrowed his eyes, and the Anomaly just heaved a tired sigh.
[Whatever, not that it matters.]
He shrugged.
And then—
[I suppose I should try it.]
He muttered as he extended his free hand outward, and a faint ripple formed around his palm, instantly expanding into something much larger, and then—
Zpp
The screen the Infinities were watching on suddenly turned dark, taking them back. The Infinities waited patiently for the battle to continue, but then—
"It’s over.
Whatever happened after this wasn’t recorded."
Eternity clarified.
"What...?"
Balance frowned.
"Wasn’t recorded? Your Infinity Relics were still there, weren’t they?"

Every Relic in the Universe could be tracked at any moment. Not just that, these Relics recorded everything that happened around them, and the Supreme Beings of Eternity who created these Relics could watch these recordings anytime they desired, finding the information relevant for them.
Infinity Relics, of course, were similar—no, actually, they were much better at this.
While beings could still outsmart normal Relics, because the Infinity Relics were directly created by Eternity himself—they couldn’t be outsmarted.
One couldn’t simply cover the Relics in darkness to hinder their vision—they would be able to pierce through the darkness—but—
"From this moment forward, I lost the connection I had with Zarveth or the Infinity Relics I gave him.
The Anomaly... managed to break that connection."
Eternity revealed, and in an instant, the air in the Hall changed.

If before, they still had doubts, now, everything was clear—after all, there was only one way to get rid of the connection Eternity has with his people and the Relics throughout the Universe—a way all Infinities use.
To create their own World.
Even the very Universe couldn’t sense what the Infinities did inside their Worlds, let alone Eternity.
Could Eternals make it such that Eternity could no longer sense his Relics inside their domains?
Well, technically yes. As Absolutes, they could will the Relics to freeze—or be destroyed, even—but this would only continue as long as their domain was active.
And even then, since Eternity would know the last location of the Relic, he would know where the Domain was created, essentially giving him the ability to track the Eternal down.
But...
This was different.
"I no longer know where they are.
I no longer know whether Zarveth is alive or dead.
It is... almost as if he was taken away from the Universe."
Eternity spoke, and just as the Infinities expected...
Having the ability to hide things from someone like Eternity...
The Anomaly was indeed an Infinity.

Just as Darkness said, it showed just how much the girl and the Anomaly disregarded Zarveth.
Their conversation wasn’t just a little greeting—it was a full-blown conversation with no care for anything around them.
It was quite humiliating, actually.
Even the Infinities felt bad for Zarveth.
Then suddenly, something even more surprising happened—
[Then how about I give you another chance?]
Suddenly, the Anomaly spoke up as he extended his hand and grabbed the Blade of Rewriting that had pierced through the girl’s core.
And then—
[Crack Crack Crack
Shatter]
The Blade of Rewriting was crushed into pieces.
"What...?"
Light narrowed her eyes, a little surprised.
Balance too reacted quite strongly.
"So... the Anomaly’s an Infinity, huh...?"
Darkness spoke.
There was no doubt about it.
No being other than an Infinity could break an Infinity Relic with such ease.
The other Infinities did not say anything either.
This was the reason it surprised them.

Yes, being able to break an Infinity Relic wasn’t exactly the sign of an Infinity, since every single one of them could do it with a mere thought, especially considering it was a Relic given to an Eternal, so it was much weaker than Relics Eternity himself used.
But still...
It wasn’t something even the Eternal whose entire focus was physical strength could do.
Or at least... not by the Universe’s standards.
So either the Anomaly was an absurdly strong Eternal, a being at the level of Zylarith when he was an Eternal, or... he was an Infinity, just like them.
[Tsk Tsk, I can’t believe you were defeated by this Toy.
You disappoint me, Sharnoth Nocthys.]
The Anomaly snorted, dusting his hand away as if he had touched something disgusting, and Darkness—
"Would it be alright if I side with him instead?"
He grinned.
The more he watched the Anomaly, the more he started liking him.
Now, even killing him seemed boring.
This one...
He was even more interesting than Zylarith himself!
The other three Infinities did not say anything, but in their minds, they started considering the possibility of Darkness actually betraying them when the time came.
Darkness, on the other hand, did not care about what they were thinking.
None of them were true allies in the first place; they just sat here together because the monopoly they had was convenient.
Of course, he had a few thoughts of his own as well, but for now, he pushed them all to the side and enjoyed the show in front of him.
He saw how the Anomaly looked for the Relic that stopped Sharnoth from moving, completely disregarding Zarveth.
The Eternal tried to stop him, but then—
[Shatter]
The second Relic was shattered.
[Now I am even more disappointed in you, Sharnoth Nocthys.
To think you lost against someone who can’t even differentiate between an illusion and reality.
Tsk Tsk Tsk.]
The Anomaly snorted as his illusion faded away and...
"He doesn’t seem to be an Infinity..."
Light muttered in a low voice.
One could still sense her uncertainty.
The Anomaly was overpowering Zarveth, one of the strongest Eternals in the Universe.
She could see that.
But...
An Infinity wouldn’t need to play such games against an Eternal...
Sure, if an Infinity wanted, they could still play around, but most of the time... they just wouldn’t bother.
What’s the point of playing around with an opponent you can defeat with a flick of your hand?
One would rather capture the opponent if they had any need for him, or end his existence and be done with it.
Dragging things out like this...
It didn’t seem like something an Infinity would do.
The other Infinities agreed in silence—even Darkness.
The Anomaly... didn’t seem as strong as an Infinity.
But...
If he was truly an Eternal—then things become much more complicated.
After all, every single one of them could see it.
The Anomaly...
He was physically stronger than the strongest known Eternals.
He was faster than the fastest known Eternals.
And... he was far trickier than any known Eternal.
He...
He was a True Absolute.
Seeing as how he wasn’t just fighting Zarveth, but also playing around with the Chaos girl, holding her by her neck, it was clear that he was far, far stronger than them.
He...
He was stronger than Zylarith when he was an Eternal.
If such a being became an Infinity...
None of them would be able to defeat him, even if they acted together.
Of course, all of this was still under the assumption that the Anomaly was only an Eternal and not an Infinity who simply enjoys playing with his prey.
Heck, for all they know, he might know that this battle of his might be getting recorded by Zarveth’s Relics and he was simply trying to trick them.
It wouldn’t be very surprising considering just how tricky that being is.
After all, he had the very Universe at his toes.
Never once in their long lives had they seen the Universe on edge because of one individual.
Using normal standards on the Anomaly was quite foolish.
So for now...
The Infinities decided to watch till the end.
[Unhand me!]
The Chaos girl shouted, trying to do everything in her power to get away from the Anomaly, but everything failed.
[We will play later.
I have something to do.]
The Anomaly replied, and for the first time ever since he appeared, he glanced at Zarveth—
[You and Neremoth—who amongst you is stronger?]
He questioned.
[What did you do to him?]
Zarveth narrowed his eyes, and the Anomaly just heaved a tired sigh.
[Whatever, not that it matters.]
He shrugged.
And then—
[I suppose I should try it.]
He muttered as he extended his free hand outward, and a faint ripple formed around his palm, instantly expanding into something much larger, and then—
Zpp
The screen the Infinities were watching on suddenly turned dark, taking them back.
The Infinities waited patiently for the battle to continue, but then—
"It’s over.
Whatever happened after this wasn’t recorded."
Eternity clarified.
"What...?"
Balance frowned.
"Wasn’t recorded?
Your Infinity Relics were still there, weren’t they?"
Every Relic in the Universe could be tracked at any moment.

Not just that, these Relics recorded everything that happened around them, and the Supreme Beings of Eternity who created these Relics could watch these recordings anytime they desired, finding the information relevant for them.
Infinity Relics, of course, were similar—no, actually, they were much better at this.
While beings could still outsmart normal Relics, because the Infinity Relics were directly created by Eternity himself—they couldn’t be outsmarted.
One couldn’t simply cover the Relics in darkness to hinder their vision—they would be able to pierce through the darkness—but—
"From this moment forward, I lost the connection I had with Zarveth or the Infinity Relics I gave him.
The Anomaly... managed to break that connection."
Eternity revealed, and in an instant, the air in the Hall changed.

If before, they still had doubts, now, everything was clear—after all, there was only one way to get rid of the connection Eternity has with his people and the Relics throughout the Universe—a way all Infinities use.
To create their own World.
Even the very Universe couldn’t sense what the Infinities did inside their Worlds, let alone Eternity.
Could Eternals make it such that Eternity could no longer sense his Relics inside their domains?
Well, technically yes.
As Absolutes, they could will the Relics to freeze—or be destroyed, even—but this would only continue as long as their domain was active.
And even then, since Eternity would know the last location of the Relic, he would know where the Domain was created, essentially giving him the ability to track the Eternal down.
But...
This was different.
"I no longer know where they are.
I no longer know whether Zarveth is alive or dead.
It is... almost as if he was taken away from the Universe."
Eternity spoke, and just as the Infinities expected...
Having the ability to hide things from someone like Eternity...
The Anomaly was indeed an Infinity.

chapters.title: Chapter 2126: Stop with the pointless provocations.
paragraphs: "So now we have six Infinities, huh..."
Balance muttered in a solemn tone, staring at the blank screen in front of him.
"And a Zylarith no one knows the plans of."
Light spoke up.
"There is the Seer too. I never once liked that woman."
She added.

The Infinities turned silent at the mention of the Seer’s name. The woman just randomly appeared one day out of nowhere. No one in the entire Universe knew anything about her—and in complete contrast, she knew everything about everyone.
Even the Infinities didn’t seem to be exceptions to that.
Her presence obviously made the Infinities wary. They had tried capturing that woman more than once, but she managed to escape every single time.
No, ’managing to escape’ was the wrong way to describe it—she never once fell for any of their traps, which was something the Infinities had never experienced.

Even someone like Zylarith had fallen for their traps more than once. This was the reason he stayed hidden almost all the time, never making a bold appearance for fear of the four of them learning his whereabouts and capturing him.
But Seer?
The woman didn’t seem to have any reservations at all.
She appeared and reappeared anytime she wanted, without any care for any being in the Universe.
Heck, she even boldly contacted the four of them—more than once, actually. She simply left a message for them.
Yes, a message for them!
The four beings who had the habit of summoning any being they wanted to contact—this woman dared to summon them and give directions as to how to contact her.
What’s worse?
They went!
They followed her directions!
Why?
Because even they knew how useful the Seer was.
She knew things even Eternity did not!
Heck, she predicted Zylarith’s movements more than once—she was the reason they were able to stop Umbrasol before Zylarith made too big of a mess there.
Yes, the cunning bastard did disappear, but the woman was still correct about him.
Honestly, if the Seer was completely by their side, half of the problems the Infinities currently had would be solved.
Zylarith wouldn’t be able to escape. Even the Fifth Infinity wouldn’t be able to hide. As for Anomaly...
They believed the woman was in contact with him as well.
She just...
Wasn’t answering them anymore...
It was frustrating to think about her, but...
Light was correct. Right now, they were in no position to take her out of the equation.
"Zylarith, Seer, the Fifth Infinity, and now the Sixth Infinity... Our Universe is becoming much more complicated than I remember. No wonder it is so sensitive these days.
I didn’t even know the birth of a Sixth Infinity was possible."
Suddenly, Eternity chuckled. His tone seemed much lighter than the others’, as if he was hiding something—something that gave him absolute confidence.
The other Infinities did not react to his tone. They knew he was simply trying to get more out of them—they were long used to such trickery.
"Maybe... the Anomaly is not the Sixth Infinity..."
Suddenly, Light spoke up in an uncertain tone.
The other Infinities turned towards her and—
"What if... the Fifth Infinity is the Anomaly itself?"
She suggested another theory.
"He appeared to defend him, did he not? What if he was defending his clone instead? Or maybe the one defending was the clone.
We did see Anomaly use a similar ability, so it wouldn’t be surprising if he used that ability before."
"That... could be true."
Balance did not deny the theory outright.
It actually made more sense if that were the case.
After all, this way, the Universe’s rule that had not been broken for trillions of years would stay intact.
But...
If that was the case, then...
"Are you saying...
The Universe’s Child is one of us?"
Eternity questioned. Even though their faces weren’t visible, every other Infinity knew he had a light, provocative smile on his face when he said those words.
And once again, the air in the hall became tense.
The Infinities had had this conversation before—the Universe had chosen a ’Hero,’ a being who was connected to the Universe, a being who didn’t have to face restrictions other beings had to face.
A being who could grow... beyond Infinity.
Of course, not every being would get such an opportunity—only the beings close to the Universe could.
What did it mean?
It meant that only the Infinities could become the Universe’s Child.

The four of them had discussed this before, trying to figure out who amongst them was the Universe’s Child. However, after endless discussions, observations, investigations, agreements, disagreements, questions, and answers, to continue a formal discussion on every future topic—
The Four Infinities made a consensual decision.
None of them were the Universe’s Chosen.
It was the Fifth Infinity.
It was a much safer choice. After all, a Universe’s Chosen should have some level of change in them, but none of the Four Infinities grew.
Sure, they could have hidden it—but hiding their rise in strength and influence from beings as sensitive as Infinities wasn’t easy.
And since the Four Infinities couldn’t sense any changes in any of them—they directed their attention to the Fifth Infinity.
However, if Light’s theory about the Fifth Infinity and Anomaly being the same entity was indeed correct, then—
Their unanimous decision would be wrong. After all, the Universe wouldn’t possibly choose and empower the Anomaly to get rid of itself.
So once again, the suspicion fell on all of them—and this time, it was much heavier than before.
After all, if the Universe’s Chosen was indeed one of them, then he or she had managed to fool them once—it was something that none of their egos would accept.
Once again, a long heavy silence fell in the Hall until finally—
"Stop it."
Balance spoke up.
"We have been through this before. Such discussions are pointless. What Light said was just a theory, and from the looks of it, one that is highly unlikely at this point.
The Fifth Infinity and Anomaly cannot be the same—not when the Fifth Infinity is the Universe’s Chosen.
We do not have the time to derail the conversation."
"Haa! Spoken like a true Universe’s Chosen."
Darkness laughed, glaring at Balance.
"I always doubted you."
He spoke directly.
"You doubt everyone."
Balance spoke calmly.
He then glanced at the others and—
"Do not forget—the entire reason the Anomaly is known as Anomaly is because he does things that go against the rules and restrictions set by the Universe.
For someone like him, becoming the Sixth Infinity is not impossible."

Balance explained, and his words gained nods of approval. Yes, the Infinities did suspect him of being the Universe’s Child—no, not just him—they suspected every single one of them. But to continue the conversation and get something meaningful out of it, they decided to follow Balance’s words.
Infighting at times like these was foolish, and the Infinities knew that.
"It is quite fun, don’t you think?"
Suddenly, Eternity chuckled, once again attracting everyone’s attention.
"Will you stop it!? Do not force me to end your existence first!"
Darkness glared at him in anger.
He never liked the kid to begin with—but he could swear that he was purposefully being more annoying than usual.
"You are welcome to try."
Eternity chuckled.
"As I said before, I am not the same child as before."
"You—alright then, be prepared, I am com—"
"Calm down."
Balance interrupted. He then turned towards Eternity and—
"Stop with the pointless provocations."
"I am not trying to provoke anyone; I am just stating what I feel."
Eternity answered.
"Think about this—how long has it been since our meetings became this frequent? No—did it ever happen before? Us meeting every few years.
Things are so chaotic, so many beings have so many Grand Plans of their own—and all these Grand Plans are finally coming together, all at the same time.
It’s a storm.
A very big storm is coming.
Something that would change the very history of our Universe—and we get to see everything from such proximity.
Don’t you feel it as well?
Our pointlessly boring lives where we did nothing but command our people are going to change.
Something big is about to happen.
It is just like what Mother said would happen before her death."
Eternity laughed—and suddenly, the Infinities turned silent as they recalled another existence.
Eternity’s mother, the previous Eternity.
The entity who predicted Zylarith’s movements and stopped him before he could overpower all of them alone and take over the Universe.
She was the reason all of them were still alive—and Zylarith was in such a state.
It was said that in her last moments, she said something to her son—the current Eternity—something he hadn’t revealed to anyone.
"...what do you mean?"
Balance questioned in a low, careful voice.
"What? I am just stating what I’m thinking. There is nomeaningbehind my words."
Eternity chuckled.
"YOU—"
Darkness was prepared to rush forward, wanting to make this bastard speak what he had in his mind but then—
"Wait."
Light muttered, her tone much different than before.
"Your mother..."
She called out, staring at Eternity and—

chapters.title: Chapter 2127: Why don’t you give it a try?
paragraphs: "Wait."
Suddenly, Light called out, instantly attracting everyone’s attention. She then stared at Eternity and—
"Your mother...
She revealed the existence of a Law that Zylarith was working on—that was the reason we all came together.
The Law of Absolute Growth.
What happened to it?"
Light questioned. Her words silenced Darkness, who was close to losing his temper.
The Law of Absolute Growth.

A power that was derived from Chaos’s property of growing without limits, a power that the previous Eternity felt threatened by—to the point where she gave her life away just to look into the future and see how it would turn out.
And the result?
Absolute destruction.

’I saw our heads perched upon spears, displayed like mere ornaments that only glorified a throne and, on that throne, sat one man—Zylarith Chaosveil, the Ruler of the Universe, and the only being in the entirety of the Universe to reach a level beyond Infinity: the Level of Omnipotence.’
Those were the words she used before her death—words that forced the Infinities to come together to face a common enemy for the first and, to this date, last time in the long history of the Universe.
But...
The Law that brought the Three Infinities together...
For something like this to not be talked about all this while...
For some reason, this made Light more wary.

"Zylarith is still alive, is he not? What if he has completed the Law of Absolute Growth? What if the Body of Chaos is not his strongest weapon? What if... it is the Law of Absolute Growth? And what if...
The one who has the Law of Absolute Growth is... the Anomaly?"
Light spoke, and the more she thought about it, the stronger this possibility became in her mind.

"Think about it, a being like the Anomaly couldn’t possibly have appeared out of nowhere. There has to be a reason behind everything. In our Universe, most things that went close to going against the Universe had Zylarith’s hand behind them.

Umbrasol’s Reaper’s Veil was an example of it—Zylarith managed to create a combination of energies that somehow managed to create space that is outside the influence of the Universe, without having an Infinity on his side.

And this wasn’t the only time he did something like this. He was behind the Great Unmaking, the Soul Storm, Stillness Before the End—he was behind them all, and every single one of these things happened because he did something no one in the Universe ever did.
Every single one of these things happened because he tried going against the Universe’s rules.
So what if...
What if this time, he succeeded?
What if this time he created an entity that even the very Universe fears?
What if... Zylarith is the Anomaly himself?"

Light spoke, and a heavy silence fell in the hall. Once again, her words made logical sense—well, there was not much to be made sense of here anyways; they were talking about a being who went against the rules set by the Universe—nothing about this should make any sense here.
All of this was...
"A theory,"
Eternity muttered.

"All of this is merely a theory, something you came up with in your head. There is no proof behind it. As mentioned before, I am sure every single one of us has multiple such theories. If we began discussing everything one by one, that would be the only thing we would be able to do—discuss.
It is good to worry about things; it shows you do not foolishly believe that you are always in control and cannot be dethroned. It is a good mindset but...
Too much of it is called paranoia.
And too much of it is detrimental."
The Being of Eternity spoke in a calm voice, wanting to change the topic, but this time, Light did not allow him to do that—
"It is a theory, yes, and it is a highly likely one.
Why does it seem like you are trying to avoid it?"
She questioned.
"I am simply trying to save our time."
"Time does not flow in this hall—we can discuss for millennia, and it wouldn’t affect the outside Universe.
You were the one who made it that way."
Light countered.
"That does not mean we are required to continue the discussion for millennia. Ceaselessly discussing mere theories with no proof behind them is unproductive. I do not wish to waste my time that way."
Eternity spoke directly.
"So what do you wish to do?"
Light questioned.
"What is your suggestion?
You do not want us to watch everything in silence andhave fun, do you? Because if that is indeed the case,
Then it gives me reason to believe that your goal might not be aligned with ours."

Light spoke, her voice lowering, but the threat in it wasn’t hidden. It seemed like she was accusing Eternity of siding with the enemy—a thought that the other two Infinites couldn’t just deny outright.
Eternity’s actions have been strange from the very beginning, but the way he seems to be trying to shut down Light felt like... he was trying to hide something.
"Pffft!"
Suddenly, Eternity laughed out loud, unable to control himself.

"That statement of yours is only valid if all four of us had one common goal."

Why did you not do it?"

And the result?
Absolute destruction.

Those were the words she used before her death—words that forced the Infinities to come together to face a common enemy for the first and, to this date, last time in the long history of the Universe.
But...
The Law that brought the Three Infinities together...
For something like this to not be talked about all this while...
For some reason, this made Light more wary.
"Zylarith is still alive, is he not?

The one who has the Law of Absolute Growth is... the Anomaly?"

So what if...
What if this time, he succeeded?
What if this time he created an entity that even the very Universe fears?
What if...
Zylarith is the Anomaly himself?"
Light spoke, and a heavy silence fell in the hall.

chapters.title: Chapter 2128: What are you trying to hide?
paragraphs: "You could have appeared next to Zarveth and caught the Anomaly yourself any moment you wanted,
Why did you not do it?"
Darkness questioned, and for an instant, silence fell over the place.
And before Eternity could give any excuses—
"Yes, I know Zarveth sealed the Space, making it impossible for any being to get to them but...
You aren’t just ’any’ being, are you?
You had your Infinity Relics, I refuse to believe that someone like you would not have a way to get to your Infinity Relics, even if the Space in that region is sealed."
Darkness took a small pause and once again—
"So why did you not take action? Why wait till the Universe reacted and everything happened before you finally came to us?"
"What are you implying?"
Eternity questioned directly. For the first time ever since their conversation began, his tone seemed to have faltered, as if he no longer had control over the situation.
"You should know what I am implying."
Darkness muttered, soon however, as if not wanting to give him any chance to turn this around—
"Why didn’t you deal with the Anomaly when you had the chance to? Or did you... purposefully let him go?"
The allegations were clear.
Then suddenly, the screen that hovered above the absurdly large table started showing something. It was a sight that somewhat surprised Eternity—after all, he wasn’t the one showing this.
The control he had over the screen was taken away.
And... noticing whose perspective was being played, he quickly understood who took control of the screen.
It was Darkness.
And the screen was currently showing the time when Zarveth, leading the Supreme Party, had just reached where the Anomaly was waiting for him.
This scene... it was being played from Neremoth’s perspective.
It meant...
Darkness was watching everything through Neremoth’s eyes...
It wasn’t just Eternity who had sent Zarveth to die just so they could gather more information, Darkness was the same.
Darkness fully understood Neremoth’s chaotic thoughts and nature, and he used it to his own advantage.
Eternity stared at Darkness in silence.
Neremoth being there because Darkness wanted him to wasn’t something that surprised him—Darkness was far more clever than he let on, he knew that well.
What did surprise him, however...
Was that he decided to showit.

The screen showed how the Anomaly and the Supreme Party were quite far from each other before suddenly, Zarveth closed the distance between the two, prepared to behead the Anomaly—but the Anomaly dodged.
[Oh?]
Zarveth’s amused voice was heard.
[You moved.]
He spoke, almost as if he was surprised by it. Something that confused the Infinities—of course he moved.
What else was he expecting?
To defeat an opponent like the Anomaly with such ease?
Had he lost his mind?
[I have never seen a Primordial react so quickly.]
Zarveth’s next words were heard, and in an instant, a heavy, almost deathly silence fell in the hall.
What...?
A Primordial...?
What... was he talking about...?
And... why was the Anomaly staring at Zarveth with such a grim look on his face?
Was he... playing around with him?
That didn’t seem to be the case.

From what they saw, the Anomaly did not seem the type to act weak in front of an opponent—yes, he might want to elongate their opponent’s suffering, crushing every single sliver of hope they might have, but this...
This did not seem like a mere act.
But then something even more surprising happened—
The Anomaly made his move—
A wave of destructive energy rushed towards Zarveth. He, of course, dodged that energy but...
The Infinities widened their eyes when they recognized the energy.
[Energy of Chaos, huh?
Now this is surprising.]
And Zarveth’s voice confirmed it.
The Anomaly used the Energy of Chaos.
And it wasn’t just the Energy of Chaos—the Anomaly used Space Laws as well.
But...
Wasn’t his physical strength his strongest advantage...?
How was he... using all these energies...?
The battle continued. The Anomaly then summoned Sharnoth Nocthys, the one believed to be Zylarith’s heir, but now...
Everything changed.
The Anomaly...
Zarveth treated him as a Primordial.
Heck, he even thought Sharnoth Nocthys was the true enemy and completely ignored the Anomaly as if he were a mere subordinate.
The Anomaly and the Heir to Chaos finally made a move, teleporting next to the Supreme Party and covering them with that strange energy of the Anomaly.
An energy that none of the Infinities recognized.
The Supreme Party disappeared. Every single Infinity realized that this was the moment when they felt their connection with their subordinates disappear.
It was also the moment Zarveth realized the being he was facing was not just a mere subordinate, but the Anomaly himself.

If before, all his actions were taken because he wanted to be ’entertained’, now, his greed took over. He wanted to get his hands on the Anomaly—and every single being present in this room could tell what he was thinking.
"The Anomaly was weak."
Darkness began as the scene he was playing momentarily paused.

"So pitifully weak that Zarveth called him a Primordial, and from the way the Anomaly reacted at Zarveth’s arrival, it was clear that he was quite unsure of whether he could deal with Zarveth or not."
As if to prove his words, the ’fight’ between Zarveth and the Anomaly continued. Zarveth completely sealed the Space around them, making sure no one could come there or realize what was happening.
The Anomaly prepared to face Zarveth together with Sharnoth, but then, Neremoth revealed his existence and...
The Anomaly escaped.
Once again, the screen stopped. The Infinities narrowed their eyes.
After all, all of them could see what Darkness was trying to say.

The Anomaly was weak, much weaker than they initially expected. Now, they couldn’t sense his energy through the screen, but considering that even Neremoth dared to reveal his existence in front of him, and how confident both he and Zarveth sounded—not even thinking of the Anomaly as a threat, but as a target—
It would be surprising if he was indeed a Primordial.
But...
If that was indeed the case—
Then the Anomaly they saw before and the one right now...
They were two entirely different entities.
So much so that the Infinities were actually wondering if it was indeed someone else.
Then...
Did it mean that there were actually two Anomalies?
But that didn’t seem to be the case.

A simple change in one’s appearance wouldn’t fool someone like Zarveth—they had watched the battle between the Anomaly and Zarveth. Zarveth seemed shocked at how absurdly strong the Anomaly was, but it was clear that he didn’t think the two were different people.
Then...
What happened?
What happened after the Anomaly disappeared?
What did he do?
How did he get so strong after he returned?
How did he—a mere Primordial—become an Infinity?
Or...
Was he... not an Infinity like they thought him to be?
The moment they thought about it, the Infinities’ expressions turned solemn. Darkness, however, wasn’t done yet.
He glanced at Eternity and—
"You could watch every single being that uses your Relics or is connected to your World any time you desire.
Zarveth was no exception to this rule, we all know that.
Then why didn’t you show us this initial battle?"
He questioned, and in an instant, the other Infinities turned towards Eternity.
"Why didn’t you show us that the Anomaly we believe to be Infinity... was just seen as a Primordial a few hours ago?
Why didn’t you show us how he used the Energy of Chaos and so many different energies together?
Why didn’t you show us how he... grew at such an absurd rate?

Why did you... purposefully try to make us believe that the Anomaly is an Infinity with low potential... instead of showing us that he is a monster who... probably isn’t an Infinity but a monster at a far lower stage, but so strong that he was mistaken as one?"
Darkness questioned, letting every single one of his words sink in. And as the tension in the air grew—
"What are you trying to hide, Orravyn?
First, you refuse to make a move yourself when you could have captured the Anomaly yourself.
Then you try to cover for him, trying to make us underestimate his potential.
What are you trying to do?
Why do your actions... make it seem like you are on the enemy’s side?"
Darkness questioned, and this time, it wasn’t just a random accusation that could be ignored or be seen as Darkness blabbering whatever came to his mind.
This time—
It truly felt like Eternity was indeed on the enemy’s side, and if he didn’t explain himself here—things might not turn out well for him, this time, for real.
Eternity realized it as well. He knew crazily challenging them to a battle like he did before wouldn’t work—
Therefore, he came up with something else, something... better.
"Then let me ask you the same question—
You knew everything I knew—
Why didn’tyoumake a move?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2129: ...how are we going to face them?
paragraphs: "If you knew everything I knew—
Why didn’tyoumake a move?
Don’t tell me someone like you does not have a way to move to a sealed space, that would make it quite laughable."
Eternity replied, asking the same question Darkness asked him.
And it wasn’t just the same question—
"If you knew everything I knew, why did you stay silent all this while? Why didn’t you call me out when you thought I was lying?
Wereyoutrying to hide the enemy’s potential?
Areyouon the enemy’s side?"
He raised the same allegations.
"Stop playing around.
I am not the same as you, you know that well."
Darkness, however, answered calmly.
"I did not see everything happen when it did. I realized what was happening after the Universe reacted and my connection with Neremoth disappeared.
What I showed earlier was Neremoth’s Vision before he disappeared."
"Is that so?"
Eternity replied, amused by those words.
Then with a wave of his hand, the Vision that had paused played further, this time, through Zarveth’s perspective.

Anomaly and Sharnoth moved towards the Supreme Party, devoured them, Neremoth revealed himself, the two talked about going against the Infinities and capturing the Anomaly, the Anomaly then disappears and this time, the Vision continues as Neremoth chases after the Anomaly and disappears with him.
"This must be what you were talking about, correct? He must have ’disappeared’ after this, huh?"
Eternity asked, his amused tone did not fade away.
"...that is correct."
Darkness nodded. This time, however, his words seemed somewhat heavier, and the other two Infinities knew why that was the case.
From one look, Neremoth chasing after the Anomaly didn’t seem like a big deal, however, for the Infinities, it revealed quite a few things.
One couldn’t forcefully enter an Infinity’s domain in such a manner.
If the Anomaly was indeed an Infinity like they first thought, then Neremoth wouldn’t have been able to follow him. Of course, this could be the Anomaly trying to lure Neremoth out, but...
The fact of the matter remained the same... if the Anomaly was an Infinity like they thought... he wouldn’t need to play such games.
Heck, Neremoth himself wouldn’t have the gall to chase after him.
From all these things, one thing couldn’t be any clearer.
The Anomaly, at least the one shown on the screen, was not an Infinity.
But if that was the case—
Then what was he?
What was... that dark energy that none of them seemed to recognize?
What was that energy that seemed... out of this Universe?
The more the Infinities thought about it, the more questions appeared in their heads.
Where did the Anomaly escape to?
How did he escape when the Space was sealed?
It definitely wasn’t a teleportation, it couldn’t be teleportation.
Yes, the Infinities had a way to move when Space is sealed, but it wasn’t something any being could pull off. They needed to alter the very Laws of the region they were in and—
Seeing Zarveth’s surprised reaction, it was very clear that the Laws of the region were not altered.
It was something... entirely different than what any of them knew.
And no, it wasn’t a new form of Law or something like that.
These beings who have been alive for trillions of years wouldn’t have missed something like that.
It was something much, much different.
Something... all four Infinities now had a rough idea about... just that... none of them wanted to say it out loud.
Eternity actually wanted to hide it, but since Darkness said what he said, he had no choice but to give in and reveal everything.
And now...
Every Infinity knew what the other was thinking.
Why didn’t Eternity or Darkness make a move?
It wasn’t because they were trying to hide something.
It wasn’t because they were trying to side with the enemy.
It was because...
They were scared.
They were scared not of the Anomaly, of course, but... what his existence represented.
"Why did you try to hide it...?"
Light questioned in a low voice, staring at Eternity. It was clear that she did not want this foolish game to continue any longer.
Not when... all of this could mean the end of them all.
"...I was not sure."
Eternity answered honestly.
This time, he played no games. There was no amusement or playfulness in his voice. There was no mysteriousness in his words. It was a simple, honest answer.
"So you decided to hide?"
Light raised her eyebrow.
Balance, however, had a stronger reaction—
"Not sure? What is there to be ’not sure’ of?"
He questioned, his voice higher than usual. He who remained calm throughout their conversation, had finally reacted.
"No wonder the Universe reacted so strongly to that being’s appearance. It all makes perfect sense now!"
He spoke as if he had discovered the greatest truth.
"What were you thinking trying to hide something this crucial from us!? Have you lost your mind!?"
"As I said, I was not sur—"
"What are you not sure about!?
We have an entirely different Universe that has found the way to voluntarily cross the Multiversal restriction and overlap with ours!
You think you have the time tobe sureabout it!?"
Balance snapped.
And once again, heavy silence fell over the table as Eternity, Light, or Darkness, none of them spoke.
After all, the matter truly wasthatgrave.
The Anomaly...
He wasn’t a Primordial or an Infinity.
No, the threat he represented was far, far greater.
He...
He came from a different Universe.

Yes, another Universe. Every Infinity knew there were countless Universes different from their own. The beings from the Supreme World of Eternity had been constantly trying to study these different Universes. However, other than simply knowing of their existence and the fact that sometimes these Universes collide with each other, leading to a few exchanges of souls between two or even three different Universes, nothing more could be learned about these different Universes.
Of course, they had captured a few souls that accidentally came from other Universes to research and learn more about the other Universes through them.
However, at the fundamental level, the souls that came from the other Universes were exactly the same as the souls in their Universe.
So much so that if they did not catch these foreign souls the instant they sensed the Universal Collisions, there was no way to tell them apart.
And of course, since all the souls they captured had all their memories removed, just as their Universe removes soul memories, they couldn’t learn anything about the other Universes.
There were theories, yes, but nothing concrete.

It was something that always bothered the Infinities—well, mostly Eternity—since he wanted to know everything there was, and the fact that there existed knowledge that he could not possess... it did not sit well with him.

It bothered him quite a lot. The rest of the Infinities, however, did not particularly care. What they could not rule did not matter to them. Since there was no way to go to the other Universes and rule them, in their eyes, the other Universes did not exist.
Well...
Till now, that is.
But now, things were different.

Beings from another Universe had somehow found their way inside their Universe. And unlike the souls that came to their Universe through the Universal Collision that happens probably once every few million years and is completely by chance—this seemed... voluntary.
The Anomaly seemed to have perfect control over Universal Travel. He could come to their Universe and return to his whenever he wanted.
All of this meant one thing...
The beings from another Universe had learned something they did not.
And considering how they seemed to be moving so openly these days, it is clear that they are no longer ’investigating’ them.
The enemies are prepared to attack.
They are prepared to face them.
They have captured more than a few of their men, and by reading their memories, they would have all the information they would need about them.
And the worst part?
They were clueless.
They had absolutely no information about the enemy.
Who were they?
Which Universe did they come from?
How did they achieve Universe travel?
How strong are the strongest beings in their Universe?
What powers or Authorities do they have?
The cultivation system the enemy follows.
Nothing. They knew nothing.
The difference between the information the two sides had of each other was absurdly high.

Not to mention there is also Zylarith running around, preparing who knows what. His plans were unknown. The Seer was no exception either—if anything, she might even be from the enemy Universe. There is also the Fifth Infinity none of them has contact with. Whether he is a friend or an ally isn’t clear either.
The problem was apparent.
There were too many non-optimal factors on their side.
And the worst part?
The enemy probably knew of every single one of these factors.
It... it wouldn’t be surprising if they were overwhelmed in this War.
Things... did not look good.
In the end, Balance took a deep breath, calming himself down. Then, he stared at his ’allies’ and asked a direct question.
"...how are we going to face them?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2130: Our target is him.
paragraphs: "...how are we going to face them?"
Balance questioned as he took a deep breath, calmed himself down, and stared at his ’allies.’
"We would have known if some of us weren’t too cowardly to act."
Light snorted.
They didn’t need a genius to know who she was targeting.
Darkness growled, the black light that represented him intensified. He wanted to say something, but right now, he held himself back. After all, he wasn’t the only one who was being targeted.
Eternity was with him as well.

In truth, most of the blame was currently on Eternity. After all, the very fact that the enemies from another Universe figured out the way to breach the multiversal barrier and raid their Universe before them could be seen as a failure on Eternity’s part.
After all, out of the four of them, he was the one who prided himself on his knowledge, but now...
He was outsmarted.
And he wasn’t just outsmarted—when he realized that he was, he didn’t take action either and decided to hide things until he was ’sure’ of the situation.
All three Infinities, especially Light, stared at Eternity, who had had enough of it and—
"Alright then."
He began.
"Since you are obviously much braver than I am, the next time I encounter the Anomaly, I will send you to him instead.
How does that sound?"
He questioned directly, and in an instant, Light turned silent.
She obviously was not going to the Anomaly alone.
And Eternity, who already expected this reaction, simply ignored Light and glanced at Balance instead—
"Since Seraphielle isn’t jumping on the matter as bravely as she threw blame at others, why don’t you give it a try, Equarios?"
And just like Light, Balance stayed silent as well.
Eternity chuckled. Of course, he wasn’t planning on leaving Darkness alone either,
"What about you, Ul’Thakar?
You are the bravest of us all, are you not?
Also, it seems that darkness is a way to enter the enemy’s Universe. If it is you, you can easily enter their Universe and annihilate every single one of them.
That sounds interesting, does it not?
I can already imagine your blissful face as you crush all your enemies and take over an entirely different Universe.
Who knows?
You might even become the sole Lord of their Universe."
Of course, all those words were empty. Eternity knew it, and so did Darkness, but...
Just like the other two Infinities—Darkness stayed silent as well.
It was clear, none of the Infinities wanted to step forward.
Were they scared?
Of course!
This was an entirely different Universe they were talking about!
They did not know how strong the beings from this Universe were, but since these beings had managed to do something they didn’t even think was possible—it was clear that they weren’t weak.
Who knows?
The Anomaly might as well be baiting them out with his movements, and the instant any one of them gets there to capture him, they might get ambushed by two or three Infinities.

None of the Infinities wanted to step forward and test this theory by risking their lives. Yes, despite being trillions of years old, every single one of them cherished their lives more than anything.
But...
The fact that they needed to make a move couldn’t be ignored.
The enemy was already at their doorsteps; hiding in their homes as the enemy ran amok was clearly not a solution.
"Alright, enough of these games."
Balance spoke up after a long silence.
He needed to keep the conversation going.
"The Anomaly is a far bigger threat than what we previously believed. We need to act carefully and..."
Balance stared at his allies and—
"We need to move together."
This was the only option.
"The fact that the enemy hasn’t attacked us yet must mean they are being wary. They already have an informational advantage over us, but they are not using it.
This clearly indicates that the enemy is not as strong as we believe them to be. At the very least, they are not capable of taking all four of us together."
The other Infinities nodded at those words.
If the enemy could indeed take all four of them together, they wouldn’t be discussing here—they would have perished a long time ago.
"We now need to ensure that none of us is isolated anymore. Keep your senses on alert all the time. The moment you sense something is wrong, act.
Do not let the enemy take us down one by one because...
If any single one of us falls...
The rest will follow.
The enemy has no reason to accept surrender."
Balance gave out general directions.

At their level, accepting the enemy’s surrender was indeed foolish. They were beings who could manipulate anyone’s mind, turning them into what they desired. Honestly, any being at their level could do it—even those weaker than them weren’t out of options.

If the enemy was indeed strong enough to take them out, then they wouldn’t be exceptions either. Instead of accepting their surrender and keeping an uncertain variable alive, they would rather have a completely loyal puppet that they created as their subordinate, even if the said subordinate was weaker than them.
The other Infinities knew that as well.
After all, every single one of them would have done the same thing as well.
They realized it—for now, their strength was in their unity.
They needed to become true allies if they wanted to survive this crisis.
Seeing that all of them were on the same page, Balance nodded, satisfied.
"What we need to do from here on out is simple—"
He began, giving a clearer, better plan—
"We need information. We need to understand the enemy, so no matter what, we need to capture at least one of them.

For now, we will target the Anomaly that has been spreading chaos all over the Universe. We will send a few of our subordinates after him. This time, we will confirm his strength and once we see the opportunity,
We will move next to him—together."
The Infinities nodded again. None of them found anything wrong with it.
Was it shameful that four Infinities were going to act together to catch one child?
Well, the ’child’ wasn’t the threat here. They needed to move together because the child’s superiors might be watching through the child.
They might be waiting to surround them the instant they arrive, and if that indeed happens, the Infinities wanted to stay together.
This was the only way they would have the highest chance of victory.
"We will also try to contact the Fifth Infinity."
Balance spoke. This time, however, not everyone seemed to be on the same page as him.
"The Fifth Infinity? He protected the Anomaly once. It is clear he is with the enemy. What are you trying to gain here?"
Darkness frowned.
"We are not sure that he is the enemy."
Balance shook his head.
"He protected him! Wha—"
Darkness raised his voice.
"Only once."
Balance, however, interrupted him, and his words silenced Darkness for a moment. Balance continued,
"The Fifth Infinity only protected him once. After that, there were no signs of clear contact between the two.
It could be that the Anomaly did not need his help, but the possibility that the Fifth Infinity figured out the Anomaly’s secret and the two of them broke apart cannot be denied either.
If anything, the Fifth Infinity might be in danger or... he might be dead already."
Balance spoke with a grim look on his face, but then—
"That is not possible."
Eternity shook his head.
"There is no way the Universe wouldn’t have reacted strongly if the Fifth Infinity had died at the hands of the beings from another Universe.
And if an Infinity truly fought with his life on the line, there is no way we wouldn’t have felt anything."
"What if he was taken into their Univers—ah..."
Balance tried to give out another possibility. Soon, however, he realized how the Universe would have reacted if that had happened and shook his head.
Eternity nodded at his words. He then glanced at Darkness and Light and—
"The possibility that the Fifth Infinity is with the enemies cannot be denied. However, in the end, he does belong to our Universe.
The enemy wouldn’t have any reason to keep him alive after everything is done, and he should know that as well.
It is highly likely that he will become our ally.
So we do need to approach him."
Light nodded at those words, and Darkness... he nodded as well.

Having another Infinity with them was something they could not miss out on, especially when the said Infinity is technically a replacement of Zylarith, the strongest Infinity to ever exist in the Universe.
As he thought of all this, suddenly, another thought appeared in Darkness’s head—
"What about Zylarith?
What are we going to do about him?"
And this time, the one who answered his question was Eternity—
"His actions are too unpredictable for us to focus on him right now.
For now, we will leave him be.
Our target is him."
He spoke as the screen showed Nux’s face.
And then suddenly, a few more faces appeared beside Nux.
His wives.
"And them."
Eternity spoke

This time, we will confirm his strength and once we see the opportunity,
We will move next to him—together."
The Infinities nodded again.
None of them found anything wrong with it.
Was it shameful that four Infinities were going to act together to catch one child?
Well, the ’child’ wasn’t the threat here.
They needed to move together because the child’s superiors might be watching through the child.
They might be waiting to surround them the instant they arrive, and if that indeed happens, the Infinities wanted to stay together.
This was the only way they would have the highest chance of victory.
"We will also try to contact the Fifth Infinity."
Balance spoke.
This time, however, not everyone seemed to be on the same page as him.
"The Fifth Infinity?

It is clear he is with the enemy.
What are you trying to gain here?"
Darkness frowned.
"We are not sure that he is the enemy."
Balance shook his head.
"He protected him!
Wha—"
Darkness raised his voice.
"Only once."
Balance, however, interrupted him, and his words silenced Darkness for a moment.
Balance continued,
"The Fifth Infinity only protected him once.
After that, there were no signs of clear contact between the two.
It could be that the Anomaly did not need his help, but the possibility that the Fifth Infinity figured out the Anomaly’s secret and the two of them broke apart cannot be denied either.
If anything, the Fifth Infinity might be in danger or... he might be dead already."
Balance spoke with a grim look on his face, but then—
"That is not possible."
Eternity shook his head.
"There is no way the Universe wouldn’t have reacted strongly if the Fifth Infinity had died at the hands of the beings from another Universe.

"What if he was taken into their Univers—ah..."
Balance tried to give out another possibility.
Soon, however, he realized how the Universe would have reacted if that had happened and shook his head.
Eternity nodded at his words.

It is highly likely that he will become our ally.

chapters.title: Chapter 2131: Time for the Infinities to meet the Anomaly.
paragraphs: "Our target is him."
Eternity spoke as the screen he was controlling now stopped showing the fight between Nux and Zarveth and started showing Nux’s face instead.
Then suddenly, a few more faces appeared beside Nux’s.
They were his wives.
"And them."
Eternity spoke, pointing at the man and the women and the rest of the Infinities...
"Who are they?"
They questioned, curious.
Did they actually know more about these beings from another Universe than they were expecting?
This was definitely good news.
And while all of them were still wondering why Eternity did not show this before, for now, they did not question him.
Eternity, however, could sense what all of them were thinking and—
"They are the Leander Family."
He began.
"I had my subordinates look into Sharnoth Nocthys and while there were quite a few things odd about her, she is currently the sovereign of a High-Level World called Khaemorr.
When my men arrived at Khaemorr and captured their higher-ups, they found an interesting connection."
Eternity muttered in an amused tone.
"Connection?"
The Infinities frowned.
"Khaemorr was thought to be one of the stronger High-Level Worlds."
"If its leader is that girl, that is not a big deal."
Darkness shrugged.
The girl had the Body of Chaos. Even if it was incomplete, just the fact that she had some connection with Zylarith made this... quite insignificant.
Rather, it was quite embarrassing that Khaemorr, the world she led, wasn’t called one of the strongest High-Level Worlds instead.
Darkness could already sense how disappointed Zylarith would be in this situation.
Eternity and the other Infinities knew what he was thinking as well, and they all somewhat agreed with that line of thought.
Just that...

All of them knew that the girl couldn’t use her powers openly, she needed to disguise her Energy of Chaos into something else, so they could see how she would have to hold back, limiting the status of her world.
Not that any of this mattered—
Be it the strongest High-Level World or the weakest, it was all the same to the Infinities. They just stared at Eternity, waiting for him to continue, and Eternity did exactly what they wanted.

"From the reports I received, under that girl’s leadership, Khaemorr’s position has been quite stable in the Universe. They have good relationships with their allies, and the world only had one enemy—Aurendor.

Interestingly enough, Aurendor is also the world that destroyed the High-Level World named Nocthys a few years ago. The girl we are talking about is the Nocthys Princess—it isn’t difficult to see what she is trying to do."
"Why are you telling us all this?"
Darkness questioned with a yawn.
He had no interest in following the story of a little girl who had come back for revenge. He had heard so many of these stories that he was now sick of it.
Eternity didn’t react to Darkness’s question, he just continued. After all, he knew that even though Darkness was acting like this, he would still listen—
"A few days ago, something happened to the stable Khaemorr."
"What?"
Light questioned. Even she wanted Eternity to hurry up now.

"Their ally worlds started getting attacked and these weren’t simply assaults—the World Leaders were killed, leaving these worlds in such a weak state that their enemies’ worlds attacked, instantly ending the wars that have been going on for centuries.
This started happening more and more often, affecting Khaemorr’s image, portraying them as a world that does not know how to protect its surroundings.
The girl tried to do something about it—

But the enemy was full of tricks. It was impossible to track him. He knew where to attack, when to attack, he knew his target’s strengths and weaknesses, and every time he attacked, there was nothing left.
Nothing but the same sigil that proved this was all done by the same group.

Within just two weeks, Khaemorr’s stable situation completely turned around. Tens of worlds under their jurisdiction were destroyed in a similar way. Everything the girl did turned out to be useless. In the end, their allies started declaring their neutrality, not wanting to participate in war from Khaemorr’s side in fear of getting targeted like the other worlds were.

Khaemorr was now getting isolated, with more and more of their allies leaving their side—some even directly joined Khaemorr’s long-time enemy, Aurendor, severely weakening them and strengthening the enemies instead."
"That seems... quite frustrating..."
Balance muttered. He could see how even he would begin losing his mind if something similar happened to him.
"An enemy that cannot be detected, huh..."
He muttered, and soon, he realized something.
"That sounds quite familiar..."
Light muttered directly, and a single suspect appeared in every single Infinity’s mind.
"Who was this enemy?"
Balance questioned as he glanced at Eternity.
"It is the Mercenary Party named the Leander Family."
Eternity answered with a smile. It was clear he was already expecting this question.
"A Mercenary Party?"
Balance raised his eyebrow.
"My men were quite surprised about it when they first heard it. Usually, Mercenary Parties aren’t strong enough to put a High-Level World in such a desperate situation."
Eternity nodded.

"I then sent my men to Vael’Terros to learn more about the Leander Family, and as one would expect, they are quite the popular bunch. Almost all the Mercenary Worlds—even the ones who come from considerably far regions—have had missions assigned specifically for the Leander Family.
However, the interesting thing to note about the Leander Family is that none of the Mercenary World Leaders knew anything about that man.
When asked about the members of the Leander Family—"
Eternity then pointed at the women’s pictures on the screen and—
"Most of them only talked about the women."
"Does this mean the Anomaly is not part of the Leander Family?"
"No, he is part of the Leander Family."
Eternity shook his head.
"He just... doesn’t appear very often."
"So he has appeared before."
Light did not miss what Eternity was implying, and Eternity nodded.
"He has. Quite recently at that."
He spoke as suddenly, another being’s picture appeared on the screen.
"This is Vexarion Aurendor.
Recently, the representative of the Leander Family, Nux Leander, contacted him."
"Nux Leander?"
"That is how the Anomaly introduces himself."
"Nux Leander, huh..."
Darkness muttered, as if etching that name into his mind.
"What did he say to Aurendor?"
Balance questioned.
Rather than the name, he was more interested in knowing what the Anomaly was planning.
"He promised Vexarion a chance to have a one-on-one battle with Sharnoth Nocthys."
"Why would he want that?"
Light frowned.
She obviously knew who Vexarion was. After all, he belonged to her Faction, so even if she hadn’t directly met the man, she still knew he existed.
And of course, she also knew that in a one-on-one battle, he stood no chance against Zylarith’s Heir.

From her tone, it was clear that Light was against this battle. For some reason, she thought this to be a battle between hers and Zylarith’s heir, and in no Universe did she think a weakling like Vexarion could be considered her heir.
It was clearly unfair.
Eternity chuckled at her reaction, then he shook his head—
"He isn’t doing this because he wants to."
"Then why is he doing it?"
Light questioned, and Eternity—
"So what happened was..."

He began telling everything that happened so far—how Sharnoth issued a challenge, how the Anomaly enticed Vexarion into accepting the challenge and whatnot—and in an instant, the Infinities realized what the Anomaly wants.
"No wonder that girl acted like his subordinate."
Balance spoke lightly, as if a big mystery inside his head was solved.
"The Anomaly must have promised her revenge in return."
"To think Zylarith’s heir would need someone else to get her revenge—that too, on a mere leader of a High-Level World."
Darkness snorted.
But Balance—
"The relationship between Zylarith and his heir might not be as good as what we were expecting."
He muttered in a solemn tone.
"What...?"
Darkness narrowed his eyes, and Balance continued—
"We all know what sort of being Zylarith is. He plans to control his heir through the Body of Chaos. That girl must have realized it."
"So she sold out her Universe for her revenge."
Light frowned.
"These are hundred-thousand-year-old children we are talking about, Seraphielle. Letting their personal feelings get the best of them is extremely common at that age.
I wouldn’t be surprised if she promised the control of her entire body to the Anomaly for a lifetime once she gets her revenge."
Balance explained.
"Lifetime, huh...
These children don’t seem to realize how long... life is."
Light spoke in an inexplicable tone.
Balance didn’t comment anything on it.
His focus was somewhere else,
"It doesn’t matter.
For now, all we need to focus on is contacting the Fifth Eternity and capturing the Anomaly or any of the women associated with him.
As for how we are going to do it..."
Balance paused, his gaze falling on Vexarion Aurendor, and in an instant, the other three Infinities realized what he was thinking.
They now had a new bait.
A bait that had the highest chance of making the Anomaly move.
It was finally time for the Infinities to meet the Anomaly.

chapters.title: Chapter 2132: Intuition
paragraphs: "I-I am telling you, t-that is not me."
Sharnoth spoke for the nth time as the rest of the women surrounded her. In front of them, there was a huge screen that showed Sharnoth attacking Nux with a huge, almost perverted smile on her face.
"It definitely looks like you..."
Felberta spoke in a low, teasing voice, staring at the woman on the screen and the one hovering in front of her.
"Indeed, indeed, she looks drunk."
Shadow laughed, walking behind Sharnoth with a cheeky grin.
"I do not drink and that is not me."

Sharnoth repeated herself, staring at the woman who did not act the way she looked one bit. Rather than her, it looked like the woman had another personality inside her body that had now taken control over her body.
"Wow, you are that boring huh...
How can you live without a drink?"
Shadow shook her head, disappointed.

The rest of the women stared at her with flat looks on their faces. Every single one of them wanted to say that Shadow didn’t drink either but, in the end, knowing that they would only get a shameless answer and might even get Shadow to start drinking—they decided it was better to continue targeting the woman who was actually worth targeting.
"I wonder if you were doing this just to get Nux’s attention?"
Allura questioned with a playful smile on her face as she stared at Sharnoth. Sharnoth blinked at that question and replied instantaneously—
"Wha—No I did not do it to get his attention! Why would I want that!?"
"So you do admit it was you."
Allura grinned.
The rest of the women grinned as well, acting like predators who had finally caught their prey.
Sharnoth tried to defend herself from the group but then—
"You people sure are getting along."
Nux, who was finally done with dealing with everything, appeared with a grin on his face.
"You took your sweet time."
Shadow commented. As the Soul of the Universe, she saw Nux standing straight, staring at the void after reading Zarveth’s and Neremoth’s memories and turning them into his subordinates.
"I was... thinking."
Nux spoke in a low voice.
"About what?"
Shadow questioned, tilting her head in confusion.
Nux glanced at Sharnoth and before he could say anything, Amaya answered Shadow’s question with an expressionless look on her face.
"About Vexarion."
Nux glanced at Amaya and nodded grimly.
As for Sharnoth... her very attitude changed the moment she heard those words.
"What about him?"
She questioned, staring at Nux.

Usually, every time Nux talked about Vexarion, he looked confident. Even before, when he wasn’t strong enough to defeat him, with countless tricks up his sleeve, he could easily fool him into falling for his trap.

Not to mention, now he was powerful enough to take down two Eternal Level Supreme Borns who were incomparably more powerful than Vexarion. Someone like Vexarion shouldn’t even be a problem worth mentioning to him.
Then why...
Why did his expression look so grim?
Sharnoth couldn’t understand.
But Amaya was different.
"The Supreme Worlds..."
She began, the rest of the women turned towards her and with a solemn look on her face, she continued,
"The Supreme Worlds might protect him."
"I do not understand."
Sharnoth frowned.
"They do not have the reason to do that."
"They didn’t have a reason before everything that happened."
Amaya answered.
"What do you mean?"
Sharnoth’s frown deepened.
After all—

"They shouldn’t even know what happened here. The Eternal from the Supreme World of Eternity completely sealed the space around us. The rest of the Universe, including the Supreme Worlds, shouldn’t know what happened inside, else everything Zarveth did would be all for naught."
The woman muttered.
Amaya, however, shook her head.
"If that was the case, he wouldn’t be making that face."
She spoke as she glanced at Nux.
Sharnoth called out, turning towards Nux as well.
"...what happened?"
She asked.
"I am having a hard time believing that the Infinities did not know what happened. Now I do not have a way to prove what I say, but... my instincts are telling me something doesn’t add up here."
Nux answered honestly.
"What do you mean?"
Astaria questioned.

"I read Zarveth’s memories, I saw how the Infinities, despite being the so-called strongest beings in the Universe, erased their abilities, their faces, and even their names from their subordinates’ minds.
Both Zarveth and Neremoth knew nothing about the Infinities, the Infinities constantly manipulated their memories to make that happen, and both Eternals had no clue this was happening to them."
Nux explained.
Astaria tilted her head, confused.
This wasn’t the first time she had heard about something like this; many beings manipulated their subordinates’ memories.
What was the big deal?
"They are cautious.
Too cautious."
Nux spoke with a solemn look on his face.
"It is almost... unnatural.
It seems as if they are wary of something."
"What does this have to do with them knowing what happened here...?"
Sharnoth couldn’t understand; the rest of the women, including Amaya and Aeliana, had the same question in their minds.
And Nux...
He just shook his head.
"As I said... I have no way to prove my words.
It is all an intuition, really.

I am... having a difficult time believing that all-powerful beings who would go out of their way to make sure their subordinates have no memory of them, would purposefully let a subordinate have a way to hide things from them.
Do not forget, these are the same beings that keep an eye on the entirety of the Universe through their relics, I confirmed that from Zarveth’s memories.
Do you truly believe that the Infinity Relics he used in the battle won’t have a function that reports everything back to Eternity’s Infinity?"
Nux questioned and for a moment, the women turned silent.
Nux, on the other hand, stared at Sharnoth and continued.
"My face may not be well known, but if the Infinities saw your face, they will connect it to Khaemorr, Aurendor and your connection with the Leander Family.
If that is truly the case,
Then it wouldn’t be difficult to narrow down our next target to... pretty much just Vexarion.
They would be fools if they did not make any preparations for that."

Someone like Vexarion shouldn’t even be a problem worth mentioning to him.
Then why...
Why did his expression look so grim?
Sharnoth couldn’t understand.
But Amaya was different.
"The Supreme Worlds..."
She began, the rest of the women turned towards her and with a solemn look on her face, she continued,
"The Supreme Worlds might protect him."
"I do not understand."
Sharnoth frowned.
"They do not have the reason to do that."
"They didn’t have a reason before everything that happened."
Amaya answered.
"What do you mean?"
Sharnoth’s frown deepened.
After all—
"They shouldn’t even know what happened here.
The Eternal from the Supreme World of Eternity completely sealed the space around us.
The rest of the Universe, including the Supreme Worlds, shouldn’t know what happened inside, else everything Zarveth did would be all for naught."
The woman muttered.
Amaya, however, shook her head.
"If that was the case, he wouldn’t be making that face."
She spoke as she glanced at Nux.
Sharnoth called out, turning towards Nux as well.
"...what happened?"
She asked.
"I am having a hard time believing that the Infinities did not know what happened.
Now I do not have a way to prove what I say, but... my instincts are telling me something doesn’t add up here."
Nux answered honestly.
"What do you mean?"
Astaria questioned.

"I read Zarveth’s memories, I saw how the Infinities, despite being the so-called strongest beings in the Universe, erased their abilities, their faces, and even their names from their subordinates’ minds.
Both Zarveth and Neremoth knew nothing about the Infinities, the Infinities constantly manipulated their memories to make that happen, and both Eternals had no clue this was happening to them."
Nux explained.
Astaria tilted her head, confused.
This wasn’t the first time she had heard about something like this; many beings manipulated their subordinates’ memories.
What was the big deal?
"They are cautious.
Too cautious."
Nux spoke with a solemn look on his face.
"It is almost... unnatural.
It seems as if they are wary of something."
"What does this have to do with them knowing what happened here...?"
Sharnoth couldn’t understand; the rest of the women, including Amaya and Aeliana, had the same question in their minds.
And Nux...
He just shook his head.
"As I said...
I have no way to prove my words.
It is all an intuition, really.

I am... having a difficult time believing that all-powerful beings who would go out of their way to make sure their subordinates have no memory of them, would purposefully let a subordinate have a way to hide things from them.
Do not forget, these are the same beings that keep an eye on the entirety of the Universe through their relics, I confirmed that from Zarveth’s memories.
Do you truly believe that the Infinity Relics he used in the battle won’t have a function that reports everything back to Eternity’s Infinity?"
Nux questioned and for a moment, the women turned silent.
Nux, on the other hand, stared at Sharnoth and continued.
"My face may not be well known, but if the Infinities saw your face, they will connect it to Khaemorr, Aurendor and your connection with the Leander Family.
If that is truly the case,
Then it wouldn’t be difficult to narrow down our next target to... pretty much just Vexarion.
They would be fools if they did not make any preparations for that."

chapters.title: Chapter 2133: Do we... let Vexarion go?
