If that is truly the case,
Then it wouldn’t be difficult to narrow down our next target to... pretty much just Vexarion.
They would be fools if they do not make any preparations for that."
Nux explained and Sharnoth’s face turned grim as well. Soon however, the woman frowned and—
"But if they saw everything...
Why didn’t they make a move?"
She questioned, staring at Nux.
"If they already saw us, why wait till we attack Vexarion and ambush us? I am an Eternal and you are...
Well, whatever you are, you definitely aren’t stronger than the Infinities.
Then why didn’t they attack us directly?"
"I do not know."
Nux shook his head.

This was one of the reasons he said it was just his intuition. He had next to no information about the Infinities, so everything they said and discussed here was just theories they could come up with.

While Sharnoth’s question still made sense, disproving Nux’s theory, Nux still found it hard to believe that the Infinities who would go as far as manipulating their subordinates’ memories and had the habit of keeping an eye on all major powers in the Universe through their Relics, wouldn’t have a way to keep an eye on their closest subordinates.
"What if... they cannot leave their Worlds either?"
Suddenly, Aeliana muttered in a low voice, attracting everyone’s attention.
The Vampire looked into Nux’s eyes and—
"You have memories of billions and billions of year-old worlds and yet never once did you mention the appearance of the Infinities.
All these people are at the same level as Father, are they not?
Then what if... they are in a situation similar to what he was in before?"
"Father...?"
Hearing her words, Sharnoth tilted her head, confused.
Father?
Whose Father?
Who was she talking about?
Seeing her strange reaction, the rest of the people realized it.
"Ah, you don’t know huh..."
Skyla muttered in an understanding tone, patting Sharnoth’s shoulders lightly, as if telling her that she was there for her.
Of course, her actions and words only confused Sharnoth even further.
"She is talking about her Father, my Father-in-law, Azriel Ruinous, one of the Progenitors of the World we come from."
Nux explained and as Sharnoth glanced at him, he continued,
"You can think of him to be Zylarith’s successor.
He is the Fifth Infinity of the Universe, well, at least he once was."
Nux spoke those last words with a shrug.
"The Fifth Infinity...?"
Sharnoth’s expression changed.

Of course, as someone who had Zylarith as her Teacher, she wasn’t clueless regarding the way the Universe worked. She knew that unlike what the rest of the Universe believed, there were once Five Supreme Worlds, meaning there should be Five Infinity-level beings instead of four.

But after Zylarith’s death, the Fifth Infinity never appeared. Sharnoth asked about the Fifth Infinity and the possibility of his existence many times, but every time, Zylarith shook his head, telling her how he was a ’Soul’ of the Fifth Infinity and unless he returned to the Universe, the Universe could not give birth to another Infinity.
"And what do you mean ’he once was?’"
The woman questioned, her frown turning deeper.
"He was chosen by the Universe and freed from his world—"
Soon, Nux shook his head.
"It is a long story, we will talk about it later, just know that he is currently not as strong as he used to be."
Nux then turned towards Aeliana and shook his head again,
"Although what you said is possible, the situation with Father-in-law was far more complex considering Yrniel made too many mistakes and Father-in-law had to pay for those.
I do not think the Supreme Worlds made the same mistake, so at the very least, the situation isn’t exactly the same.
As for whether the Infinities could leave their Worlds or not...
It is too big of an assumption to make considering the information we have."
Amaya nodded as well.
"That is correct.
Do not forget that these Infinities fought against Zylarith at a time, that fight wouldn’t be possible if they couldn’t leave their Worlds.
Although there is a chance that something happened after or during that fight.
Another much more likely scenario would be that the Infinities never appeared before because they simply never needed to."
Amaya slowly turned towards Aeliana and—
"The Infinities are Absolute in the Universe, their Words are Laws, their subordinates hold immense power simply by being their subordinates.
Their wills are announced by their subordinates, and no one dares to go against it, no one dares to stand up to them either,
And in the past billions and billions of years, there has never been a being capable enough to challenge the Infinities.
They had literally no reason to show themselves."
"They do now."
Aeliana answered back and she was correct.
The Infinities indeed had a reason to act now, after all, they were the only beings who could stop the current Nux.
"They do."
Amaya nodded at the Vampire’s words.
"And this is why we should be careful.
They will be after us."
The Devourer spoke with a grim look on her face.
"They could have ended us without us having a chance to be careful,
They had the chance."
Sharnoth repeated her words and the Devourer just turned towards her and shrugged,
"Maybe they were being careful as well.
Maybe sending Zarveth and Neremoth was a test.
To see how strong the Anomaly actually was.
And now that they know the truth..."
Amaya didn’t continue.
She didn’t have to.
The women understood it.
Sure, Nux was strong, but now that the Infinities knew how strong he actually was, they would most probably make their move now.
After all, even they must feel threatened by a being who grew from running away from them to being able to toy around with an Eternal, in front of their very eyes.
What do we do now...?"
Sharnoth questioned in a low voice.
"Do we... let Vexarion go?"
She asked, clenching her fists in frustration.

chapters.title: Chapter 2134: My dear Father-in-law, where is he?
paragraphs: What do we do now...?
Do we... let Vexarion go?"
Sharnoth questioned in a low voice, her fists trembling in frustration and helplessness.
As much as she wanted her revenge, she wasn’t foolish enough to charge right in when she knew that all this might be a trap set by their enemies in order to catch her.

If she were alone, it was a different scenario. This was the same woman who pretty much sold herself to another being just for the sake of her revenge. Even if she knew it was all a trap, if there was even a sliver of a chance of her getting her revenge, she would go in.
But now, things were different.
She was no longer alone.
She now had someone who was prepared to help her, someone who went against the Supreme Worlds for her sake.
She...
She wasn’t shameless enough to ask this person to risk not just his but his entire family’s life for her sake.
She couldn’t possibly ask him to walk into a trap knowingly.
Thinking all that, Sharnoth prepared herself, forcefully calming her feelings and suppressing her vengeful thoughts.
She had waited for a hundred thousand years, she could wait longer, for billions, trillions of years if she had to.
But...
Nux’s answer was different than what she was expecting.
"Of course not."
The man shook his head.
"I promised you revenge and I will fulfill that promise."
"But you just said this might be a trap set by the Infinities."
Sharnoth answered. She then looked into his eyes and with a solemn look on her face—
"Nux, don’t be foolish.
Infinities are different from beings you have faced before,
They are...
There is a reason they have Absolute Authority in the entirety of the Universe."
The Heir of Chaos spoke, turning towards Nux’s wives and—
"Say something."
She urged, wanting a little support.
The wives, however, were a little taken aback.
Yes, Nux’s words didn’t exactly surprise them, they all knew Nux wouldn’t go back on his words, his pride wouldn’t allow him to.
But...
His love for them was far higher than his pride.
This was the man who would turn the entire Universe around for the sake of his wives.
So willingly walking into a trap set up by Infinities was definitely not something he would normally do, after all, this very act would put the wives he cherished in danger.
So...
What was he planning?
The women wondered.
"I have no intention of endangering myself, don’t worry."
Nux shook his head, trying to calm Sharnoth.
But—
"You are going against Infinities."
She countered.
"My target is only an Eternal."
Nux answered.
"Only an Eternal..."
Vyriana repeated those words with an empty smile on her face.
To think this man would not even put Eternal Level beings in his eyes.
Of course, she knew this was going to happen one day. Considering the monster’s potential, it was obvious it was going to happen but...
To think it would happen so quickly.
’Would I stand a chance against him in a fight...?’
For a moment, the Dragon wondered in her head, but very quickly, she abandoned that thought.
It was impossible.
Yes, she was a Transcendent as well but...
Nux was...
He was something... much different.
The way he played around with Zarveth while holding a crazy Sharnoth with one hand was more than enough to prove it.
They weren’t in the same league.
They never were.
In the end, the Dragon shook her head again, getting all these thoughts out and focusing on the conversation.
"An Eternal protected by Infinities."
Sharnoth retorted.
"Trust me, I have plans of facing Infinities.
I know my limits,
I might be strong, but I will not foolishly test my strength against Infinities."
Nux shook his head.
He didn’t say he would lose because honestly... he did not know.
With him now being able to use his complete strength after using his Domain, he wasn’t sure if an Infinity could actually defeat him.
But...

Infinities were tricky opponents and he had next to no information about them. Facing them just to test his current strength was foolish, especially when this action could put his wives’ lives at risk.
"Nux, what are you thinking?"
Melia questioned directly.
"I am still not sure, but I might have a way."
Nux began.
"What does that mean?"
Sharnoth asked.
"We need outside help to confirm it."
"Who is going to help us?"

The Heir of Chaos asked another question. She was one hundred percent sure that her people back in Khaemorr were currently under the Supreme Worlds’ scrutiny, plus, they weren’t exactly strong enough to help them.
"Well, there are people."
Nux chuckled as he then contacted someone who might be able to help them.
’Mother.’
He called out using their connection.

’Nux? Are you alright? The Universe just reacted and this time, it is much angrier than before? What did you do? Are you in the Main Universe? I have been trying to contact you, but I couldn’t. I couldn’t enter your Universe either, something restricted me. What happened? Is everything alright? Where are yo—’
Faustina replied instantly, asking a series of questions without taking a single breath. It was clear that the woman was worried, and she had all rights to be.
’Mother, I am fine.
Calm down.’
Nux answered in a low voice, interrupting her in the middle of her words.
’Where are you?’
Faustina questioned in a tone that made it clear that she needed an instant, direct answer.
’I am in my Universe. You couldn’t enter the Universe because it was undergoing some changes, it is all done now, I have released the entry restrictions, you can return anytime you want to.’
Nux explained.
’As for what happened, I will tell you everything later, but right now, I need your help.’
He spoke in an urgent voice and very quickly, Faustina’s tone changed.
’What do you need?’
’My dear Father-in-law, where is he?’
Nux questioned with a playful smile.
’Where else?
He is cultivating, as always.’
Faustina answered with a flat, bored sigh. It was clear that she was already used to this sight of Azriel cultivating, too used in fact.
’I need to talk to him.’

chapters.title: Chapter 2135: What? It is a genuine question, okay?
paragraphs: ’Where else?
He is cultivating, as always.’
Faustina answered with a flat, bored tone. It was clear that she was already used to this sight of Azriel cultivating, too used in fact.
’I need to talk to him.’
Nux requested.
’Is everything alright?’
Faustina questioned; her concern was clear.
’Ah yes, I just needed his help with something.’
Nux answered calmly. He knew Faustina wanted to ask many questions but was holding herself back, and he appreciated it.
His mother was indeed the best.
’Mm, I will tell him to call you.’
Faustina nodded, her words, however, made Nux frown.
’Call? Mother, we cannot do that.’
He spoke with a slightly confused look on his face; after all, Faustina should already know about it.

His Father-in-law was the Universe’s Child, the Universe constantly kept an eye on him. He couldn’t directly get in contact with him or else the Universe might find out about the connection between its Child and the Anomaly.
This was also the reason that every time they talked, Faustina or other Progenitors became the mediator.
Did his mother forget about this?
It was difficult to believe; after all, at Faustina’s level, forgetting something was... difficult. Their minds even remembered the smallest details, let alone something as important as this.
’Ah, we now can.’
Soon however, Nux heard Faustina’s voice. His frown deepened, but before he could even ask anything else,
Bzzz
His Call Artifact buzzed, instantly freezing him.
It was Azriel.
Nux slowly stared at Aeliana, who seemed to have the same questions in her mind as him, but in the end, she trusted her father and nodded at Nux.
Nux accepted the call and a screen showing Azriel’s face appeared in front of him.
[What is it?]
Azriel questioned.

His tone had the same annoyance he usually had. After all, he was talking to the bastard who took away his daughter. Never in his life would he actually like the guy even if he had already accepted him as his son-in-law.
"F-Father-in-law."
Nux greeted, a little taken aback.
It wasn’t just him; the rest of the women around him were taken aback by the sudden call as well, especially Sharnoth.
This was her first time seeing Azriel, and she felt a strangely overwhelming sensation inside her.
The Fifth Infinity...
A being who could be called her Master Zylarith’s successor.
What kind of being was he?
Was he... as strong as Zylarith was when he was at his strongest?
Also, Nux said he was no longer the Fifth Infinity and was chosen by the Universe itself. What did that mean?
All these questions appeared in her head.
She also couldn’t help but notice how nervous Nux seemed when he was talking to this man. This was probably the first time she had seen him act in such a manner.
Was it because he was talking to his Father-in-law and did it out of respect?
Or was it... because of the man he was talking to?
While she was thinking all this, Azriel’s eyes fell on her, making her flinch and then—
[Another one?]
He spoke directly.
"I-It is not certain yet..."
Nux answered, making the rest of his wives roll their eyes.
Azriel too, stared at the man with a deadpan look on his face. He then glanced at Shadow and—
[And why does she look like that?]
"Do you like how I look now?"
Shadow turned around in a playful manner; her words made the other women flinch.
"Come on, people, why are you all so nervous? He is inside an entirely different Universe. We don’t even know how far he actually is.
What could he possibly do from that far?"
The woman shook her head, and the rest of the women didn’t dare to say anything.
Shadow was probably the only one who could act like this in front of Azriel. Well, the fact that she hadn’t actually met him face to face must have had something to do with it as well.
Azriel ignored the woman and stared at Nux.
"Things happened."
Nux answered ambiguously; he knew Azriel wasn’t interested in details. He could see it on the man’s face.
And just as he thought,
"Alright."
Azriel just nodded and then—
[You better tell everything in detail to your mother later. She has been fidgeting around because of all her worries; I am having a hard time cultivating.]
[You—shut your mout—]

Hearing those words, Faustina did try to jump at Azriel, wanting to silence him, but the man waved his hand and appeared somewhere else, dodging the advance of a Primordial without any effort whatsoever—something that Nux didn’t fail to notice.
"Father-in-law...
How strong are you now?"
He questioned in a low voice.
[Transcendent.]
Azriel answered, and the first to react to those words was—
"Already!?"
Vyriana.
Azriel turned towards her and—
[Yes, I am once again stronger than you, Dragon.]
"We do not know that for certain."
Vyriana’s answer was instantaneous.
But—
[I do.]
Azriel replied with absolute certainty, certainty that silenced every single person present here.

Even Vyriana couldn’t say anything; after all, deep down, she knew it as well. Against a being who was once hailed as the strongest in all the Universe, she wouldn’t stand a chance, even if they were on the same level.
"Father, should you be talking to us so openly?"
Suddenly, Aeliana questioned.
She didn’t care much about her Father’s strength; she knew her Father would soon be at the level he was before and get even stronger from there.

What worried her more was him being targeted by the Universe. After all, because of their connection, the Universe could now track him no matter where he went. If it sensed that he was actually in cahoots with its enemies...
It wouldn’t end well.
[I am inside my Domain, Lia.
You don’t have to worry, I am perfectly fine.]
Azriel answered with a gentle smile.
"Tsk, he is so different when he talks to her."
Shadow complained.
"It is almost as if we are talking to two different people."
Then suddenly, as if she thought of something, her eyes shimmered, and she glanced at Azriel,
"Lord Azriel, are you sure you don’t have another personality inside you as well?
We have been seeing a rise in such cases these days."
She spoke and, in an instant, the entire area turned silent.
Even Nux was staring at his wife, speechless.
And Shadow—
"What?
It is a genuine question, okay?
Swear on Nux’s life that you guys don’t feel the same!"

chapters.title: Chapter 2136: What do you say, Father-in-law?
paragraphs: "What?
It is a genuine question, okay?
Swear on Nux’s life that you guys don’t feel the same!"
Shadow raised her voice as she looked around, staring at every single one of the women around her, hoping to get support from even one of them.
But it was hopeless. The women very quickly turned their heads away the instant they sensed her gaze, even Lane, whom Shadow considered to be her closest ally after Nux, did the same.
"Lane... you too...?"
Shadow blinked in surprise. Lane, however, didn’t turn back and just continued to stare at an empty space.
Shadow’s mouth twitched at that reaction and then—
"You do realize most of my thoughts are formed because of your influence, correct?
These aren’t just my thoughts, they are yours too!"
She shifted the blame.
"...you are now capable of having independent thoughts."
Lane answered in a low voice and Shadow pointed her trembling fingers at every one of her sisters,
"Cowards! You are all cowards!"
She raised her head.
As for Azriel—
[This one has gotten braver.]
He commented as he stared at Shadow with his usual expressionless face.
For a moment, his gaze made Shadow flinch; soon, however, she manipulated the Space Law and appeared behind Nux.
"Yes! I am not scared of you! My husband is stronger than you!"
She retorted, looking directly into the Vampire’s eyes with a look of defiance on her face. To get some more self-confidence, she tightly held the corner of Nux’s shirt, an act that made Nux chuckle.
He slowly placed his hand on the woman’s waist and pulled her close,
"Alright, that is enough."
He spoke in a calm voice.
"What? I am not lying.
Don’t think I don’t know what you are thinking, my connection to you is stronger than theirs."
Shadow answered, eyeing the rest of the women provocatively when she said those words.
For a moment, Nux turned silent. He slowly stared at Azriel and then—
He grinned.
Azriel stared back without any change in his expression; even the Vampire knew what the brat was thinking, after all, he had spent quite some time observing him.
Obviously, Nux couldn’t care less about his cultivation regressing. Even when Azriel became a mortal, Nux never once showed him any disrespect.
He wasn’t like that.
Azriel was one of the few people Nux truly respected; he would never stoop so low as to compare himself to a weakened Azriel.
Right now, however, things were different.
Azriel was no longer a weakened mortal; sure, he was still far, far weaker than when he was at his prime, however...
Right now, Azriel was technically on the same level as Nux.
This was the reason Nux was grinning like a madman.
He wanted a fight.
The fighting spirit that first Astaria and then Vyriana instilled into him was now burning far more strongly than it ever had.
After all, this was his chance.
The chance to face the man he respected the most on a fair level.
Because of their connection, Shadow sensed his strong fighting spirit as well; it flickered the moment Azriel said he was now a Transcendent and never calmed down after that.
This was also the partial reason she was acting out.
"What do you say, Father-in-law?"
Nux took his chance, his golden eyes shining with a fierce light. His grinning face now resembled a madman who could no longer hold himself back.

"If your Domain can truly block the Universe’s senses, then how about we have a go at it? I am sure you’re itching to have a good fight after all this while as well, aren’t you? I doubt the Progenitors are giving you much of a challenge now."
[Oi, you brat! What did you say!? You dare say it to my face!?]
The instant Nux said those words, another angry face appeared on the screen. It was Dagahra, the Dragon Progenitor.
[Tone it down, Daga. It’s not like he is wrong; you were defeated in a single punch when Azriel was only a Primordial. You are no match for him now.]
Another, much calmer voice was heard.
It was Saphira, the second Dragon Progenitor.
[Hah!? It’s not like you were any better!]
Dagahra retorted, but Saphira simply shrugged in a light voice,
[I am not the one shoving my face in front of the Call Artifact.]
The woman then stared at her husband and—
[Also, stop threatening Nux like a thug. You should be able to get some sense as to how strong he has gotten; your threats wouldn’t even faze him.]
Saphira was ruthless.
Very quickly, Dagahra’s expression changed; it hurt even more when he knew his wife was correct.
[Monsters...]
He cursed out loud as he glared at Nux and then Azriel, then he moved away from the screen. Azriel’s face, which was no longer covered by Dagahra, remained neutral.
He was already used to the guy’s antics, so it didn’t even faze him now.
His eyes remained on Nux; unlike the brat, who was full of fighting spirit, he was much calmer. However, it was an offer he couldn’t just refuse.
Even he wanted to hit the brat a little, and he was curious about how strong Nux actually was since he could no longer read him like he used to.
But...
[You might get hurt, boy.]
He warned, but his words only made Nux’s grin wider.
"You sound confident."
[I should be the one saying that.]
Azriel spoke as if it were the most obvious thing in the Universe.
He wasn’t the challenger here; he was the champion who was being challenged.
"Alright then, let’s do it."
Nux agreed instantaneously.
"I am coming there right now."
He declared as he prepared to appear from Faustina’s shadow,
But then—
[Shouldn’t you first talk about the reason you called me in the first place? I thought it was quite urgent considering the way your mother came to me.]
Azriel spoke and Nux momentarily froze.
He...
He may have forgotten about it in his excitement...
"R-Right, let’s do that first..."
He nodded with a light cough, not daring to look into Sharnoth’s eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 2137: What are you thinking, Nux Leander?
paragraphs: [Shouldn’t you first talk about the reason you called me in the first place? I thought it was quite urgent considering the way your mother came to me.]
"R-Right, let’s do that first..."
Nux nodded with a light cough, not daring to look into Sharnoth’s eyes.
The woman in question, however, had completely zoned out.

At first, although she was overwhelmed by Azriel’s presence, it wasn’t that big of a deal since she was literally raised by one of the strongest beings in the entirety of the Universe. Not to mention, just like Shadow said, Azriel himself was in a completely different Universe; there was only so much he could do from that far away.
So yes, Sharnoth was overwhelmed, but it wasn’t to the point of intimidation or her completely zoning out.
Things, however, changed when Azriel used the words "your mother." Sharnoth’s ears perked up the instant she heard those words, even more so when she heard a woman’s voice.

Because Azriel dodged Faustina’s jump and moved away from her, Sharnoth wasn’t able to see her face, but realizing that Nux’s mother was on the other side of the screen and listening to their conversation, for some reason, made her extremely nervous.

It was something she couldn’t understand. She had absolutely no idea why she was feeling the way she was, but something inside her screamed at her, telling her to go look for a mirror and make sure she looked her very best.
All this time, Sharnoth had been fighting the urge to disappear from the group. She had absolutely no idea how the conversation had continued after it.
[So what do you want?]
Azriel, too, ignored Nux’s usual antics and quickly jumped to the main topic.
"I need an outsider’s perspective. I didn’t know who to contact, so I contacted you."
[An outsider’s perspective?]
The Vampire raised his eyebrows.
"That is correct."
Nux nodded and Azriel waited for him to explain.
"Mother said the Universe reacted again and it seemed angrier than before. Do you know why it happened?"
[You must have done something.]
Azriel was already used to the Universe’s tantrums, so in his case, all these tantrums came in one ear and went out the other.
"Of course I did something, but what? Why was the Universe angrier than normal?"
[Why are you asking me? Shouldn’t you be the one telling me that?]
"I... I do not completely understand it either."
Nux answered in an uncertain tone.
"This is why I needed an outsider’s perspective; I do not completely understand how my Power works."
[That is an odd thing to say.]
Azriel commented.
In the Universe where one had to comprehend the power before being able to use it, to say they do not understand the power they are using was indeed... odd.
But...
"It is not that simple, okay?
I have built an entirely different Universe here and have now somehow found a way to use its influence outside of... the said Universe."
Nux explained and Azriel very quickly narrowed his eyes. Not just him, even the rest of the women frowned, trying to understand what Nux just said.
In a way, it seemed like a paradox, something that shouldn’t be happening. Even Shadow was confused. After all, how could the Soul of the Universe understand something even the very Universe did not?
[Have you completed your Universe already?]
Azriel questioned, trying to understand everything from his perspective.
"Yes."
Nux answered his question.
[And you have broken through the Transcendent Stage?]
"Something like that."
Nux nodded again and, thinking that his answer wasn’t enough, he began explaining,
"I no longer follow a normal Cultivation Bridge. As you know, I am a Universe, so my bridge is—"
[You do not have to explain it. I am not a Universe; I would not understand anyway.]
Azriel quickly shook his hand dismissively.
Nux turned silent and then—
[This Power you just mentioned, a way to use your Universe’s influence outside of... your Universe, is this something similar to your Domain?]
Azriel questioned and in an instant, Nux’s eyes brightened up.
"Yes, exactly that! I knew you would understand!"
[So what outside perspective do you need for your Domain?]
Azriel asked directly, completely ignoring Nux’s sudden outburst.
"I need to understand what kind of influence my Domain has in the Main Universe."
Nux began, looking into Azriel’s eyes with a serious look on his face.
"My Domain is something like an extension of my Universe; it allows me to exert my influence to its fullest extent, just as I do when I am inside my Universe, despite not being inside my Universe."
[So your Domain allows you to be as strong as you are in your own Universe, without being inside your own Influence.]
"That is correct."
Nux nodded.
[That is quite a powerful Domain.]

Azriel nodded. He had heard about Nux’s situation. He had heard how almost all of his strength was suppressed because he was no longer part of the Main Universe, so if his Domain nullifies that effect, then Azriel was looking forward to seeing how strong Nux actually was.
"It is."
Nux nodded at those words. His Domain allowed him to defeat two of the strongest Eternals in the Universe, so of course it was strong.
Just that—
"I just do not understand what my Domain actually is.
I say it is an extension of my Universe, but it isn’t exactly my Universe either. If anything, it would be closer to an... extremely similar copy of a part of my Universe."
Nux tried to explain everything in words, which was extremely difficult since he knew not many here would be able to understand him, but he had no other choice.
He didn’t have any other Universes to talk to.
"Basically, I do not know what my Domain is.
Is it a part of my Universe? Or is it still a part of the Main Universe but has become something I altered to how I want it to be?
This is what I want to know."
[And why do you want to know this? And why so urgently that you had to call me?]
The Vampire then narrowed his eyes and—
[What are you thinking, Nux Leander?]
He questioned and Nux—
"I plan to slap the faces of the Infinities, the so-called Masters of the Universe."
He grinned.

Azriel was already used to the Universe’s tantrums, so in his case, all these tantrums came in one ear and went out the other.
"Of course I did something, but what?
Why was the Universe angrier than normal?"
[Why are you asking me?
Shouldn’t you be the one telling me that?]
I do not completely understand it either."
Nux answered in an uncertain tone.
"This is why I needed an outsider’s perspective; I do not completely understand how my Power works."
[That is an odd thing to say.]
Azriel commented.
In the Universe where one had to comprehend the power before being able to use it, to say they do not understand the power they are using was indeed... odd.
But...
"It is not that simple, okay?
I have built an entirely different Universe here and have now somehow found a way to use its influence outside of... the said Universe."
Nux explained and Azriel very quickly narrowed his eyes.
Not just him, even the rest of the women frowned, trying to understand what Nux just said.
In a way, it seemed like a paradox, something that shouldn’t be happening.
Even Shadow was confused.
After all, how could the Soul of the Universe understand something even the very Universe did not?
[Have you completed your Universe already?]
Azriel questioned, trying to understand everything from his perspective.
"Yes."
Nux answered his question.
[And you have broken through the Transcendent Stage?]
"Something like that."
Nux nodded again and, thinking that his answer wasn’t enough, he began explaining,
"I no longer follow a normal Cultivation Bridge.
As you know, I am a Universe, so my bridge is—"
[You do not have to explain it.
I am not a Universe; I would not understand anyway.]
Azriel quickly shook his hand dismissively.
Nux turned silent and then—
[This Power you just mentioned, a way to use your Universe’s influence outside of... your Universe, is this something similar to your Domain?]
Azriel questioned and in an instant, Nux’s eyes brightened up.
"Yes, exactly that!
I knew you would understand!"
[So what outside perspective do you need for your Domain?]
Azriel asked directly, completely ignoring Nux’s sudden outburst.
"I need to understand what kind of influence my Domain has in the Main Universe."
Nux began, looking into Azriel’s eyes with a serious look on his face.
"My Domain is something like an extension of my Universe; it allows me to exert my influence to its fullest extent, just as I do when I am inside my Universe, despite not being inside my Universe."
[So your Domain allows you to be as strong as you are in your own Universe, without being inside your own Influence.]
"That is correct."
Nux nodded.
[That is quite a powerful Domain.]
Azriel nodded.
He had heard about Nux’s situation.

He had heard how almost all of his strength was suppressed because he was no longer part of the Main Universe, so if his Domain nullifies that effect, then Azriel was looking forward to seeing how strong Nux actually was.
"It is."
Nux nodded at those words.
His Domain allowed him to defeat two of the strongest Eternals in the Universe, so of course it was strong.
Just that—
"I just do not understand what my Domain actually is.
I say it is an extension of my Universe, but it isn’t exactly my Universe either.
If anything, it would be closer to an... extremely similar copy of a part of my Universe."
Nux tried to explain everything in words, which was extremely difficult since he knew not many here would be able to understand him, but he had no other choice.
He didn’t have any other Universes to talk to.
"Basically, I do not know what my Domain is.
Is it a part of my Universe?
Or is it still a part of the Main Universe but has become something I altered to how I want it to be?
This is what I want to know."
[And why do you want to know this?
And why so urgently that you had to call me?]
The Vampire then narrowed his eyes and—
[What are you thinking, Nux Leander?]
He questioned and Nux—
"I plan to slap the faces of the Infinities, the so-called Masters of the Universe."
He grinned.

chapters.title: Chapter 2138: Yes, Infinities are that strong.
paragraphs: [What are you thinking, Nux Leander?]
Azriel questioned directly, his instincts warned him that he wasn’t going to like where this was going.
And hearing those words—
"I plan to slap the faces of the Infinities, the so-called Masters of the Universe."
Nux grinned and in an instant, Azriel’s face dropped.
[Have you lost your mind...?]
He asked with a flat look on his face, as if he was done with the brat’s antics. Then with a solemn look on his face,
[Do not let your Power get into your head, Nux.
It doesn’t matter how strong you are or how your domain makes you even stronger,
You cannot win against Infinities.]
Azriel spoke.
And as a previous Infinity, his words meant something.
"Why do you say that...?"
Nux questioned in a low voice, even if he had no plans of directly facing Infinities, his Father-in-law was acting like that felt... strange.
It felt as if he was missing something—
"If I use my Domain, I will be as strong as a High-Level World, stronger actually, considering I don’t just have Umbrasol in my Universe.
Shouldn’t I have some chance against Infinities?
What if instead of facing all four of them, I face just one of them? The weakest of them, let’s say... uhh... Eternity.
What if I face Eternity’s Infinity in a fair, one-on-one battle?"
Nux asked.
[It will be a one-sided loss.]
Azriel answered without a pause.
It almost felt like he was saying this just so Nux would throw out whatever plan he had out of his mind.
"Even though I am as strong as a High-Level World...?"
Nux asked. For some reason, he was having a hard time believing Azriel’s words. Sure, he wasn’t foolish enough to actually fight Infinities when he wasn’t sure of how strong they were, but...
He truly believed he now held a chance against them.
Yes, he was that strong now.
But...
[It doesn’t matter, Nux.]
Azriel shook his head again, his expression didn’t change.
[Even if you devour a few more High-Level Worlds, it wouldn’t make a difference.]
He explained.
"Why is that?"
Nux questioned, his frown deepening. Not just him, his wives had the same reactions, even the other progenitors who were hearing Azriel’s words seemed a little taken aback.
Everyone waited for Azriel to explain and finally, the Vampire began with a sigh,
[When it comes to Infinities, things change.
Other levels depend on Phase, the Universe has set itself in a way that the difference in Phase is absolute, no entity is an exception to that.
However, this does not apply to us.
I am the Universe’s child, I can use its power to strengthen myself and defeat my enemies, Cultivation Phases no longer matter to me.
As for you, well, you are not even a part of the Main Universe, its restriction simply does not matter to you.
However,
When it comes to Infinities, things change.]
The Vampire took a brief pause, looking at Nux to make sure he was listening and understanding his words.
Nux nodded, signaling him to continue.
[For Infinities, things aren’t just about the difference in Phases.
Infinities are not stronger than Eternals because they are a Phase higher, while that is indeed part of the reason,
In truth, even if the restriction of Phase was removed, Eternals would never be able to get close to Infinities.]
Nux frowned at those words, a little confused. He still didn’t understand the Main Universe as well as Azriel did, so his words were somewhat confusing.
Azriel realized it as well. This was also the reason he never bothered to explain it before, he knew the boy wouldn’t be able to understand it.

But seeing as to how the boy reacted, Azriel knew he needed to say something right now, even if he had to twist a few explanations in a way that they weren’t essentially incorrect, but weren’t incorrect either.
[Think of it like this.]
Azriel began.
[Infinities are essentially the Universe’s strongest creations after the Supreme Worlds, basically, they are the Universe’s Protectors.
If you compare it in terms of strength,
Infinities are much stronger than High-Level Worlds.]
"What...?"
Nux’s expression changed.
A single being stronger than an entire World? That too, a High-Level World?
This didn’t make sense, it didn’t follow the usual pattern.
Take an Eternal for example,

An Eternal is nowhere close to being stronger than even a Lowest-Level World. Sure, an Eternal can definitely destroy a Lowest-Level World, but that is only because the World in question isn’t a living entity and is unable to ’fight back’.
But in terms of pure energy, an Eternal is nowhere near close to the energy that a Lowest-Level World has.
So even if an Infinity is stronger than a Lowest-Level World, he shouldn’t be stronger than a higher-level world, especially not a High-Level World.
Or at least...
This was what Nux believed.
But...
[Yes, Infinities are that strong.]
Azriel simply nodded.
[Devour a High-Level World and devour an Infinity,
You will sense the difference yourself.
High-Level Worlds are the Universe’s third favorite Entities, but it is still nowhere close to Infinities, the Universe’s second favorite Entities.

If the Universe reacts strongly to the disappearance of a High-Level World, the disappearance of an Infinity would pretty much make it initiate self-destruction just so it can get rid of the filthy entity that has been stealing what did not belong to it.]
Azriel explained.
He then looked into Nux’s eyes and—
[So if you are planning to go against Infinities,
Remove that thought from your head.
You are not strong enough yet.]
He spoke with a concerned look on his face, an expression that for a moment surprised Nux.
Was his father-in-law... worried about him...?
That was a first.
[Don’t get ahead of yourself. I only want you to be careful because my Lia’s life is connected to yours. I cannot lose my daughter just because I gave in and chose a reckless and foolish son-in-law.]
Azriel snapped.
"How did you know what I was thinking?"
Nux blinked.
[Did you see how your face looked like just now?]
Azriel retorted with a disgusted face, a look that made Nux turn towards his wives. The women nodded silently and in the end, Nux just sighed,
"Whatever,
I wasn’t planning on facing Infinities anyways, so you do not have to worry, my caring Father-in-law~"
Nux answered with a big smile on his face,
A smile that made Azriel feel the urge to enter his Universe and slap him.

chapters.title: Chapter 2139: Universe’s Authority.
paragraphs: "I wasn’t planning on facing Infinities anyways, so you do not have to worry, my caring Father in law~"
Nux answered with a big smile on his face,
A smile that made Azriel feel the urge to enter his Universe and slap him.
The Vampire, however, had much better control over his emotions than most beings, so he quickly calmed himself for his daughter’s sake and—
[What do you mean? How are you going to ’slap the Infinities’ then?]
He questioned.
It was much more important to know what this crazy fool was planning in order to make sure he was safe in all scenarios.
After all, no matter how much he hated the boy, for the sake of his daughter, he could not let him die.
"That was just a figure of speech obviously."
Nux answered with a smile.
[Nux, explain to me before I come there.]
Azriel threatened, his mouth twitching in annoyance.
It had been a while since he had felt this much frustration, the boy truly had the knack of getting on anyone’s nerves.
"Right right..."
Not wanting to lose his life just now, Nux began explaining everything.
These past few decades, Azriel only cared about cultivating, so he pretty much had no clue what had happened.

Nux explained to him how Zylarith targeted his wives when they were on their mission, how he found out about Sharnoth, how he learned Sharnoth’s truth and what happened to her. Then he started explaining how they faced the Supreme Borns, how he suspected that the Infinities saw Sharnoth and how they must have connected her with the Leander Family.
He talked about how they might be after him and Vexarion, Sharnoth’s enemy, was a bait that they had set to capture them.
So Nux’s plan was to get his hands on Vexarion, who was being indirectly protected by the Infinities, essentially slapping their face.
Of course, it went without saying that he would only be doing this when what he was thinking comes out to be true.

The explanation alone took about three hours, even though it was heavily briefed. Azriel kept asking questions in between, raising his eyebrows in doubt at other times. Once Nux was done, the Vampire only had one question...
[So you can now defeat Eternals...?]
"That is correct. I defeated two Supreme Born Eternals, the rest shouldn’t be more difficult, according to their memories, they were quite strong."
Nux answered with a shrug, as if he couldn’t see how these beings were ’strong’.
Azriel didn’t say anything, an action that Nux found quite surprising.
The old man didn’t have anything to say?
This was a first as well.
Soon, a grin appeared on his face and—
"Why? Can you not do that, Father in Law?"
He questioned, his grin widening as he spoke more words.
"Doesn’t that mean there is no point in us sparring against each other? There is no way you can win when you can’t even defeat ’mere’ Eternals."
Azriel didn’t say anything.
He couldn’t.
After all, it was true.
He cannot defeat Eternals, let alone Supreme Born Eternals who can easily be called few of the strongest Eternals in all of Universe.
The Vampire could only stand and feel his mouth twitching the more he saw the boy grin.
"Father..."
Seeing her father act like this, Aeliana called out with a frown.
Azriel turned towards her, his face instantly warming up.
"Didn’t you say Cultivation Phases no longer matter to you? Then how..."
Aeliana didn’t know how to say what she wanted to say.
She couldn’t just ask how her Father is unable to face Eternals, now could she?
These were Eternals they were talking about! Immortal Beings who could pretty much defeat anyone in the Universe except for a few!
Nux was a monster through and through, Aeliana already knew that, she just... didn’t like comparing her husband and father.
[I can.]
Azriel, as if knowing what his daughter was thinking, answered.
Aeliana stared at him with a frown, and he began,
[As I said, I can use my Authority as the Universe’s Child to strengthen myself and surpass the restrictions it has set.
So yes, using my Authority, I can defeat Eternity.
But this power doesn’t come without a cost.]
"What cost?"
Aeliana questioned in worry.
[When I use this Authority, I am no longer a free Entity, I am the Universe’s Child who needs to fulfil his responsibilities.]
"What...?"
Aeliana tilted her head, a little confused.
"He is saying he cannot use his powers against me, because if he does, he will be forced to kill me."
Nux was the one who answered Aeliana’s question, staring at Azriel with a serious look on his face, his smile long gone.
After all, even if he didn’t show it, he was still worried about his Father in Law.
Azriel nodded at Nux’s words,
[That is correct.]
"Does it mean the Universe controls you if you use its Authority?"
Nux questioned directly.
He had already seen a similar case with Sharnoth, he didn’t want another one. After all, a once defeated Infinity who is pretty much a cripple now was still something he could take on.
But... even Nux wasn’t prepared to face a fucking Universe that is being protected by a monster like Azriel.
Aeliana’s face paled when she heard Nux’s question. She quickly turned towards her Father, panicking even before she heard his answer,
But then—
[No.]
Azriel shook his head.
[The Universe no longer holds much power over me, not until I use its Authority.]
"What about when you use its Authority?"
Aeliana questioned quickly.
[My Domain keeps me out of the Universe’s detection, but that fails when I use its Authority. The Universe would then be able to see what I see and if it sees Nux standing in front of me...]
"It will tell you to kill me and if you do not act, it will think you are in cahoots with the enemy, forcing it to take extreme actions."
Nux guessed.
[That is correct.]
Azriel nodded again.
[The same is true for Eternals.
I can defeat them if I use my Authority, but I need a reason convincing enough for the Universe to allow me to use its power and destroy its own Entity.
After all, this Power wasn’t given to me to face the beings from my Universe.]
Azriel slowly glanced at Nux and in an instant, the Anomaly realized what his Father in law was trying to say and completed his sentence again—
"It was given to you to face enemies from another Universe."
[Yes.]

paragraphs: "It was given to you to face enemies from other Universes."

[It will have to wait.]

Nux sighed, it would seem like his dream to spar against his Father-in-law on equal footing would remain a dream.
Shadow, who saw Nux’s sigh, sighed as well. She could pretty much see his thoughts on his face, after all, she knew how much he was looking forward to it all.

Of course, the woman also knew that not once did Nux consider this his ’victory’. He was definitely stronger than Azriel if he didn’t use the powers the Universe gave him, so in some way, one could view this as a victory.
But Nux simply did not think in that manner.
The Universe’s Authority was Azriel’s strength. If he couldn’t use it in battle, it would defeat the purpose of the spar.
The result would never truly satisfy a battle maniac like Nux.
"You seem disappointed."
And as if sensing all his emotions, Felberta slowly hovered towards him and held his hands.
Nux stared at her and smiled lightly. Seeing this chance, the rest of the women, including Shadow, surrounded Nux.
The only ones who weren’t part of the group were Sharnoth and... Aeliana.
The Vampire was now staring at her father and—
"You aren’t in any sort of danger, right Father?"
She questioned with a worried look on her face.
[Danger?
Who do you think I am?]
Azriel answered with a confident smirk, something that made Aeliana smile lightly as well.
"I am just... worried."
She spoke in a low voice.
[Then you should start calling me whenever you feel such a way. That is much better than constantly contacting Faus and asking about me.]
"I was worried that the Universe will..."
Aeliana lowered her head.
[As I said, what I do inside my Domain, the Universe cannot see.
You can call me anytime you want.]
"I will bother you every single day then."
Aeliana answered with a smile, her crimson eyes shining excitedly as she stared at her father.
[Yes, you should.]
Azriel nodded, a gentle, sweet smile appearing on his face.
This was half the reason he called so quickly the moment Faus informed him about Nux wanting to talk to him.
The boy didn’t matter, he just wanted Aeliana to know that the Universe did not restrict him anymore. She could now talk to him every day, like she used to before.
"*Yes, you should.*"
Shadow, who had been staring at the father and daughter, mimicked Azriel’s words in an exaggerated manner. She then placed her hand over Sharnoth’s shoulder and—
"You cannot possibly think that man doesn’t have two personalities, can you? How can one not see the difference? It is so glaringly obvious, no?"
Sharnoth blinked at those words, she had no clue how she was supposed to react in this situation. In all her long life, it was rare for someone weaker than her to leave her this speechless.
Completely oblivious to her thoughts, Shadow tilted her head and—
"What do you think?
You see, the two of us here are the only experts in this matter, so your opinion is quite valuable—mmhhfffhh!!"
Before the woman could speak too much, Lane placed her hand on Shadow’s mouth and pulled her away.
The Shadow Demon then stared at Sharnoth and—
"Don’t mind her words, treat them like air actually.
You do not have to hear what she says.
Actually, ignore everything she ever tells you."
The usually silent woman mentioned.
The blabbermouth had already ruined her reputation in front of many, she wasn’t going to let this happen again.
Yes, this time she was prepared.

Again, Sharnoth was speechless. She could only silently nod at the woman’s desperate words as she pulled the desperately flailing Shadow away. All this while, Sharnoth only had one question in her head...
Just what place has she come to...?
Why does... every single person here feel... crazy?
After the chaos settled, with Nux being surrounded and pampered by his wives, and Azriel and Aeliana having a long chat,
At last, their conversation shifted to the reason they were here.
[So you plan to capture this Vexarion.]
"That is correct."

Nux nodded, staring at Sharnoth, as if ensuring her that he *will* fulfil his promise. The Chaos Heir smiled lightly, for some reason, Nux’s simple gesture reassured her more than Zylarith’s countless claims ever did.

He questioned.
"It is simple,
The Supreme Worlds want me to attack Aurendor and that is what I will do,
But before that, I will attack Gracevale."
[Gracevale...?]
Azriel narrowed his eyes.
From his reaction, it was clear he knew what it was.
"Mhm, it is one of the strongest High Level Worlds in the Universe. It has around 15 Eternals and is considered to be one of the cores of the Faction of Light.

Be it participating in the War in the name of the Supreme World of Light, or finding exceptional beings that can benefit the Supreme World of Light and ’offering’ them to them, they stand ahead in every case.

They are also one of the only few worlds that have a direct connection with the Supreme World of Light. Most beings in the Universe who wish to request a meeting with a being from the Supreme World for any reason need to enter Gracevale to initiate the process.
I am sure attacking them would be fun."
Nux answered with a smile.
"I want to see how the Supreme Worlds react when one of their Dogs is targeted."
His grin widened.

chapters.title: Chapter 2141: I am a demon.
paragraphs: "I want to see how the Supreme Worlds reacts when one of their Dogs are targeted."
Nux spoke, his grin widening with every second.
Azriel, on the other hand, had more questions,
[Why them specifically?]
The Vampire could tell what Nux was thinking and from their conversation so far, he could already guess what the boy’s basic plan was.
He will be using his Domain as he attacks an Entity of the Main Universe and he wants him, a being closest to the Universe, to observe the Universe’s reaction.
At the same time, Nux also wanted him to see how his Domain impacted the Main Universe—an outsider’s perspective to his Domain.
And once he has that information, he will plan ahead accordingly.
It was a basic, simple plan.
Honestly, Nux didn’t even have to attack a World to put the plan into action, this would have worked even if he attacked even the weakest of the Universe’s Entities.
This is what confused Azriel.
He knew Nux wasn’t the type to take unnecessary risk, then why do something that will definitely earn the Supreme Worlds’ ire?
What if Gracevale was well protected?
What if he encounters Light Infinity during this and his plan doesn’t work out?
Of course, Azriel understood that the chances of this happening were low, but... they still existed.
It wasn’t in Nux’s nature to act this rashly unless one of his wives was in danger.
And even if he was targeting the Supreme Worlds, whyherworld first?
Azriel was curious.
"Hmm, I don’t know."
Nux tilted his head, a little... confused?
"I can play it safe but...
I don’t want to?"
Even he wasn’t sure of what he was saying, usually, he would have strong reason as to what and why he was doing something, especially when it is something that held such significant importance.
But this time...
"My gut tells me this is the best course of action...?"
Nux muttered in an unsure voice.
[Your gut...?]
Azriel frowned, not liking the tone of that statement.
Nux however, just nodded.
"I cannot explain it, but this is what I believe is the best course of action."
[It is dangerous.]
Azriel warned.
"It will be quite rewarding,
I trust my instincts.
They brought me this far."
[It was your caution that brought you this far.]
The Vampire countered.
Even Nux’s wives seemed a little uncertain but then—
"No, I will follow my instincts this time."
Nux shook his head firmly, not willing to change his mind.
An action that made Azriel frown even more,
[Why are you being so stubborn?]
He questioned.
It almost felt like... Nux’s thoughts were being influenced by an outside entity that they did not know about.
"I am not being stubborn. I just believe it will work out."
[What will?]
"The Four Supreme Worlds have been enemies for trillions of years, correct?"
Nux questioned.
[Yes, ever since they came into creation.]
Azriel nodded, that was how the Universe designed them. Equally powerful but completely opposite when it comes to power, so one becoming powerful would mean the fall of others.
It was the Universe’s way of ensuring its survival.
"Think about it, how can entities that have been at each other’s throats for Eternity... work together seamlessly?"
Nux questioned with a grin.
[Are you...]
Azriel’s expression changed and Nux nodded.
"What if the enemy keeps targeting just one out of the Four Supreme Worlds? How do you think that World will react? What will the Light Infinity think?"
Nux spoke and just like Azriel, the rest of his wives stared at him with a surprised look on their faces.
"You plan to put them against each other?"
Amaya questioned.
"It is the most basic of tactics so it might not work bu—"
"No, it will work."
The devourer nodded.
"I do not know why I did not think of this. My mind must have frozen for a while."
She spoke honestly, staring at Nux with her dark eyes shining brightly.
"It is a basic plan, but it will definitely work on entities that have been enemies for such a long time, especially when they do not truly understand ’what’ it is they are actually facing.
If anything, from their perspective, the Anomaly could very well be created by one of them to get rid of others."
The devourer grinned just like Nux.
It wasn’t just her, Aeliana too understood the plan but—
"Why target the Supreme World of Light?"
She questioned with a frown.
"Wouldn’t it work best on the Supreme World of Darkness?"
"That might make this too obvious."
Amaya answered.
"It is already an obvious tactic."
Aeliana countered.

"And it doesn’t matter even if it is, if what we know about Beings of Darkness is true and the Darkness Infinity is anything like them, then the chances of him listening to reason when it’s only his Forces being targeted will be low."
The Vampire explained.
"If anything, we might even see Darkness declaring War against the rest of the Supreme Worlds.
There will be unrest, that is for sure."
She added and Amaya couldn’t exactly counter his words.
Seeing the two women now standing in front of each other, not willing to back down, Nux interrupted.
"I do not have a specific reason to target the Supreme World of Light."
When the women turned towards him, he grinned like a demon.
"I am just targeting them because I want to see what those pretentious bastards would do in return.
Don’t you think it will be interesting to see as well?
The ’Harbingers of Peace’ showing their true faces and declaring what could possibly be the biggest War in the history of the Universe."
Nux laughed.
"I want to see how far we would need to push them before they break."
"...you realize that you resemble a demon right now, don’t you?"
Allura commented, staring at Nux.
Nux however, just laughed at those words as he gently pulled the woman towards him and placed his hands over her hair and his forehead on hers.
"What do you meanresemble?
Iama demon.
A Devil."
He spoke as his appearance changed, turning into an entity that oozed with sex appeal.

chapters.title: Chapter 2142: Gracevale
paragraphs: Gracevale shines.
That was what most people said when they first saw it.
The world floated in a ring of soft white light and was wrapped in gentle day. Tall towers rose like clean spears. Bridges ran between them like ribbons of glass.
Songs hummed from the wards that guarded the city.
Priests in pale robes walked the streets with baskets of bread.
Doves circled above gardens that never seemed to wilt.
If anyone asked the people of Gracevale what kind of place this was, they answered the same way every time.
"It is heavenly."
"A bright world."
"A World where evil does not exist."
"The Heart of Light."
This was Gracevale.
The World that almost all beings in the Universe that were part of the Supreme Faction of Light wanted to settle in.
A World where every being had equal opportunity. A World where Corruption didn’t exist. A World where power wasn’t misused. A World where the weak weren’t suppressed.
It was a world that seemed straight out of fantasy.
But...
Calren knew better.
He walked down Processional Avenue in Dawnspire, the capital of the only Nation that existed in Gracevale.

The Avenue was a straight line of polished stone that ran from the Prism Gate to the Petitioners’ Hall. The stone was always warm, as if the sun lived inside it. The air smelled like citrus and clean rain. The banners of the Faction of Light hung on both sides—white cloth, gold thread, the sigil of a rising sun spreading its light in the Dark Universe.
Calren’s badge caught that light.
It was a small disk on his chest with three rays cut into it, the moment the light assimilated into his chest, the doors opened.
Calren was a registrar in the Hall, Grade Five, Master of Intake Lanes Two and Three.
Yes, he was a powerful man.

People bowed when he passed, guards saluted with their spears crossed, and they did not do it out of fear, they did it all willingly, out of the respect and love they had for people working in the Hall.
Calren too, smiled and nodded at everyone, showing absolute grace in every single one of his movements.
He moved without slowing down, as the native folk made way for him, each having the same grace and effortlessness in their existence as him.
The Luminari.
These were one of the natives of Gracevale.
They were a tall, pale-eyed race born of Gracevale’s light, the most common in the City.
Of course, these weren’t the only race that lived in a world that was called the Core of the Supreme Faction of Light.
There were others too.

The Seraphkin with soft wings folded close stood outside shrines and sang mid-day hymns. Their hymns had the power to heal most injuries and yes, because these hymns constantly echoed throughout the City, injuries here healed on their own, without needing potions or healing magic.
It was one of the reasons Gracevale was considered the most desired World to live in.
The third race that resided here were the Auriels.

The Auriels were known as one of the fastest races in the entire Universe. When angered, they could become an enemy even the Supreme Borns would be careful against. Of course, in Gracevale, these beings had no reason to be angry.

As one of the most peaceful Worlds in existence, other than the army it trained, the rest of the beings lived calm, carefree lives, not worrying about cultivation since their blood alone made them stronger with time.

All Gracevale races could spend their entire lives sleeping, doing nothing, and still be at least a Primordial at the end, not that being Primordial was impressive in a world that had fifteen Eternals.
Of course, these beings simply didn’t care, they lived a life too privileged to care about strength.
Most Auriels, one of the fastest beings in the Universe, used their speed to work as couriers, gliding from balcony to balcony, earning their keep.
Because Gracevale was such a popular World in the Universe, one of the most densely populated races in the Universe, the Humans, were quite common here as well.
Of course, most of them were merely visitors, here to either request for help or hoping to settle here permanently if they could.
Yes, many humans had become part of this world as well, every single one of them had a bright glow on their skin after staying in this heaven for so long. A look that received envy from many.
As he stared at his surroundings, Calren finally reached the steps of the Petitioners’ Hall. It looked like a temple and a court at the same time.
A dome of crystal sat above a wide hall of pale stone. Light flowed through the crystal and made soft patterns on the floor. Lines of benches filled the room in long arcs.
At the far end, six doors waited, each marked with a rune: Audience, Appeal, Pledge, Vow, Remission, and Transit.
Behind those doors, as Calren liked to say, the true Gracevale was run.
He walked forward and passed the front clerk with a little nod, stepping through a side arch to the intake desks.
He sat at Lane Two, set his badge on the holder, and woke the slab in the desk. Blue letters rose on the polished surface, numbers that climbed and fell.
Finally, Calren looked forward, petitioners queued in a slow, long line from the gate to his lane.
As he settled down, a guard banged his spear on the floor and finally,
The long line moved.
"Next,"
Calren said as he turned towards his desk, not even bothering to look at who was standing in front of him.

The woman wearing a simple green robe stepped on the rail, her hands shook, but she kept her chin up. Calren glanced at the slab she presented, it showed her details, or more accurately, the name of the World she came from, this was what told Calren how seriously he needed to take this matter.
And in this particular case—
Greenmarch, a Lowest Level World.
—he didn’t have to at all.
Without any change in his expression,
"Remission is that door."
He pointed forward.

They were a tall, pale-eyed race born of Gracevale’s light, the most common in the City.
Of course, these weren’t the only race that lived in a world that was called the Core of the Supreme Faction of Light.
There were others too.
The Seraphkin with soft wings folded close stood outside shrines and sang mid-day hymns.
Their hymns had the power to heal most injuries and yes, because these hymns constantly echoed throughout the City, injuries here healed on their own, without needing potions or healing magic.
It was one of the reasons Gracevale was considered the most desired World to live in.
The third race that resided here were the Auriels.
The Auriels were known as one of the fastest races in the entire Universe.
When angered, they could become an enemy even the Supreme Borns would be careful against.
Of course, in Gracevale, these beings had no reason to be angry.

As one of the most peaceful Worlds in existence, other than the army it trained, the rest of the beings lived calm, carefree lives, not worrying about cultivation since their blood alone made them stronger with time.

All Gracevale races could spend their entire lives sleeping, doing nothing, and still be at least a Primordial at the end, not that being Primordial was impressive in a world that had fifteen Eternals.
Of course, these beings simply didn’t care, they lived a life too privileged to care about strength.
Most Auriels, one of the fastest beings in the Universe, used their speed to work as couriers, gliding from balcony to balcony, earning their keep.
Because Gracevale was such a popular World in the Universe, one of the most densely populated races in the Universe, the Humans, were quite common here as well.
Of course, most of them were merely visitors, here to either request for help or hoping to settle here permanently if they could.
Yes, many humans had become part of this world as well, every single one of them had a bright glow on their skin after staying in this heaven for so long.
A look that received envy from many.
As he stared at his surroundings, Calren finally reached the steps of the Petitioners’ Hall.
It looked like a temple and a court at the same time.
A dome of crystal sat above a wide hall of pale stone.
Light flowed through the crystal and made soft patterns on the floor.
Lines of benches filled the room in long arcs.
At the far end, six doors waited, each marked with a rune: Audience, Appeal, Pledge, Vow, Remission, and Transit.
Behind those doors, as Calren liked to say, the true Gracevale was run.
He walked forward and passed the front clerk with a little nod, stepping through a side arch to the intake desks.
He sat at Lane Two, set his badge on the holder, and woke the slab in the desk.
Blue letters rose on the polished surface, numbers that climbed and fell.
Finally, Calren looked forward, petitioners queued in a slow, long line from the gate to his lane.
As he settled down, a guard banged his spear on the floor and finally,
The long line moved.
"Next,"
Calren said as he turned towards his desk, not even bothering to look at who was standing in front of him.
The woman wearing a simple green robe stepped on the rail, her hands shook, but she kept her chin up.
Calren glanced at the slab she presented, it showed her details, or more accurately, the name of the World she came from, this was what told Calren how seriously he needed to take this matter.
And in this particular case—
Greenmarch, a Lowest Level World.
—he didn’t have to at all.
Without any change in his expression,
"Remission is that door."
He pointed forward.

chapters.title: Chapter 2143: I have a report to make.
paragraphs: "Remission is that door."
Carlen pointed forward, from the start till finish, he didn’t even look at the woman standing in front of him.
The woman’s body trembled and she bit her lips.

She was the only daughter of Greenmarch’s Progenitor, and she had come here to request aide. Because the recent shaking of the Universe was stronger than normal ones, the Artifact they bought that prevented their world from being affected by it failed, which destroyed almost all of Greenmarch. About a million people had died and the most important buildings had crumbled.
More than half of the remaining population was gravely injured and the woman desperately needed the Faction’s help to deal with this matter.
But...
Even then, the aide she was requesting here wasn’t direct help.
What she wanted was Remission.
Because of the recent tragedy, Greenmarch did not have enough tribute for the Faction of Light but...
Things didn’t seem like they were working.

After all, this wasn’t her first time here. The last time she was sent to the Remission door, they only offered to reduce the Annual Tribute by a fifth and in return, they wanted twice the tribute for the next decade.
It was something Greenmarch could not accept because of their condition,
So she needed to do something.
Anything.
The fate of her World relied on her shoulders.
"...we do not have anything."
The woman spoke directly, not moving away as Carlen wanted her to. Seeing her odd reaction, Carlen frowned.
He finally raised his head, looking at the woman for the first time.
He, however, did not show his disgust, he just displayed a gentle but confused look, signalling the woman to explain.
"I went to Remission five days ago, they still asked for tribute, but we do not have that."
And she did.
"But if you do not give tribute, the Faction will not accept you."
Carlen spoke with a look that made it seem like he actually cared.
A complicated look appeared on the woman’s face when she heard those words,
"...this is why I came to you.
I need your help."
She requested as she bowed her head, her body began to tremble, showing her desperation. After all, her World had to be part of the Light Faction.

If they left, aside from the fact that their safety would no longer be guaranteed, they would also need to return the artifacts the Light Faction gave to them, artifacts that... no longer existed because they were all destroyed in the recent tragedy.
Yes, before they were even attacked by the rest of the worlds around them, the Light Faction would be the one they would need to give answers to and...
They would have no way to get out of that situation alive.
Leaving the Faction was absolutely impossible.
Did she share this problem with the Light Faction?
She couldn’t.

The Artifacts that were destroyed, were what her Grandmother begged for. While the Faction didn’t charge for them, they absolutely had to return them if their world ever left the Light Faction. This was made clear on the very first day.
Something that, at that time, they did not care about since, well, why would they leave the Light Faction in the first place?
But...
Here she was...
Bowing in front of a man she did not know, hoping to find a way out.
"You do not have to do that.
Please raise your head."
Carlen spoke gently.
The woman slowly raised her head and then—
"If the mercy rate isn’t working, you can take the pledge for service to Light.
Six centuries.
Pledge Greenmarch for service of Light for Six Centuries and the Tribute will be absolved."
"Six Centuries...?"
The woman muttered, staring at Calren with a complicated look on her face.

Pledging their world to the Service of Light for six centuries would mean that their people would be under the direct command of the Supreme Faction of Light. The higher ups of the Faction would be able to use it however they wanted.
Be it wanting to use them as mercenaries, soldiers, or even servants.
It was basically a slave contract written in golden words.
The woman wanted to clench her fists in frustration, it was clear that these bastards were using their misery for their benefit, but she knew acting out wouldn’t do anything.
If anything, it might make things worse.
She secretly glared at Calren, the man smiled gently, as if he was the most noble, honest being in the Universe, a look that made the woman feel disgusted,
But in the end—
"We pledge to the service of Light."
In the end, she had to give in.
Being their slaves was better than being their enemies, this way, at least they would be alive. At her words, Calren showed no reaction, as if he was already expecting the same answer.
He then nodded lightly and—
"As Authorized by Ravana Greenmarch, the Leader of Greenmarch, you represent your world, so with your words as proof,
From this forth, to the next six centuries—
Greenmarch is now part in the Service of Light."
He spoke, smiling in the easy way he had practiced.
"May the Light reward the faithful."

He then pointed at the Vow door and the woman walked away with heavy steps. To think they would need to sell themselves to the Faction of Light because the artifact they were given by the very same Faction, couldn’t protect their World from the Universe’s trembling like it was built for.
’Justice my...’

The woman wanted to curse, but in the end, she shook her head and controlled herself. Even if she was only doing this in her head, she did not know what other strange abilities beings here might have.
Taking a foolish risk like this wasn’t worth it.
In the end, she went to the Vow door.
Calren moved the Tribute credit to Lane Two’s "adjustment" line and tapped "close." The coin count climbed in the corner of his slab. He got his cut for gathering more ’believers’.
The numbers soothed him, but he didn’t show anything on his face, he just—
"Next."
He called.
And this time—
"I have a report to make."
He heard a strangely calm, almost amused voice.

chapters.title: Chapter 2144: A world was attacked.
paragraphs: "Next."
Carlen called in an unbothered tone,
And this time—
"I have a report to make."

He heard a strangely calm, almost amused voice, that made him raise his head in confusion. He then stared at the nearly two meter tall being standing in front of him, the being had long black hair, black horns and wings, long ears, hypnotic purple eyes and a smile that, for some reason, made Carlen feel uneasy.
"A report...?"
Carlen raised his eyebrow, ignoring this strange feeling that warned him about something he did not understand.
Dangerous.
That’s what his instincts told him.
But...
That was ridiculous.
He was a Transcendent Level Being and was sitting inside the Administrative Hall of Gracevale, one of the strongest High Level Worlds.
Even right now, there were about Eight Eternals in the building he was in, and if that wasn’t enough, there were seven more who could appear the moment they sensed something was wrong.
Not to mention that there were fifteen Eternals who would act the instant they sensed something, but the entire Universe knew just how important Gracevale was to the Supreme Faction of Light.
It had direct support and the protection of the Supreme World of Light. Because of all these reasons, no one in their right mind would even think of doing something here.
The fact that Gracevale had never faced a terror attack despite being open to the Universe was proof of that. Let alone being attacked, Gracevale had never even been attacked before.

Sure, the Four Supreme Factions constantly battled against each other, but Gracevale was one of the worlds that held too much importance, so it was never asked to participate in the War, which would stop all the functions it sustained.
Understanding that and fearing that it would start a complete all-out war, no world belonging to any Faction ever attacked it.
Inside such a world, inside the Hall that was the core of everything Gracevale did, there was nothing ’dangerous’.
Heck, one wouldn’t be wrong to say that Carlen was currently inside one of the safest places in all of the Universe.
But then...
Why was it that despite ignoring his instincts again and again, instead of settling down, they were only ringing faster...?
Carlen didn’t understand, he just stared at this man, confused.
"Yes, a report."
"...what report?"
Carlen questioned, trying to get more information regarding the being in front of him using the administrative system he had.
"A World was attacked."
The being answered, his words confusing Carlen even further.

Two High Level Factions were at War with each other. Although the situation of the War was unclear, there were still more than a thousand worlds that were part of this War, worlds that were still attacking their enemies.
In a situation like this, tens of worlds were being attacked right now as they spoke.
Why was he reporting something like this here?

Carlen thought inwardly, looking at the being in front of him with an exhausted look on his face, as if he was dealing with another one of ’those’ fools. Of course, he didn’t say or show any of this outside, outwardly, he had a concerned look on his face and—
"What? Which world? Are you from that world? Are you alright? Do you require any help?"
He asked a series of questions.
"I am not from that world."
The being however, shook his head and his words...
They made Carlen’s mouth twitch.
If you aren’t part of that world, then why the fuck were you here?
He wanted to ask it out loud, but again, he had an image to maintain.
"Is that so...?"
He muttered in a low, awkward tone.
"What world are you talking about?"
He questioned.
He still couldn’t find any information regarding this man with just his face, maybe learning about the world he was talking about would give some clues.
But then—
"Gracevale."
The man answered.
"Ah, Grac—"
And in an instant, Carlen froze.
He stared at the being in front of him, and this time, with a solemn, almost threatening look on his face—
"What are you talking about?"
He questioned in a heavy tone.
"This is not the place you can joke around.
Do you see the long line of people behind you?

Every single one of them has come here because they are facing problems that might cause harm to millions. Do you feel it is the right thing for you to stand in front of them, saying something absolutely bogus, while they wait for their turn?"
For a moment, the being seemed taken aback by those words.
"Wow, I almost bought that one."
He commented in a surprised voice, he almost looked impressed.
"Of course, that is if I hadn’t seen them wait in this ’long line’ for hours because you were busy entertaining the guests you had."
"What—"
Carlen narrowed his eyes, for a moment, his gentle, noble appearance disappeared, but before he could get his act together and think what to do about the clear troublemaker he was dealing with—
"Also, what made you think I was merely playing around?"

The man questioned as he tilted his head, the grin on his face widening. And just as he did, Carlen’s instincts screamed, this time, much more loudly than before, as if telling him to run right now else this wouldn’t end well.
And since the situation felt so odd, Carlen decided to listen to the instincts he had trusted all his life—
But it was already too late.
Suddenly, the man extended his hand, grabbing Carlen by his throat. The sudden action shocked every being present inside the Hall, especially Carlen.
He stared at the man, wide eyed, in absolute disbelief. He had used all his strength to free himself, but the man’s fingers didn’t even budge.
They...
They were leagues apart in terms of strength.
And if this man wanted...
He could snap his neck at any moment.
"W-What are you..."
Carlen tried asking in a hoarse voice, the man however, completely ignored him, he just grinned, as if he found something and then—
"So they didn’t give out any warnings huh...
Was it because they wanted to take me by surprise when I attacked Aurendor?"
Nux spoke after reading Carlen’s memory, then, he stared at the poor man in his grasp and—
"Well,
Too bad for you I guess."
He shrugged and—
"AAAAAGGGGGGHHHHHHHHHHHHH!!!"
Carlen screamed in agony.
